beeFormer
This is the official implementation provided with our paper
beeFormer: Bridging the Gap Between Semantic and Interaction Similarity in Recommender Systems
.
main idea of beeFormer
Collaborative filtering (CF) methods can capture patterns from interaction data that are not obvious at first sight. For example, when buying a printer, users can also buy toners, papers, or cables to connect the printer, and collaborative filtering can take such patterns into account. However, in the cold-start recommendation setup, where new items do not have any interaction at all, collaborative filtering methods cannot be used, and recommender systems are forced to use other approaches, like content-based filtering (CBF). The problem with content-based filtering is that it relies on item attributes, such as text descriptions. In our printer example, semantic similarity-trained language models will put other printers closer than accessories that users might be searching for. Our method is training language models to learn these user behavior patterns from interaction data to transfer that knowledge to previously unseen items. Our experiments show that performance benefits from this approach are enormous.
Steps to start training the models:
create virtual environment
python3.10 -m venv beef
and activate it
source beef/bin/activate
clone this repository and navigate to it
cd beeformer
install packages
pip install -r requirements.txt
download the data for movielens: navigate to the
_dataset/ml20m
folder and run
source download_data
download the data for goodbooks: navigate to the
_dataset/goodbooks
folder and run
source download_data
download the data for amazonbooks: navigate to the
_dataset/amazonbooks
folder and run
source download_data && python preprocess.py
in the root folder of the project run the
train.py
, for example like this:
python train.py --seed 42 --scheduler None --lr 1e-5 --epochs 5 --dataset goodbooks --sbert
"
sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2
"
--max_seq_length 384 --batch_size 1024 --max_output 10000 --sbert_batch_size 200 --use_cold_start
true
--save_every_epoch
true
--model_name my_model
Evaluate the results. To reproduce numbers from the paper using our hugginface repository, run for example:
python evaluate_itemsplit.py --seed 42 --dataset goodbooks --sbert beeformer/Llama-goodbooks-mpnet
or
python evaluate_timesplit.py --seed 42 --dataset amazon-books --sbert beeformer/Llama-amazbooks-mpnet
Datasets and preprocessing
Preprocessing information
We consider ratings of 4.0 and higher as an interaction. We only keep the users with at least 5 interactions.
LLM Data augmentations
Since there are no text descriptions in the original data, we manually connect several datasets with the original data and train our models on it. However, this approach has several limitations: texts from different sources have different styles and different lengths, and this might influence the results. data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A/B测试中的因果推断问题及其应用场景

不同观点：
• Ozzie_osman认为，文章指出的问题在于这些A/B测试无法提供因果推断，因为平台可能会对两个测试组进行不同的定位。如果是研究者想证明“广告A比Y更具吸引力”，确实需要因果推断，而这些测试无法满足这一点。但对于营销人员来说，如果只是想确定哪个广告支出更有效率，因果推断并不是必须的。因此，文章讨论的焦点是这些工具在研究中的局限性，而非营销应用。

• gdc3000对文章提出的问题表示关注，并基于自己在Qualtrics的工作经验提出，是否可以通过在产品中加入某种审核机制来帮助发现潜在的平台偏差，例如样本比例不匹配或元数据平衡检查。这一观点更关注于如何从技术层面解决或缓解文章中提到的问题。

• drpossum以讽刺的语气质疑发表这篇文章的期刊（International Journal of Research in Human Manipulation and Subjugation）是否因为自己的方法论过于薄弱而选择发表此类文章。这个评论更倾向于对文章的学术价值提出质疑，没有直接讨论A/B测试的技术问题。

• charcircuit则反驳了对测量仅限于广告创意的期望，认为平台的定位能力本身就是测量的一部分。他们认为实验的目标是看哪个创意对指标的推动最大，因此平台的定位能力是不可分割的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于A/B测试是否能够以及应否用于因果推断。Ozzie_osman和charcircuit在这个问题上存在分歧，前者强调因果推断在研究中的重要性，后者则认为平台的定位能力本身就应被纳入测量。
• gdc3000提出的技术解决方案提供了一种新的讨论方向，即通过产品改进减少偏差，而非仅仅讨论方法论问题。
• drpossum的评论带有讽刺性，并未直接贡献建设性观点，但反映了部分读者对文章或期刊的质疑态度。

data.title: Everything I learned from (finally) completing The Artist's Way
data.author: cf100clunk
data.article_summary: 《The Artist's Way》是一本关于创意的自助书籍，由Julia Cameron于1992年出版，帮助许多人解开创意障碍。作者Madeleine Dore分享了她多次尝试完成这本书的经历，最终在五年断断续续的尝试后成功坚持了十二周的课程。通过每天写 Morning Pages 和定期进行 Artist Dates，她发现自己发生了变化，但又似乎没有改变，强调改变是一个不完美、进两步退一步的过程。她学会了向内探索，理解了支持和尝试的重要性，并认识到勇气而非天赋，是成为艺术家的关键。这本书鼓励被创意障碍困扰的人去尝试，并提供了深刻的自我反思机会。

• 评论中提到“Twelve weeks, a dozen artist dates and three Moleksine journals filled with morning pages”显示出作者对Moleskine笔记本的长期使用，以及其在艺术或创意项目中的应用。
• 该评论引发了一个潜在的语言学现象：即使长时间接触某个词汇，用户仍可能对其正确形式产生怀疑，这可能与词汇的陌生感或外来词的引入有关。
• 争议的焦点可能在于，Moleskine作为一个品牌名，其拼写和发音是否在不同语言和文化中有不同的变体或适应性，从而导致用户的困惑。

Everything I learned from (finally) completing The Artist’s Way
Words by Madeleine Dore
Maybe you’ve heard people referring to the morning pages or talking about going on an artist date. Maybe you’ve just started reading the first few chapters, or adopted some of its core practices into your daily routine. Maybe you’ve abandoned it halfway through, or dipped in and out, or even completed the entire twelve-week course.
For those not familiar,
The Artist’s Way
is a seminal text for creative unblocking and was published in 1992 by Julia Cameron. It has sold over five million copies and has helped demystify the creative process and transform countless lives, from
philosophers
to
illustrators and authors
.
In many of the hundreds of conversations I’ve had with creatives, I’ve asked or been asked the question, “Have you read
The Artist’s Way
?” The answer that follows is often some iteration of, “I enjoyed some of the exercises, but have never finished the book,” or “it’s been sitting on my shelf for years.”
“
“I’m completely changed, and simultaneously unchanged. That, to me, is the wonderful thing about it ­– change is imperfect, it’s two steps forward and one step back, and often vice versa. When it’s lasting, it’s almost undetectable as your new self and your old self merge and stroll and stumble together.”
”
Five years ago, while on a break after finishing studies I bought the Kindle version and began the week by week tasks with gusto, filling three pages with stream-of-consciousness writing each morning and taking myself on artist dates. By week three it came to an abrupt stop.
It’s difficult to determine why I didn’t keep stumbling through – perhaps it was feeling daunted by the “homework” or the religious undertones that didn’t resonate. In the proceeding years, I would stop and start the habit of the morning pages, what Julia Cameron describes as the ‘primary tool for creative recovery’.
With a particularly rocky start to the year, I had decided to be more diligent with filling three pages of brain drain each morning, but hadn’t yet picked up the text I put down five years ago. It wasn’t until an afternoon spent reading by the pool with a dear friend that I spotted her copy of
The Artist’s Way
and began to flip through the pages again. Snippets like “get out of the way, let it work through you” and “you have to stop telling yourself it’s too late” were a balm for this particular period of stuckness I was experiencing.
It was time. I moved into a new sublet in Melbourne and with the new environment came a clean slate to create new habits. I found a copy in a second-hand bookstore, the owner tapping on the cover saying “now this, this will change your life” while she put it through the cash register. Later that evening, I began from the beginning, the homework now viewed as a bedrock for a new routine, and the religious undertones swapped out for words like ‘flow’ and ‘energy’.
Twelve weeks, a dozen artist dates and three Moleksine journals filled with morning pages later, I closed the final page of
The Artist’s Way
and find myself in New York City.
I’m completely changed, and simultaneously unchanged. That, to me, is the wonderful thing about it ­– change is imperfect, it’s two steps forward and one step back, and often vice versa. When it's lasting, it's almost undetectable as your new self and your old self merge and stroll and stumble together.
I learned what can only be learned through going inward, even if that means
looking like you’re doing nothing
from the outside.
Here are my week by week notes and learnings – from listening to yourself to reframing lost opportunities – from the book I encourage any individual feeling blocked to dip into.
Lessons from making it all the way through The Artist’s Way
Week 1: Progress not perfection
The first time I began
The Artist’s Way
it helped spark the idea for my labour of love, Extraordinary Routines. This second attempt is exactly five year’s after the first interview was published in 2014.
So many of this week’s lessons resonate with what I’ve unearthed in the conversations I’ve had with creatives and own personal principles – creativity’s chief need is support and the key is to keep trying and experimenting.
I’m stuck by the description of ‘shadow artists’ – those that are drawn to other artists, but are blocked artists themselves and “caught between the dream of action and the feature of failure.”
I’ve spent been five years of inspecting how other people are creative and yet I haven’t written that book I wanted to write, or launched that podcast I wanted to launch. I can’t linger on that point for too long without spiralling.
“Very often audacity, not talent, makes one person an artist and another a shadow artist – hiding in the shadows, afraid to step out and expose the dream to the light, fearful that it will disintegrate to the torch.

data.title: How arrow-rs is able to decode JSON so fast
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Arroyo团队如何通过arrow-rs库实现高效的列式JSON解码。JSON是流处理管道中常用的序列化格式，但其解析过程往往占用大量CPU资源。为了提高性能，Arroyo使用基于Apache Arrow的列式内存格式，并扩展arrow-json以支持流式处理、原始JSON存储和无效数据处理。通过批量解码，Arroyo能将JSON文档转换为列数组，实现高效操作。与Flink使用的Jackson反序列化器相比，arrow-json在处理大型嵌套记录时速度提升了2.3倍。文章详细介绍了列构建、字符串和列表处理以及结构解码等技术细节，展示了如何通过优化JSON解码提升流处理引擎的速度。

Blog
Updates from the Arroyo team
Fast columnar JSON decoding with arrow-rs
February 25, 2025
JSON is the most common serialization format used in streaming pipelines, so it pays to be able to deserialize it fast. This post covers in detail how the arrow-json library works to perform very efficient columnar JSON decoding, and the additions we've made for streaming use cases.
Micah Wylde
CEO of Arroyo
My day job is working on the
Arroyo
stream processing engine, which executes complex, stateful queries over
high-scale streams of events. Computing things like windowed aggregates, stream
joins, and incrementally-computed SQL involves, as you might imagine, a lot of
sophisticated algorithms and systems. Doing it much faster than existing systems
like Apache Flink took careful performance engineering at every level of the
stack.
But…I'm going to let you in on a little secret. The sad truth of this industry,
which no one will tell you, is that so, so many data pipelines spend the bulk of their
CPU time…deserializing JSON
1
.
That's right. Everybody's favorite human-readable and sorta-human-writable data
interchange format has been responsible for >50% of CPU usage on several
high-scale Flink pipelines I've worked on. And so if you want to build a
fast stream processing engine, you need to start with a fast JSON
deserialization strategy
2
.
Arroyo's internal data representation is built on top of
Arrow
, a columnar in-memory format designed for
fast analytical processing
3
. So our challenge is to take row-oriented JSON;
parse it, and build out columns from the corresponding field in each
document. And do this as fast as possible.
Fortunately, we don't have to start from scratch: the
arrow-rs project
includes a very fast JSON
decoder, largely written by
Raphael Taylor-Davies
. I found the approach quite
interesting and thought it was worth writing up. So we'll dig into how
arrow-json works and then talk through Arroyo's extensions to support
raw
JSON
—leaving parts of the JSON serialized—and the ability to skip records in a
batch that don't match the schema. Along the way you should pick up some
intuition for how to work with columnar data, which many engineers find
challenging and unfamiliar in our typically row-oriented world.
Table of contents
But is this fast?
Batched decoding
Stealing from the best
Run the tape

Lists
An example

Primitive and String decoding
Streaming extensions
Raw JSON
Invalid data handling
Wrapping up
But is this fast?
Before we get into the details, we might want to answer the question…is this
actually fast? And the answer is: yes! Benchmarking against the Jackson-based
deserializer used for Flink SQL, arrow-json is up to 2.3x faster:

(See
https://github.com/ArroyoSystems/json-benchmarks
for the benchmark source code and test documents.)
Arrow-json does particularly well with large, deeply nested records, and poorly
with enum-like structures where there are many null fields.
Batched decoding
Arrow, like other columnar formats, operates in
batches
. We're almost never
dealing with just one record (or “row”) of data, because columnar formats
achieve their high performance by storing many values together in a single
array. If you just have one row, the columnar overhead eats any performance
gains.
So our goal is to take a bunch of JSON documents (generally with a top-level
object) and turn them into a set of arrays representing each column of the
schema.
To make this concrete, let's take data representing HTTP server logs:

data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章展示了ASCII艺术和与之相关的一系列创作，包括文本和视觉元素。主画面是一个以ASCII码构成的卧室，伴随各种作者和作品名称，如Eileen Ahn的"Airs"和Reuben Son的"Pure Information"。文章探讨了幻觉、沟通、导航等主题，并通过不同的艺术形式表达。例如，Maya被描述为神和恶魔制造幻觉的超自然力量，而导航队列则比喻成没有终点的无限滚动条。其他作品如Nica Marimba和Answered Interruptions则通过音乐和中断的主题进行艺术表达。整体上，文章结合了视觉艺术和概念性探讨，呈现出多样化的数字创作。

data.title: Blue Ghost lander captures sunset shots on moon before falling silent
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 2025年3月18日，由Firefly Aerospace和NASA发布的私营月球登陆器Blue Ghost在月球上拍摄了首批高清日落照片，展示了地球和金星。这些照片是在Blue Ghost于3月2日登陆后、于周末失去动力前拍摄的。Blue Ghost是首个成功垂直着陆并完成全部任务的私营航天器，在月球夜间仍继续工作了五个小时，直至因缺乏太阳能而停止运行。NASA表示，这些高分辨率照片将用于深入分析月球地平线辉光是否由悬浮尘埃造成。尽管所有任务目标已达成，但登陆器钻机仅钻入月球表面1米，未达预期3米。Firefly计划于4月初尝试重新激活Blue Ghost，但工程师对此持怀疑态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：从月球上看地球日食的照片，以及月球探测器在寒冷夜晚失效的原因。

不同观点：
• [perihelions] 分享了从月球上看到地球日食的照片链接，展示了多个照片。
• [crazygringo] 对这些照片表示困惑，特别是对其中一些照片中出现两个“太阳”的现象提出疑问，怀疑其中一个是镜头光晕或曝光问题，因为从照片上看是地球的暗面。
  • 具体论据：指出其中一张照片中，地球的暗面不应该有过曝的亮光，且另一张照片中，地球似乎遮挡了第二个“太阳”的一部分，这增加了其困惑。

• [celeritascelery] 则关注月球探测器在月夜中失效的原因，特别提到是否是由于电池问题，并推测电路系统应该不受影响。
  • 具体论据：提出电池可能是探测器在寒冷夜晚失效的主要原因，暗示电路系统可能比电池更耐寒。

补充讨论：
• [babyent] 表达了对月球探测器的同情，尽管探测器只是一个机器，但其失效仍然引发了情感共鸣。
  • 这一评论并未涉及技术讨论，而是从情感层面回应了探测器失效的问题。

争议焦点：
• [crazygringo] 对照片中两个“太阳”现象的真实原因表示不解，并提出了镜头光晕的可能性，但未得到明确解答，显示出对照片真实性的争议。

总结：讨论主要围绕月球上看到地球日食的照片真实性及其可能的解释，以及月球探测器在月夜中失效的技术原因。

Blue Ghost lander captures stunning sunset shots on the moon before falling silent
by Marcia Dunn
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace, Tuesday, March 18, 2025, shows the sun setting on the moon, with Earth and Venus in the distance. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
A
private lunar lander
has captured the first high-definition sunset pictures from the moon.
Firefly Aerospace and NASA released the stunning photos Tuesday, taken before the
Blue Ghost lander
fell silent over the weekend. One shot included Venus in the distance.
Firefly's Blue Ghost landed on the
moon
on March 2, the
first private spacecraft
to touch down upright and perform its entire mission. It kept taking pictures and collecting science data five hours into the lunar night before it died for lack of solar energy.
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace shows the sun about to emerge from totality behind Earth. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace, Tuesday, March 18, 2025, shows the sun setting on the moon, with Earth and Venus in the distance. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace shows Earth captured by Blue Ghost shortly after landing from the lunar surface. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
NASA's Joel Kearns said Blue Ghost's series of sunset shots are the first
high-resolution images
from Earth's neighbor. Scientists will need to analyze them in depth, he noted, before making any determination about the horizon glow captured in at least one of the photos and whether it was created by levitating dust. That theory was put forth more than a half-century ago by Apollo 17's Gene Cernan, the last astronaut to walk on the moon.
"What we've got is a really beautiful, aesthetic image showing some really unusual features," Kearns said at a news conference.
Blue Ghost carried 10 experiments for NASA under the space agency's commercial lunar delivery program. While all objectives were met, officials said, the on-board drill could only penetrate 3 feet (1 meter) into the moon versus the 10 feet (3 meters) that had been planned.
Firefly said it will try to activate the lunar lander in early April following the two-week, bitter cold lunar night, although engineers are doubtful it will crank back up.

  • 具体论据：指出其中一张照片中，地球的暗面不应该有过曝的亮光，且另一张照片中，地球似乎遮挡了第二个“太阳”的一部分，这增加了其困惑。

• [celeritascelery] 则关注月球探测器在月夜中失效的原因，特别提到是否是由于电池问题，并推测电路系统应该不受影响。
  • 具体论据：提出电池可能是探测器在寒冷夜晚失效的主要原因，暗示电路系统可能比电池更耐寒。

补充讨论：
• [babyent] 表达了对月球探测器的同情，尽管探测器只是一个机器，但其失效仍然引发了情感共鸣。
  • 这一评论并未涉及技术讨论，而是从情感层面回应了探测器失效的问题。

争议焦点：
• [crazygringo] 对照片中两个“太阳”现象的真实原因表示不解，并提出了镜头光晕的可能性，但未得到明确解答，显示出对照片真实性的争议。

总结：讨论主要围绕月球上看到地球日食的照片真实性及其可能的解释，以及月球探测器在月夜中失效的技术原因。

Monster Cables picked the wrong guy to threaten
by
Dell C. "D. C." Toedt III
on
2008-04-16
Monster Cables, which makes extremely high-priced stereo cables, has apparently sent a
cease-and-desist letter
to
Blue Jeans Cable
, alleging various kinds of infringement.  Bad move – the president of Blue Jeans Cable, Kurt Denke, is a former litigator who
responded pretty forcefully
:
… Once I have received the above materials and explanations from you, I will undertake to analyze this information and let you know whether we are willing to accede to any of the demands made in your letter.
If my analysis shows that there is any reasonable likelihood that we have infringed in any way any of Monster Cable’s intellectual property rights, we will of course take any and all action necessary to resolve the situation.
If I do not hear from you within the next fourteen days, or if I do hear from you but do not receive
all of the information requested above, I will assume that you have abandoned these claims and closed your file.
As for your requests for information, or for action, directed to me: I would remind you that it is you, not I, who are making claims; and it is you, not I, who must substantiate those claims.  You have not done so.
I have seen Monster Cable take untenable IP positions in various different scenarios in the past, and am generally familiar with what seems to be Monster Cable’s
modus operandi in these matters.  I therefore think that it is important that, before closing, I make you aware of a few points.
After graduating from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 1985, I spent nineteen years in litigation practice, with a focus upon federal litigation involving large damages and complex issues.  My first seven years were spent primarily on the defense side, where
I developed an intense frustration with insurance carriers who would settle meritless claims for nuisance value when the better long-term view would have been to fight against vexatious litigation as a matter of principle.
In plaintiffs’ practice, likewise, I was always a strong advocate of standing upon principle and taking cases all the way to judgment, even when substantial offers of settlement were on the table.  I am “uncompromising” in the most literal sense of the word.  If Monster Cable proceeds with litigation against me I will pursue the same merits-driven approach; I do not compromise with bullies and
I would rather spend fifty thousand dollars on defense than give you a dollar of unmerited settlement funds.
As for signing a licensing agreement for intellectual property which I have not infringed: that will not happen, under any circumstances, whether it makes economic sense or not.
I say this because my observation has been that Monster Cable typically operates in a hit-and-run fashion.  Your client threatens litigation, expecting the victim to panic and plead for mercy; and what follows is a quickie negotiation session that ends with payment and a licensing agreement.  Your client then uses this collection of licensing agreements to convince others under similar threat to accede to its demands.  Let me be clear about this:
there are only two ways for you to get anything out of me.  You will either need to (1) convince me that I have infringed, or (2) obtain a final judgment to that effect from a court of competent jurisdiction.
It may be that my inability to see the pragmatic value of settling frivolous claims is a deep character flaw, and I am sure a few of the insurance carriers for whom I have done work have seen it that way; but it is how I have done business for the last quarter-century and you are not going to change my mind.  If you sue me, the case will go to judgment, and I will hold the court’s attention upon the merits of your claims–or, to speak more precisely, the absence of merit from your claims–from start to finish.
Not only am I unintimidated by litigation; I sometimes rather miss it.
(Emphasis added; hat tip: Jeff Nolan at
Venture Chronicles
.)
I can relate to Denke’s final comment quoted above ….  I wonder what the attendant publicity is doing for his sales.

data.title: Show HN: GoRead – Terminal epub reader
data.author: Ray-D-Song
data.article_summary: GoRead 是一个用 Golang 编写的命令行 EPUB 阅读器，支持 EPUB3（不含音频），具有跨平台特性。它可以记住最后阅读的文件和阅读状态，支持代码高亮、调整文本宽度、适应终端大小变化，以及查看图片（使用系统默认图片查看器）。此外，它提供 Vim 风格的键绑定，支持暗色和亮色主题。未来计划支持 mobi 格式。用户可以通过命令读取历史文件、导出 EPUB 内容以及使用多种键绑定进行导航和操作。该项目依赖于 Go 1.16 及以上版本、tcell 和 tview 库，并提供了构建多平台可执行文件的 Makefile 脚本。许可证为 MIT。

FaceStream
This is a web app that let's you swap your face in real-time without having a powerful
machine. You can try it out live
here
.
See the gif below for a demo:
Motivation
I discovered the
Deep Live Cam
project and tried to run it on my M1 MacBook, but only got 0.5 FPS. So I wanted to explore how fast and at what latency you could get this to run on a remote server via WebRTC.
How to run this yourself
Prerequisites
To run this yourself you wil need:
uv
A
modal
account as well configured credentials
Then you can run the following command to start the server:
uv run modal serve facestream.main
Or this command to deploy it:
uv run modal deploy facestream.main
Optional: TURN Server for Cellular Networks
On most cellular networks you need a TURN server for WebRTC to work. You can create a TURN app on
Cloudflare
. To use those with this app you need to:
Create a secret called
facestream
in modal with the following values:
TURN_TOKEN_ID=your-turn-token-id
TURN_API_TOKEN=your-turn-api-token
Comment out the following line in
src/facestream/main.py
:
...
secrets=[
modal.Secret.from_name(
"facestream",
required_keys=[SECRET_KEY_TURN_TOKEN_ID, SECRET_KEY_TURN_API_TOKEN],
)
]
...
Credits
This project was inspired by and uses the model of
Deep Live Cam
. Go check out their project. They have some extra features that I didn't implement here. Note that the model used in that project (and therefore also this one) is only for non-commercial use.
Modal
made this easy to build and deploy. They are generously providing free credits to host the live demo.

  - 认为社交媒体平台作为私人企业，有权对其平台上的内容进行审核和管理。
  - 强调平台需要对仇恨言论、虚假信息以及其他有害内容进行控制，以维护健康的讨论环境。

• **反对内容审核的观点**：
  - 认为内容审核侵犯了用户的言论自由，尤其是在政治观点上的审查，可能导致偏见和不公正。
  - 担心平台审核机制缺乏透明度，容易被用作打压不同意见的工具。

  - 认为可以在保护言论自由和维护平台健康环境之间找到平衡。
  - 建议建立独立的审核机构或申诉机制，以确保审核的公正性和透明度。
  - 提出通过技术手段，如人工智能辅助审核，来提高审核效率和准确性。

43458509.article_content:
← All posts
Millions are visiting the European Alternatives site––what trends are we seeing?
Mar 24, 2025
• Written by
Hricha Shandily
☝️That’s a screenshot from the publicly open Plausible Analytics dashboard of the European Alternatives
website
, featuring independent, privacy-friendly digital tools.
With almost 2M visitors, 2.3M total visits, and 8.5M pageviews, this library is no longer a niche project—it’s the go-to destination for users looking for independent, privacy-friendly tools. Over 1 million of the ~2 million all-time visitors came in 2025 alone—and we’re only in March.
Let’s use the analytics
dashboard
to see what trends are emerging and what is the demand looking like for EU-built, privacy-friendly tech.
1100% surge in 2025 traffic
Reddit surpasses Google, while privacy-friendly search engines gain traction
Top 5 categories: What are people looking for?
Not just a European trend—demand goes beyond the EU borders
European countries leading (and lagging) in the shift to privacy-friendly tools
Which European tools are winning?
Need a hand in deciding which tools to go with?
Privacy-friendly web analytics is on the rise
1100% surge in 2025 traffic
If we filter the dashboard by “Year to date” period, i.e. 2025 so far, we see there have been 1.3 million visitors to the website, with a surge of 1.1K%.
Another interesting number is the “time on page,” which is 2m47s spent on average. This goes on to show that people are interested and engaging well with the library.
Reddit surpasses Google, while privacy-friendly search engines gain traction
Look at the Top Sources report for 2025 so far:
Google is typically the dominant search driver for most websites—but not here. Reddit ranks as the second-largest traffic source, bringing in 311K visitors—significantly more than Google (193K). This isn’t a regular thing we see with sites.
This suggests that people aren’t just searching for alternatives but are actively discussing and recommending them in forums, subreddits, and privacy-conscious communities.
But here’s another interesting insight: Privacy-friendly search engines are also key traffic sources:
DuckDuckGo: 33.8K visitors
Ecosia: 13.5K visitors
Qwant: 10.8K visitors
This says something about the increasing preference for privacy-friendly tools, i.e., more people are actively using privacy-friendly search engines to discover other privacy-friendly alternatives.
Top 5 categories: What are people looking for?
A quick look at the “Top Pages” report tells us about the most popular top 5 categories:
- Email providers
- Search Engines
- Cloud Computing Platforms
- Navigation Apps
- Web Analytics Services
Upon expanding the report, we can take a deeper look at the most popular categories in terms of unique visitors, while comparing the engagement metrics.
B2B categories win?
While categories like email providers, search engines, and navigation apps attract a large B2C audience, B2B categories are more diverse and consistently rank high.
Businesses are actively seeking privacy-friendly analytics, hosting, and infrastructure alternatives, driving growth in EU-built tools.
Not just a European trend—demand goes beyond the EU borders
Looking at the
all-time Countries report
: European countries make up the bulk of visitors (as expected), but the United States ranks fourth, sending over 100K visitors to the site!
Even Canada and India make an appearance in the top 25, contributing decent amounts of visitors to the site.
If you scroll all the way down, or simply look at the “Map view,” there’s hardly any part of the globe that’s not participating in the shift towards privacy-focused digital tools.
Privacy-conscious users are everywhere.
European countries leading (and lagging) in the shift to privacy-friendly tools
Germany leads in visitor numbers, with 379K, and contributing 20.5% of the total traffic all-time! This is followed by the Netherlands (141K) and France (135K). These countries show significant engagement with European digital alternatives.
On the lower end, Guernsey recorded 130 visitors, while regions like Vatican City State and Saint Martin (French part) had 3 each. The variation in engagement levels may reflect differences in population size, internet adoption rates, etc.
Which European tools are winning?
The dashboard has an
Outbound link click goal
configured, which is useful in understanding which listed tools eventually attract real visitors. Once we filter the dashboard by this goal (see it
here
), we can see which URLs were clicked.
From these results, these are the top 10 tools receiving traffic from the EU alternatives website:
Mailbox.org
(email provider)
ProtonMail
(email provider)
Soverin
(email provider)
Startpage
(search engine)
Qwant
(search engine)
Posteo
(email provider)
Ecosia
(search engine)
Scaleway
(cloud provider)
Startmail
(email provider)
Good search
(search engine)
And if we look at the all-time data, there’s a whopping 1.2M total outbound clicks from the website to such tools

data.title: European Cloud, Global Reach
data.author: Sami_Lehtinen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对UpCloud等欧洲云服务商的评价与争议

不同观点：
• **支持UpCloud**：
   - **scandox**：认为对UpCloud的批评过于苛刻，虽然不完美，但欧洲供应商需要起步，且Hetzner在某些方面更好。
   - **hap_stark**：基于多年使用经验，认为UpCloud功能可靠，技术支持优秀，且始终有人工服务。
   - **cheeseface**：小规模使用体验良好，管理界面出色。

• **对UpCloud的批评与质疑**：
   - **sschueller**：指出UpCloud依赖Cloudflare提供SSL，质疑其完全欧洲化的承诺。
   - **rustc**：对UpCloud的“零成本出口”宣传持怀疑态度，认为其带宽限制与DigitalOcean相似，有误导嫌疑。
   - **o_m**：指出UpCloud数据中心由美国公司Equinix提供，存在安全隐患。

• **关于欧洲技术独立的讨论**：
   - **bittermandel**：认为无法完全摆脱美国公司在基础设施中的影响，Equinix等提供的解决方案非常有价值。
   - **cpach**：通过“I, Pencil”类比，说明全球经济复杂性，认为完全欧洲化的技术栈不现实。
   - **mischa108**：指出即使在欧洲，设备多运行Windows系统，难以摆脱微软依赖。

• **价格与竞争比较**：
   - **EVa5I7bHFq9mnYK**：对比UpCloud与Hetzner的48核服务器价格，认为Hetzner更具性价比。

• **其他建议与思考**：
   - **rglullis**：提议创建基于欧洲云的开放源码SaaS解决方案，集成单点登录和统一收费。
   - **ArtTimeInvestor**：只使用上市公司提供的基础设施服务，因其透明度高，目前选择限于IONOS和OVH。

补充讨论：
• **对页面和帖子管理的质疑**：
   - **bittermandel**：质疑帖子为何从首页移除。
   - **egorfine**：对UpCloud“超越合规”的宣传持批评态度，认为欧洲服务应放松而非收紧监管。

争议焦点：
• UpCloud是否真正实现了欧洲化，特别是在数据安全和基础设施方面。
• 欧洲技术独立的现实可行性及其在全球经济中的定位。
• 不同服务商的价格与性能比较，用户在选择时的考量因素。

主要讨论点：用户对Deduce软件的评价与讨论，涉及其易用性、应用场景、许可证问题以及技术实现。

不同观点：
• [iNic] 认为Deduce的语法比Lean更友好，可能非常适合教育用途，但对Deduce的Live Code环境提出批评，指出在运行首页代码时遇到错误提示，导致体验不佳。

• [rendaw] 对Deduce作为教育用途的定位提出疑问，质疑为什么它不能作为通用证明检查器使用，暗示可能存在功能或设计上的限制。

• [angelaguilera] 关注Deduce的软件许可证问题，提到网上称其为开源软件，但在GitHub仓库中未找到明确的许可证信息，对开源性质表示疑虑。

• [vitalmixofntrnt] 从技术角度出发，基于Curry-Howard同构性，询问Deduce是否具备将证明编译为机器代码的编译器，并提到是否支持内联汇编，显示出对该软件技术深度的关注。

• [ratmice] 对教育性证明检查器表示赞赏，提到以前使用过类似软件（如tutch proof checker）。同时指出Deduce缺少类似头文件的功能来声明证明类型，但对Deduce的语法表示肯定。

• [Q6T46nT668w6i3m] 表示期待尝试Deduce，通常推荐Daniel Velleman的“Proof Designer”，但听说对初学者来说可能过于晦涩，暗示Deduce可能更适合初学者。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Deduce是否仅适合教育用途，[rendaw]对该定位表示质疑，认为它可能也应该能作为通用工具使用。
• Deduce的Live Code环境和许可证问题也是用户关注的重点，[iNic]和[angelaguilera]分别对其实际使用体验和开源许可证的透明性提出质疑。
• 用户对Deduce的技术实现和功能扩展（如编译器支持和头文件功能）也有一定期待和讨论，[vitalmixofntrnt]和[ratmice]分别从不同角度提出期望和建议。

data.title: Did you spot a fish? Press the Fish Doorbell
data.author: rguiscard
data.article_summary: 《Fish Doorbell》是一项帮助鱼类通过乌得勒支Oudegracht的创新项目。每年春季，大量鱼类洄游至上游产卵，但由于Weerdsluis水闸常关闭，鱼类旅程受阻。公众可在发现鱼类时按下"Fish Doorbell"通知水闸管理员开闸。项目网站提供新闻报告、鱼类照片和物种识别功能，并鼓励用户上传鱼类照片。若未看到鱼，用户还可以观看之前的鱼类视频。此外，项目还提供教育资源，教导如何观察鱼类及保护水下生态，特别适合学生学习。通过公众参与，Fish Doorbell有效帮助鱼类完成洄游之旅。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕在水下摄像头观察鱼类及其他相关话题的讨论

不同观点：
• [怀旧与历史背景] morphle 提到自己在这个地方生活了61年，但对水中的鱼类活动毫不知情，直到看到这个水下摄像头。他还介绍了该地区的历史背景，包括乌得勒支的城市发展以及克罗姆莱茵河/维赫特河的演变，强调了这个地点在历史上的重要性。

• [幽默与调侃] throw310822 用幽默的方式将水下摄像头比作沉入 erwtensoep（一种荷兰豌豆汤），并开玩笑说看到了一只游泳的 rookworst（荷兰熏肠）。这种评论以轻松的方式参与讨论，没有深入的技术分析。

• [技术讨论与链接] ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7 提到这个话题在一年前已经被讨论过，并提供了一个链接供参考，显示出对技术社区讨论历史的关注。

• [页面设计问题] frizlab 对页面的滚动功能表示不满，认为被强行改变了，这反映了一些用户对用户体验的关注。

• [技术可行性与挑战] rapnie 提到鱼游得太快，很难捕捉到它们的截图，指出技术上的挑战。

• [兴趣与愿望] cyanf 简单表达了对水下摄像头观察鱼类的喜悦，纯粹出于兴趣。

• [技术需求与设想] MrMcCall 表达了对遥控水下机器人（ROV）的兴趣，希望能够探索湖泊、溪流或海洋，但指出了可能遇到的问题，如被卡住、电力不足和水下浑浊。

• [技术解决方案] cluckindan 提出是否可以通过人工智能（AI）进行鱼类识别，而不是依赖众包，讨论了使用一次性对象检测模型的可能性，显示了对技术解决方案的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然没有直接的激烈争议，但不同用户显然对水下摄像头的使用有不同关注点，有的侧重历史与文化背景，有的侧重技术挑战与解决方案。
• 讨论关系：一些评论是对水下摄像头观察鱼类的直接反应（如 humor 和 delight），而其他评论则引入了技术讨论和历史背景。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：页面设计问题虽然在主题上稍有偏离，但也反映出用户体验在技术讨论中的重要性。

Every spring, thousands of fish swim through the Oudegracht in Utrecht, searching for a place upstream to lay their eggs. But the Weerdsluis is often closed. You can help the fish continue their journey! If you see a fish, press the doorbell. This alerts the lock operator to open the lock.

data.title: Building and Publishing Games to Steam Directly from GitHub Actions
data.author: delduca
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用GitHub Actions自动化构建和发布游戏到Steam平台。作者通过GitHub Actions实现了一个2D躲猫猫游戏的自动发布管道，只需创建新标签，几分钟后Steam客户端就会下载更新。文章详细描述了使用GitHub Actions的YAML配置，包括并行编译Windows、macOS、Linux和WebAssembly版本，依赖缓存、构建配置、打包和发布步骤。发布到Steam需要开发者账户、生成密钥、安装steamcmd等步骤，并将相关密钥和配置保存到GitHub Actions变量中。当前仅支持Windows版本自动发布，作者计划未来可能增加更多功能如固定运行时版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用GitHub Actions和YAML进行游戏发布和工作流调试的相关问题

不同观点：
• [adobrawy] 认为在YAML中直接放置带有具体命令的"run"语句可能会导致本地调试困难。他建议减少"run"语句的数量，仅用于执行脚本，这样可以在本地运行脚本，而不必每次都等待整个CI管道执行，从而提高调试效率。

• [nevon] 指出原文并没有详细讨论如何从GitHub Actions发布游戏，只是用三行引用了包含实际实现的https://github.com/game-ci/steam-deploy链接。他暗示希望看到更多关于如何具体实现游戏发布的细节。

• [hedin_hiervard] 提出了关于Steam Guard代码处理的问题，暗示在游戏发布到Steam的过程中，如何处理Steam Guard的安全验证码可能是一个需要解决的重要问题。

补充讨论：
• adobrawy的观点特别关注工作流的可调试性和效率，建议通过减少YAML中的"run"语句来优化开发流程。
• nevon的观点强调了对具体实现细节的需求，特别是对游戏发布到Steam的实际操作感兴趣。
• hedin_hiervard的问题指向了实际应用中的一个潜在障碍，即Steam Guard的安全验证，这可能是使用GitHub Actions发布游戏到Steam的一个关键挑战。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在工作流的调试效率和实际发布游戏的具体实现细节上。特别是如何处理Steam Guard代码的问题，可能是发布流程中的一个实际障碍。

43453059.article_content:
Building and Publishing Games to Steam Directly from GitHub Actions
23 Mar 2025
I have been using GitHub Actions extensively both at work and in personal projects, as shown in this post
What I’ve been automating with GitHub Actions, an automated life
.
In my free time, I’m working on a 2D hide-and-seek game, and as you might expect, I’ve automated the entire release pipeline for publishing on Steam. After a few attempts, when it finally worked, it felt like magic: all I had to do was create a new tag, and within minutes, the Steam client was downloading the update.
As I mentioned earlier, I have a 2D engine that, while simple, is quite comprehensive. With each new tag, I compile it in parallel for Windows, macOS, Linux, and WebAssembly. Once compilation is complete, I create a release and publish it on GitHub.

data.title: The Mystery of the Oldest Writing System Remained Unsolved Until 1856
data.author: wyclif
data.article_summary: 在1850年代，楔形文字仍是未解之谜。直到四位学者竞相破译，这一世界上最古老的文字系统才开始揭示美索不达米亚古文明的秘密。特别是大英博物馆的一块有3000年历史的泥板，记录了亚述国王提格拉特帕拉沙尔一世的军事胜利。这块泥板成为破解楔形文字的关键，四位学者的竞争最终推动了古代文字的解读，揭开了历史的面纱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对Hormuzd Rassam的身份认定及其背景的争议，以及对破译古文字方法的讨论]

不同观点：
• [yubblegum的观点] Hormuzd Rassam 不是阿拉伯人，而是亚述人。yubblegum 指出，Rassam 的名字 "Hormuzd" 源自古代伊朗对神明的称呼，因此不可能是阿拉伯人。此外，yubblegum 还提到，根据维基百科的资料，Rassam 的母亲来自犹太家庭，其祖父的名字是 Isaak Halabee，这是犹太名字 יצחק חליבה 的阿拉伯化变体。yubblegum 对史密森学会旗下的杂志出现这样的错误表示失望，尤其是在一篇讨论该地区古老语言的文章中。

• [对yubblegum观点的补充] yubblegum 引用了多个来源支持其观点，包括维基百科上关于 Hormuzd Rassam 的早期生活页面，以及关于 Ishak Haleva 的页面，指出 Haleva 和他祖父的名字相同，进一步证明 Rassam 的家庭背景具有犹太和亚述成分，而非阿拉伯背景。

• [z3t4的观点] z3t4 对破译古文字的方法提出疑问，询问是否通过猜测一个符号的意义，然后通过上下文推断其含义。同时，z3t4 提到了 "Rawlinson Method"（罗林森方法），但没有详细解释，暗示对这种破译方法的兴趣或疑惑。

补充讨论：
• yubblegum 对历史人物身份的细致考证反映了对历史和文化背景准确性的重视，尤其是在讨论古代语言和文化时。

• z3t4 的问题揭示了对古文字破译方法的兴趣，尤其是 "Rawlinson Method" 可能涉及的具体技术和步骤。这一问题可能引发进一步的讨论，关于破译古代文字的方法论及其在考古学中的应用。

争议焦点：Hormuzd Rassam 的民族身份是争议的核心，yubblegum 强调其亚述和犹太背景，而非阿拉伯背景，这与某些文献可能存在的错误认定形成对比。

data.title: Rust Additions for GCC 15 Bring Support for If-Let Statements
data.author: Corrado
data.article_summary: GCC 15即将发布的稳定版引入了一系列Rust编译器（gccrs）的改进，包括对"if let"语句的支持。Polonius借用检查器及其他重大改进已合并。Arthur Cohen提交了146个补丁，增加了对"if let"语句的支持，并对AST/HIR内部表示进行了大幅修改，同时完整实现了Clone和Copy特性。对PartialOrd和PartialEq的支持预计也将在GCC 15.1发布前加入。这些改进使gccrs成为官方Rust编译器（rustc）的更实用替代方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 语言在更多场景中的应用进展以及具体语法问题

不同观点：
• Corrado 对 Rust 在更多领域中的进展表示支持和乐观态度。他认为这是将 Rust 引入更多场景的好进展，并对 Rust-GCC 中某些类型的不支持表示惊讶。
• 有人对 Rust 中的 "if" 和 "if let" 语法存在疑问或兴趣，Corrado 提供了一个参考链接（MIT 文档）来解释两者的区别，表明社区中有人关注 Rust 语言的细节和语法差异。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的 Rust-GCC 对某些类型的支持不足，暗示了在 Rust 编译器工具链方面可能存在需要改进的地方。
• 讨论中引用的外部资源（MIT 文档）表明，社区成员愿意分享学习资源来帮助他人理解语言细节，这反映了 Rust 社区的协作和知识共享文化。
• 争议焦点：目前在评论中未见直接争议，但潜在的争议可能围绕 Rust-GCC 的功能完整性以及与其他编译器（如 Rust LLVM）的比较展开。

43458633.article_content:
Rust Additions For GCC 15 Bring Support For if-let Statements, Other Improvements
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
GNU
on 23 March 2025 at 06:35 AM EDT.
11 Comments
This past week a lot of new code for the Rust "gccrs" front-end began being merged for the upcoming GCC 15.1 stable release...
The Polonius borrow checker landed
along with
other big improvements to the Rust code
ahead of this annual GNU Compiler Collection release. A third round was merged on Friday adding yet more gccrs features.
Arthur Cohen of Embecosm landed another set of 146 patches into the GCC 15 codebase on Friday. This third round includes support for Rust's "if let" statements, and some reported massive changes to their AST/HIR internal representations, and support for Clone and Copy being fully implemented.
Support for PartialOrd and PartialEq is also still expected to be upstreamed for gccrs before the GCC 15.1 stable release. Cohen commented with the
third set of patches
cover letter:
"This is our the third patchset in the series for updating upstream GCC with the latest changes in our development repository.
Most notably this contains handling for if-let statements by Marc Poulhiès, changes to our name-resolution pass rewrite, and massive changes to our AST and HIR representations to allow Rust lang-item paths to be represented. This is different from how the official Rust compiler handles lang-items, but allows us to refer to essential Rust items easily while we are still in the process of compiling said core crate.
These lang-item changes also enabled us to continue our work on built-in derive macros, with Clone and Copy being fully implemented in this patchset. The remaining built-in derive macros will be upstreamed in the next patchset. We are still missing on PartialOrd and PartialEq, which will be upstreamed in time for 15.1.
There are also multiple type-system fixes, and testsuite fixes for systems with different endianness."
It's great seeing the many gccrs improvements land in time for the GCC 15 stable release in order to make the gccrs front-end more practical and useful as an alternative to Rust's official LLVM-based rustc compiler.

data.title: A 1930s movement wanted to merge the US, Canada and Greenland
data.author: valeg
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了1930年代的“技术统治运动”，该运动主张将美国、加拿大、墨西哥、格陵兰和部分中美洲地区合并为一个由科技和科学原则治理的“技术统治体”（Technate），以消除浪费、提高生产力。该运动由工程师霍华德·斯科特等人领导，受到大萧条时期的经济困境推动，吸引了大量工程师和科学家的支持。技术统治论者反对传统政治治理，主张由科学和工程专家客观管理资源，通过自动化和机械化减少人力需求，并根据能源效率调控生产和消费。尽管该运动在早期获得关注，但其激进理念最终未能实现。不过，其思想在现代一些关于政府效率和科技治理的讨论中仍产生共鸣，例如特朗普政府时期的一些提议以及埃隆·马斯克对官僚制度的批评。

A movement that wanted to merge North America into one nation and extend its borders as far as the Panama Canal might sound
incredibly familiar
. But this group, called the
“technocracy movement”
, was a group of 1930s nonconformists with big ideas about how to rearrange US society. They proposed a vision that would get rid of waste and make North America highly productive by using technology and science.
The Technocrats, sometimes also called Technocracy Inc,
proposed
merging Canada, Greenland, Mexico, the US and parts of central America into
a single continental unit
. This they called a “Technate”. It was to be governed by technocratic principles, rather than by national borders and traditional
political divisions
.
These ideas seem to resonate with some recent statements from the
Trump administration
about merging the US with Canada. Meanwhile, the US
Department of Government Efficiency
(Doge) set up by Trump and led by tech billionaire Elon Musk, has also outlined a vision of efficiency cuts by slashing bureaucracy, jobs and getting rid of leaders of organisations and civil servants he thinks are advancing “woke”
values
(such as diversity initiatives). This slash-and-burn approach also fits with some of the ideas of the Technocrats.
In February,
Musk said
: “We really have here rule of the bureaucracy as opposed to rule of the people — democracy”. The Technocrats viewed elected politicians as incompetent. They advocated replacing them with experts in science and engineering, who would “objectively” manage resources for the benefit of society.
“The people voted for major government reform, and that’s what the people are going to get,”
Musk told
reporters after visiting the White House last month.
What did the Technocrats want to get rid of?
The
1930s’ movement
was an educational and research organisation that advocated for a fundamental reorganisation of political, social and economic structures in the US and Canada.  It drew on
a book called Technocracy published
in 1921 by an engineer called Walter Henry Smyth, which captured new ideas about management and science.
The movement gained significant attention during the
Great Depression
, a period of mass unemployment and economic problems lasting from 1929 to 1939. This was a time when widespread economic failures prompted radical ideas for systemic change. Technocracy appealed to those who saw technological advancements as a potential solution to economic inefficiency and inequality.
The Technocrats gained traction largely due to the work of Howard Scott, an engineer and economist, along with a group of engineers and academics from Columbia University. In 1932, Scott founded the Technical Alliance, which later evolved into
Technocracy Inc
.
Scott
and his followers held lectures, published pamphlets and attracted a significant following, particularly among engineers, scientists and progressive thinkers. The movement may have influenced the design of future concepts such as planned communities and economies using more automation.
The movement’s
ideological foundation
was built on the belief that industrial production and distribution should be managed scientifically. Advocates argued that traditional economic systems such as capitalism and socialism were inefficient and prone to corruption, but that a scientifically planned economy could ensure abundance, stability and fairness.
An image from the Cornell University collection on the Technocracy movement.
Cornell University – PJ Mode Collection of Persuasive Cartography
In the 1930s, members of Technocracy Inc
sought
to replace market-based economies and political governance with a system where experts made decisions based on data, efficiency and technological feasibility. Technocrats
aimed to
regulate consumption and production based on energy efficiency, rather than market forces.
Technocrats also believed that mechanisation and automation could eliminate much of the need for human labour, reducing work hours while maintaining productivity. Goods and services would be distributed based on scientific calculations of need and sustainability.

data.article_summary: 前美国弗吉尼亚东区检察官杰西卡·阿伯（Jessica Aber）在43岁时被发现死亡。她曾主导多项涉及情报泄露、战争罪调查以及敏感技术转移的高调案件，包括起诉一名泄露机密信息的CIA分析师和涉及向俄罗斯非法运输技术的公司高管。阿伯在2023年初辞职，此前她领导了约300名检察官，处理国家安全和恐怖主义相关案件。她的工作包括打击网络犯罪和洗钱活动，并强调对违反国家安全法律的行为进行严厉起诉。阿伯的去世引发了广泛关注，因为她参与的案件对美国及全球伙伴具有重要影响。

Former U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, Jessica Aber, who was found dead at the age of 43 by Virginia authorities on Saturday, was at the helm of high-profile investigations into intelligence leaks, allegations of war crimes against Russian-linked individuals and people suspected of providing sensitive U.S. technology to Moscow before she stepped down at the start of the year.
Why It Matters
Aber, an appointee of former President
Joe Biden
, resigned in January after President
Donald Trump
was inaugurated. She had risen to lead one of the most important federal prosecutor's offices and roughly 300 prosecutors, civil litigators, and support personnel, regularly tasked with national security and terrorism-related cases.
The Alexandria Police Department said on Saturday that officers responded shortly after 9 a.m. local time to reports of an unresponsive woman at Beverley Drive, north of downtown and south of Arlington.
Then U.S. Attorney Jessica Aber for the Eastern District of Virginia, center, at the Department of Justice on December 6, 2023, in Washington D.C., as former Attorney General Merrick Garland, left, and former Secretary of...
Then U.S. Attorney Jessica Aber for the Eastern District of Virginia, center, at the Department of Justice on December 6, 2023, in Washington D.C., as former Attorney General Merrick Garland, left, and former Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas, look on.
More
AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein
What To Know
In mid-January, Asif Rahman, a former
CIA
analyst, pleaded guilty to
retaining and transmitting top secret national defense information
to people who were not entitled to receive it, before the information then appeared on social media in October 2024.
Aber said at the time that Rahman had "disclosed top secret American documents in violation of his oath, his responsibility, and the law," and his actions had "placed lives at risk, undermined U.S. foreign relations, and compromised our ability to collect vital intelligence in the future."
The Justice Department said in late September that it had, along with the State and Treasury Departments and law enforcement, unsealed an indictment that charged a Russian national, named as Sergey Ivanov, with involvement in "multiple money laundering services that catered to cybercriminals, as well as the seizure of websites associated with three illicit cryptocurrency exchanges."
Another Russian national, Timur Shakhmametov, was charged in the same indictment with conspiracy to commit and aid and abet bank fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit access device fraud, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.
"Every step cybercriminals take in their pursuit of money leaves another track that leads us to their doorstep," Aber said in a statement at the time. "And if you follow them on their path of greed, they will lead us to you. We will not stop, because while domains can always be seized, justice is unyielding."
In November 2024, a Virginia-based company and two of its senior executives, were accused of running "three different schemes to illegally transship sensitive American technology to Russia," including sending equipment to a Russian telecommunications company linked to the Kremlin and Russia's notorious FSB security agency.
"We must not allow critical systems and technologies to be transferred to anyone who may use them against America and our global partners," Aber said. "Guarding against these transfers is imperative, and violations of the laws that protect our national security will be met with ardent prosecution."
In late 2023, Aber was also involved in an indictment against four Russia-affiliated individuals charged with torture, inhuman treatment, and unlawful confinement of a U.S. national in Ukraine after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The accused were named as Suren Seiranovich Mkrtchyan and Dmitry Budnik, along with two individuals identified only by their first names, Valerii and Nazar. "We are proud to be at the forefront of the Justice Department's effort to hold perpetrators of war crimes violations accountable in Ukraine and will continue to pursue them," Aber said.

data.title: Through a Glass Lushly: Michalina Janoszanka's Reverse Paintings (Ca. 1920s)
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952) 是波兰艺术家，以担任画家 Jacek Malczewski 的模特和学生闻名。她不仅作为缪斯出现在众多象征主义画作中，还创作了自己的艺术作品，特别是在玻璃背面绘制的 reverse painting（反向绘画）。她的作品以传统主题如肖像、静物和宗教场景为主，但最具特色的是超现实的风景画，采用宝石色调和金属线条，创造出如梦似幻的效果。虽然 reverse painting 在欧洲被视为民间艺术，但在 20 世纪初，美国艺术家如 Marsden Hartley 和 Rebecca Salsbury James 也开始探索这一技法，推动了现代主义的发展。Janoszanka 的作品在传统与现代之间架起桥梁，提出关于玻璃绘画跨文化影响的未解问题，值得重新评估。

Through a Glass Lushly: Michalina Janoszanka’s Reverse Paintings (ca. 1920s)
Buy as a Print
Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952) is an artist better known for her role on the other side of the canvas, as the muse and mentee of famed Polish painter Jacek Malczewski (1854–1929). She posed for countless symbolist paintings, appearing alone, alongside Malczewski in double-portraits, among satyrs, and as Medusa. However, Janoszanka was more than a muse. She was also
an artist
in her own right. Trained in Kraków and Vienna, she became a strong oil painter. Her themes were traditional: portraits, still lifes, and religious scenes. But what most captured her mentor’s excitement, not to mention the attention of the Young Poland modernist art movement, was something else: the surreal, kaleidoscopic landscapes she painted directly onto glass.
Reverse painting, achieved by building up layers of pigment onto the backside of a pane of glass, has a long history. Having spread as far as China from its birthplace in fifteenth-century Italy, the technique was favored in Eastern Europe for devotional images and icons. These paintings could be produced quickly and cheaply, and “had the added attraction of reflecting the scant light in the dark rooms of the peasant homes”,
writes
scholar Phyllis Granoff. For all their strengths, however, reverse painting was not counted among European fine art. By Janoszanka’s time, the medium was firmly in the realm of folk art.
What Michalina did with reverse painting was entirely distinct from the stiff religious imagery of traditional Polish glass painting. Brilliant gem tones and metallic lines frame her subjects — lush flowers and trees, stylized birds and frogs — in shadowy landscapes. She achieves textures and tones that call to mind other mediums. Dense linework becomes lace-like butterfly wings. In
Winter
, swirled, watercolor blues form a marbled field reminiscent of stained glass. At the birds’ breasts, Janoszanka leaves visible brush strokes, evoking individual feathers.
Butterfly
juxtaposes traditional flower patterns — simplified, geometric — with life-like dry leaves. The result is whimsical and stylized, but not childish. In
Spring
, where Janoszanka sets glowing trees against an exploding coral sky, the effect is plainly psychedelic.
Across the Atlantic, reverse painting’s heyday had come and gone by the early 1900s. By layering not just paint but also crumpled metal foil over glass, American “tinsel painting” had stretched the limits of technique — but the medium, adopted mainly by middle-class women, was viewed as “feminine”. The craft had come to be seen as hackneyed and outdated, a Victorian throwback, and the twentieth century saw many such paintings “cracked and broken and thrown away”,
writes
curator Karli Wurzelbacher. But at that very moment, modernist painters began experimenting with the old technique. Artists like Marsden Hartley (1877–1943) and Rebecca Salsbury James (1891–1968) expanded on the traditional themes (flowers, still life, birds) and pushed reverse painting in novel directions: new color palettes, new approaches to line and space, new abstractions. These American experiments, beginning in the 1910s, coincided with Janoszanka’s work in Poland.
Viewed side by side, the artists’ respective experiments in glass painting could not have been more different. But in Maine, New Mexico, and Kraków, reverse painting presented new possibilities to a generation of modernist artists. There is no telling whether Janoszanka was aware of these other experimenters in avant-garde glass painting. It is also unclear if she faced the same gendered critique: the critic Paul Rosenfeld,
argues
Wurzelbacher, “cast Hartley’s ‘canvases and rectangles of glass’ as effeminate”, comparing them to “some sweet bit of handiwork . . . the design of a sampler, a piece of embroidery.” Though her name remains overshadowed by Malczewski, Janoszanka’s work presents a compelling case for reassessment. Her dreamlike glass paintings are a bridge between folk tradition and modernist experimentation. They raise unanswered questions not just about Janoszanka’s career, but also about modernism’s engagement with glass painting across cultural boundaries. Questions that can be answered, ultimately, only through a return to the archive.

data.title: I want a good parallel computer
data.author: raphlinus
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何GPU尽管在实时图形渲染和机器学习等任务中表现出色，但在其他工作负载中未被广泛应用的原因。主要障碍有两个：一是GPU的执行模型较简单，难以高效处理动态任务；二是编程语言和工具不足，使得并行计算编程更加困难。现代GPU日益复杂，新功能虽有进步但仍不完善。作者通过开发Vello渲染器的经验，指出GPU在处理中间数据结构时存在内存管理问题，无法在有限内存中高效运行。尽管有许多潜在解决方案，但当前硬件存在致命缺陷。作者呼吁设计更简单、更强大的并行计算机，并提到历史上曾有一些有潜力的设计未被广泛应用。文章最后表达了对未来改进的期待和可能性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：并行计算架构及其在现代系统中的应用和限制

不同观点：
• deviantbit 认为现代系统在架构设计上考虑了内存保护、隔离和稳定性，摒弃了过去不稳定和不安全的架构（如Cell处理器）。他批评某些人怀旧但忽略了过去架构的实际问题，强调需要对现代系统有更深的理解和 appreciation。
• grg0 对当前GPU编程模型表示不满，指出其复杂性、缺乏标准化以及与CPU协作的困难。他希望有一种更简化和统一的并行计算架构，而不是现有的GPU模型。
• IshKebab 认为“数百个小CPU在一个芯片上”的架构会失败，因为编程模型过于复杂，未来更可能是GPU增加新功能，而不是全新的架构。
• armchairhacker 讨论了GPU的强大计算能力未被充分利用的问题，但指出并非所有任务都需要GPU的性能，且并行化某些任务可能导致更慢的执行。
• morphle 描述了逆向工程和自定义编译器以释放芯片潜力的实践，展示了通过技术手段突破现有架构限制的可能性。
• dekhn 指出新架构需要广泛的社区支持和应用才能成功，并以Cray MTA为例说明一些优秀项目因缺乏社区支持而失败。
• Animats 认为现代GPU对2D渲染是过度杀伤，并讨论了渲染器在处理复杂场景时的瓶颈问题，指出需要更好的设计来提升GPU利用率。
• bee_rider 对E-cores和Xeon Phis的架构提出改进建议，希望通过增强E-cores的能力来提高并行计算效率。
• ip26 强调GPU的高吞吐量是建立在牺牲动态工作负载处理能力的基础上。
• Retr0id 对统一内存架构下仍需模拟非统一内存模型表示 frustration，希望API能更贴近实际硬件。
• svmhdvn 和 scroot 分别提到GreenArray芯片和uFork项目，展示了对并行计算创新的不同探索。
• api 回顾了在Cell BE上进行进化计算的经历，指出其编程复杂性，并设想了一种多小核CPU的设计。
• Quis_sum 通过CM2的例子，指出现有讨论中对历史并行计算设计的误解，强调其独特的数据并行特性。
• muziq 对Epiphany-V的潜力表示兴趣，但对其未能广泛应用感到失望。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于现有并行计算架构的复杂性、实用性以及未来架构的发展方向。
• 不同评论者对GPU编程模型的优劣、新架构的可行性以及如何更好地利用现有技术资源有不同看法。
• 一些评论者通过实际经验和案例分析，提供了对不同架构的深入见解和批评。
• 讨论还涉及历史并行计算设计的价值和教训，以及这些设计对未来创新的启示。

43440174.article_content:
The GPU in your computer is about 10 to 100 times more powerful than the CPU, depending on workload. For real-time graphics rendering and machine learning, you are enjoying that power, and doing those workloads on a CPU is not viable. Why aren’t we exploiting that power for other workloads? What prevents a GPU from being a more general purpose computer?
I believe there are two main things holding it back. One is an impoverished execution model, which makes certain tasks difficult or impossible to do efficiently; GPUs excel at big blocks of data with predictable shape, such as dense matrix multiplication, but struggle when the workload is dynamic. Second, our languages and tools are inadequate. Programming a parallel computer is just a lot harder.
Modern GPUs are also extremely complex, and getting more so rapidly. New features such as mesh shaders and work graphs are two steps forward one step back; for each new capability there is a basic task that isn’t fully supported.
I believe a simpler, more powerful parallel computer is possible, and that there are signs in the historical record. In a slightly alternate universe, we would have those computers now, and be doing the work of designing algorithms and writing programs to run well on them, for a very broad range of tasks.
Last April, I gave a
colloquium
(video) at the UCSC CSE program with the same title. This blog is a companion to that.
Memory efficiency of sophisticated GPU programs
I’ve been working on
Vello
, an advanced 2D vector graphics renderer, for many years. The CPU uploads a scene description in a simplified binary SVG-like format, then the compute shaders take care of the rest, producing a 2D rendered image at the end. The compute shaders
parse
tree structures, do advanced computational geometry for
stroke expansion
, and sorting-like algorithms for binning. Internally, it’s essentially a simple compiler, producing a separate optimized byte-code like program for each 16x16 pixel tile, then interpreting those programs. What it cannot do, a problem I am increasingly frustrated by, is run in bounded memory. Each stage produces intermediate data structures, and the number and size of these structures depends on the input in an unpredictable way. For example, changing a single transform in the encoded scene can result in profoundly different rendering plans.
The problem is that the buffers for the intermediate results need to be allocated (under CPU control) before kicking off the pipeline. There are a number of imperfect potential solutions. We could estimate memory requirements on the CPU before starting a render, but that’s expensive and may not be precise, resulting either in failure or waste. We could try a render, detect failure, and retry if buffers were exceeded, but doing readback from GPU to CPU is a big performance problem, and creates a significant architectural burden on other engines we’d interface with.
The details of the specific problem are interesting but beyond the scope of this blog post. The interested reader is directed to the
Potato
design document, which explores the question of how far you can get doing scheduling on CPU, respecting bounded GPU resources, while using the GPU for actual pixel wrangling. It also touches on several more recent extensions to the standard GPU execution model, all of which are complex and non-portable, and none of which quite seem to solve the problem.
Fundamentally, it shouldn’t be necessary to allocate large buffers to store intermediate results. Since they will be consumed by downstream stages, it’s far more efficient to put them in queues, sized large enough to keep enough items in flight to exploit available parallelism. Many GPU operations internally work as queues (the standard vertex shader / fragment shader / rasterop pipeline being the classic example), so it’s a question of exposing that underlying functionality to applications. The
GRAMPS
paper from 2009 suggests this direction, as did the
Brook
project, a predecessor to CUDA.
There are a lot of potential solutions to running Vello-like algorithms in bounded memory; most have a fatal flaw on hardware today. It’s interesting to speculate about changes that would unlock the capability. It’s worth emphasizing, I’m not feeling held back by the amount of parallelism I can exploit, as my approach of breaking the problem into variants of prefix sum easily scales to hundreds of thousands of threads. Rather, it’s the inability to organize the overall as stages operating in parallel, connected through queues tuned to use only the amount of buffer memory needed to keep everything smoothly, as opposed to the compute shader execution model of large dispatches separated by pipeline barriers.
Parallel computers of the past

• morphle 描述了逆向工程和自定义编译器以释放芯片潜力的实践，展示了通过技术手段突破现有架构限制的可能性。
• dekhn 指出新架构需要广泛的社区支持和应用才能成功，并以Cray MTA为例说明一些优秀项目因缺乏社区支持而失败。
• Animats 认为现代GPU对2D渲染是过度杀伤，并讨论了渲染器在处理复杂场景时的瓶颈问题，指出需要更好的设计来提升GPU利用率。
• bee_rider 对E-cores和Xeon Phis的架构提出改进建议，希望通过增强E-cores的能力来提高并行计算效率。
• ip26 强调GPU的高吞吐量是建立在牺牲动态工作负载处理能力的基础上。
• Retr0id 对统一内存架构下仍需模拟非统一内存模型表示 frustration，希望API能更贴近实际硬件。
• svmhdvn 和 scroot 分别提到GreenArray芯片和uFork项目，展示了对并行计算创新的不同探索。
• api 回顾了在Cell BE上进行进化计算的经历，指出其编程复杂性，并设想了一种多小核CPU的设计。
• Quis_sum 通过CM2的例子，指出现有讨论中对历史并行计算设计的误解，强调其独特的数据并行特性。
• muziq 对Epiphany-V的潜力表示兴趣，但对其未能广泛应用感到失望。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于现有并行计算架构的复杂性、实用性以及未来架构的发展方向。
• 不同评论者对GPU编程模型的优劣、新架构的可行性以及如何更好地利用现有技术资源有不同看法。
• 一些评论者通过实际经验和案例分析，提供了对不同架构的深入见解和批评。
• 讨论还涉及历史并行计算设计的价值和教训，以及这些设计对未来创新的启示。

data.title: Osgint – OSINT tool to find information about GitHub user
data.author: CHEF-KOCH
data.article_summary: OSGINT是一个开源工具，用于查找GitHub用户的各类信息。其主要功能包括：通过电子邮件查找GitHub用户名，通过用户名查找关联电子邮件（但并非每次都有效），以及获取用户资料信息（如账户创建日期、公开Gists、ID、公开PGP和SSH等）。该工具通过分析公开提交记录和GPG密钥来获取电子邮件信息，并利用GitHub的用户API进行数据检索。用户可以通过命令行指定用户名或电子邮件进行查询，并可以选择以JSON格式输出结果。工具还提供了示例输出，展示了查询结果的详细信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub信息公开的影响与隐私问题

不同观点：
• zellyn: 指出个人资料中的邮箱信息可能因他人贡献而混淆，强调了邮箱准确性的问题。
• theyknowitsxmas: 质疑公开此类信息对非垃圾邮件发送者的好处，暗示可能主要有利于垃圾邮件发送者。
• cdblades: 认为有道德责任在项目文档中说明如何避免信息泄露，关注信息保护的责任。
• 1317: 认为公开的信息并无新意，因为大多可在GitHub个人资料页找到。
• ExxKA: 提到招聘人员通过GitHub发送垃圾邮件的现象，表达对隐私被侵犯的不满。
• cpursley: 提到https://reporeach.com作为一个类似概念，暗示此类信息公开可能有特定用途。
• areyourllySorry: 提到gitrecon工具，可能与信息收集相关，增加对隐私风险的关注。
• Dotnaught: 认为通过附加.patch到提交来获取信息可能更简单，质疑当前方法的复杂性。
• belter: 质疑在GitHub上使用真实姓名的做法，并通过知名人物的例子（如elonmusk, donaldtrump）强调潜在风险。

补充讨论：
- 评论中对信息公开的必要性和潜在风险存在争议，尤其是关于垃圾邮件和隐私侵犯的问题。
- 提出了如何避免信息泄露的责任问题，以及对工具和方法的提及，显示出对技术解决方案的关注。

data.title: The earliest versions of the first C compiler known to exist
data.author: diginova
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了由已故传奇人物dmr（Dennis M. Ritchie）编写的最早期的C语言编译器，这些编译器代码如今无法使用现代编译器如gcc进行编译。发布者仅为分享和缅怀这个点燃了万亿美金产业的火花。如果有人想尝试构建这个编译器，可以使用Aiju的PDP-11/Unix模拟器。同时提供了相关链接和资源，包括PDP-11模拟器和Research Unix资源库。代码主要由C语言（83.1%）和汇编语言（16.9%）编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言的历史、特性及其早期使用情况

不同观点：
• [tanelpoder] 认为Oracle数据库最早版本用汇编编写，后来为了跨平台用C重写，甚至为了在大型机上使用，开发了C编译器。这表明C语言早期在跨平台开发中的重要性。
• [ricardo81] 强调程序员应保持谦逊，现代编程建立在过去80多年的计算机科学基础上，特别是抽象机制。虽然现代程序员讨论内存安全，但过去有人已经处理了这些问题。
• [90s_dev] 认为C语言看似简单，但实际上有很多细微差别，并询问是否有其他低级语言能真正做到简单。他对Zig语言有兴趣，但也有保留意见。

补充讨论：
• [bluetomcat] 对代码中"extern"和"auto"的使用感到有趣，并指出与现代C语言的区别，尤其是全局符号的作用和数组声明的不同。
• [deweywsu] 对第一个C编译器是用C编写感到困惑，并寻求确认。
• [diginova] 提供了关于编译器自举（bootstrapping）的参考资料，解释了如何用同一种语言编写编译器。
• [tempodox] 对PDP-11上不区分`char`和`int`感到惊讶，反映了早期硬件的特性。
• [Joker_vD] 提到代码并非单次编译器，可能是对某些假设的反驳。
• [ModernMech] 认为第一个C编译器是用B语言编写的，提出了早期编译器发展的另一种视角。

争议焦点：
• 第一个C编译器的编写语言存在不同看法，[deweywsu]和[ModernMech]提出了不同见解。
• [90s_dev]对Zig语言的简单性表示怀疑，但未详细展开。

其他重要论据和例子：
• [smackay] 和 [ZhiqiangWang] 提到了关于C语言历史的具体时间点和Ken Thompson的相关内容，补充了讨论的历史背景。
• [ramon156] 和 [dark-star] 分享了对代码注释和特定函数的幽默看法，反映了程序员文化中的轻松一面。

data.title: Japanese scientists use stem cell treatment to restore movement in spinal injury
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 日本科学家通过使用诱导多能干细胞（iPS细胞）治疗脊髓损伤患者，取得初步成效。在Keio大学的研究中，四名患者中的两名在接受超过200万个iPS衍生神经细胞植入后，运动功能评分有所改善。其中一名老年男性患者已能站立并不借助支撑开始练习行走。研究主要目标是验证该疗法安全性，未观察到严重副作用。该研究获政府批准于2019年开始，首例手术在2022年进行。研究团队计划推进临床试验，以期将该疗法广泛应用于患者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： stem细胞治疗的现实性、有效性及应用现状

不同观点：
• [质疑 stem细胞治疗的现实性和可信度] hash872对stem细胞治疗的真实性表示怀疑，尤其是对一些宣传stem细胞疗法的网站和跨国治疗的合法性感到不信任。他提到自己有肩部损伤，并询问stem细胞注射是否真的有效，特别是提到很多运动员去国外接受治疗。他还批评了FDA的审批速度，并表达了对这些疗法是否接近现实的困惑。

• [提供新闻来源补充信息] pseudolus提供了NHK的新闻链接，暗示有些主流媒体也报道了stem细胞相关的新闻，但没有明确表态是否完全相信这些疗法的效果。

• [关心治疗成本和适用条件] Forbo提到自己有亲属因脊髓损伤瘫痪，对stem细胞治疗表示兴趣，并询问其成本。他在后续编辑中指出，这种治疗可能只适用于“14-28天以内”的近期损伤，暗示了这种疗法在时间上的限制。

• [指出治疗历史和先例] stared提到stem细胞手术并非新事物，并提供了2014年在波兰进行的首次成功手术的BBC新闻链接，暗示stem细胞治疗有一定的历史和成功案例。

• [提供研究机构信息] lambdaone提供了涉及stem细胞研究的日本庆应大学研究小组的链接，指向具体的科学研究，显示出对stem细胞科学进展的关注。

• [对脊髓治疗持怀疑态度] mort96幽默但略带讽刺地表示，病人可能不希望自己的脊髓损伤“开始移动”，暗示对stem细胞治疗脊髓损伤的安全性和效果持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• stem细胞治疗的跨国合法性及监管差异：评论中多次提到运动员去国外（如德国、泰国、墨西哥）接受stem细胞治疗，暗示这些疗法在某些国家可能不受严格监管。

• 治疗的时间窗口限制：Forbo提到stem细胞治疗脊髓损伤需要在“14-28天以内”进行，显示出这种疗法在时间上的局限性。

争议焦点：
• stem细胞治疗的科学现实性和可信度是主要争议点。部分评论者对其持怀疑态度，而其他人则提供了支持其可行性的案例和研究链接。

March 22, 2025
The GIST
Editors' notes

and

Japanese scientists use stem cell treatment to restore movement in spinal injury patients
Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain
A stem cell treatment helped improve the motor function of two out of four patients with a spinal cord injury in the first clinical study of its kind, Japanese scientists said.
There is currently no effective
treatment
for paralysis caused by serious spinal cord injuries, which affect more than 150,000 patients in Japan alone, with 5,000 new cases each year.
Researchers at Tokyo's Keio University are conducting their study using
induced pluripotent stem cells
(iPS)—created by stimulating mature, already specialized, cells back into a juvenile state.
They can then be prompted to mature into different kinds of cells, with the Keio researchers using iPS-derived cells of the neural stem.
The university said on Friday that the
motor function
score for two patients improved after an operation to implant more than two million iPS-derived cells into a spinal cord.
No serious adverse event was observed for all four cases after a year of monitoring, the university said.
The research's main goal was to study the safety of injecting the cells.
Public broadcaster NHK reported that one of the two was an elderly man who suffered the
injury
in an accident.
He is now able to stand without support and has started practicing walking, NHK said.
"We were able to achieve results in the world's first
spinal cord
treatment with iPS," Hideyuki Okano, a Keio professor who heads the research, said, according to NHK.
Okano said the team hoped to move to a clinical trial that would be a step towards bringing the treatment to patients.
The university received
government approval
for their initial study in 2019 and they carried out the first operation in 2022.
Details of the patients remain confidential, but the team is focusing on people who were injured 14-28 days before the operation.
The number of cells implanted was determined after safety experiments in animals.

data.title: Taming Servers for Fun and Profit
data.author: dban
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在构建自有云基础设施时，如何将硬件设备与其在操作系统中的表示进行映射和管理。作者描述了从物理硬件安装到操作系统识别的过程，强调了设备命名不稳定性带来的挑战，特别是存储设备的命名。为解决此问题，他们采用Redfish API来枚举硬件信息，并通过gRPC和内部控制平面MetalCP进行设备管理。具体流程包括：创建设备标识CSV，通过Temporal工作流导入主机，连接数据中心管理网络，获取BMC和NIC的MAC地址，创建静态DHCP租约，并更新数据库记录。最终，生成包含网络接口卡、NVMe驱动器等详细信息的稳定硬件配置，确保设备命名的一致性和可靠性。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43427595.article_content:
Charith Amarasinghe
Mar 21, 2025
We’ve all gotten used to clicking a button and getting a Linux machine running in the cloud. But when you’re building your own cloud, you’ve got to build the button first.
Lately we’ve been
writing
about building out our
Metal infrastructure
one rack at a time.
In our
last blog
, we spoke about the trials of building out the physical infrastructure. In this episode, we talk about how we operationalize the hardware once it’s installed.
Sorting your LEGO pieces
You’ve built your dream server with dual-redundant NICs and multiple redundant NVMe drives for resilience. You’ve ordered 100 units and got them all racked up and wired to your detailed diagrams. You go to the DC with your USB stick and reboot into your favorite Linux distro’s installer only to be greeted by the “Choose your Network Interface” screen with a dozen or so incomprehensible interface names.
Herein lies our first hurdle — how do you map the physical arrangement of hardware to what your operating system sees?
A Supermicro server with 12 NVMe Bays - Guess which bay is /dev/nvme0n2 as seen by Linux? (That’s a trick question).
💡
When buying build-to-order servers, it’s essential to include instructions specifying exactly where each Network Card or NVMe Drive should get installed. Otherwise you might end up with multiple different configurations across different orders.
It helps first to take a step back and discuss how Linux names devices.
When a host boots Linux, the OS enumerates the attached hardware. Most commonly, devices are attached to the PCIe bus and Linux begins enumerating these according to the hierarchical structure of the bus. When Linux encounters a device during this traversal, the
udev
daemon will get an event and associate a number of identifiers with the device - it’ll then use these identifiers to formulate a name which it then assigns to the device nodes it creates in
/dev
and elsewhere.
The consequence of this approach is that device names can be very unstable, especially if the hardware layout changes between boots or if the enumeration order is non-deterministic. If you used Linux in the olden days, you’d know the pain of plugging in a new PCIe card and booting only to figure out that your networking broke. Despite the many critiques that could be leveled against SystemD, it does succeed in
addressing these problems for network interfaces since v197
. But storage device naming is still a crapshoot and better achieved by device serial number.
Our approach to addressing this unpredictability is to lean on Redfish - a HTTP API for Board Management Controllers (BMCs) attached to server motherboards. Redfish APIs can enumerate the hardware on a board, detailing PCIe cards, NVMe drives, their serial numbers and/or MAC addresses and their physical locations.
An Extract of a Redfish System object scraped from one of our storage nodes
Our very first step once a rack is installed is to build a CSV of identifiers for the equipment in the rack - hostname, BMC MAC address, BMC password, and a few other details. We then push this data via gRPC to an internal control plane called MetalCP.
MetalCP runs a Temporal worker which implements a Host Import workflow. For each server, we then kick off a workflow that runs through the following steps:
Match the device to its representation in our internal DCIM tool (Railyard)
Connect to the datacenter's management network via Tailscale
Connect to the management router at the datacenter and identify the DHCP lease assigned to the BMC (via its MAC)
Connect to the BMC of the server via this IP and scrape all available data
Create an internal Protobuf representation of the hardware layout
Create static DHCP leases for the BMC and for the management NIC on the host using discovered MAC addresses from the scrape
Update a DB with all the details about the server
An import workflow takes less that a minute to complete in most cases and Temporal ensures recovery from any transient failures.
The timeline of a Host Import workflow
The database record that is stored by a host workflow contains all the information you could want about a server. We generate:
A list of Network Interface Cards, their Physical Location (Slot), and MAC addresses for each Port
A list of NVMe Drives, their Serial Numbers, Model Numbers, and Physical Slot IDs
System stats such as CPU core counts, RAM size, and hardware identifiers
We then match this hardware specification against a list of known configurations. These configurations encode details such as network interface names assigned to specific PCIe slots and NVMe drive bay identifiers. A hardware configuration is as simple as a set of conditionals in Golang that match the key distinguishing factors of a specific type of server, and a config object containing stable interface and drive names.
An example hardware identification function, pb.SystemInfo is an encoding of raw data we’ve scraped from Redfish
A custom plugin exposes this Hardware Config

data.title: HP avoids monetary damages over bricked printers in class-action settlement
data.author: JSR_FDED
data.article_summary:
美国加州北区地方法院批准了惠普与客户之间的和解协议。客户起诉惠普通过固件更新阻止打印机使用非惠普墨盒和碳粉。2020年12月，Mobile Emergency Housing Corp.和Performance Automotive & Tire Center对惠普提起集体诉讼，指控其通过未经授权的固件更新锁定竞争对手的墨盒。诉讼要求法院裁定惠普行为违法，并寻求禁令和赔偿。

惠普称此措施为“动态安全”，但安全专家认为没有必要。2024年8月，双方达成和解，惠普不承认任何不当行为，也不支付赔偿金，但同意支付共计15,000美元给三原告，并支付725,000美元律师费。

和解要求惠普对特定型号打印机用户披露动态安全和数据收集信息，并允许用户选择是否安装包含动态安全功能的固件更新。这些型号包括多款彩色和黑白激光打印机。然而，并非所有受动态安全影响的打印机都在此列。惠普还在产品页面添加了相关说明，提示打印机仅适用于带有惠普芯片的墨盒。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HP通过动态安全更新和强制更新限制用户使用第三方墨盒的争议，以及消费者在寻求法律正义时面临的困难。

不同观点：
• [autoexec] 和 [unyttigfjelltol] 认为此次集体诉讼的“胜利”毫无意义，因为HP无需对伤害用户的行为负责，也无需承认错误，还能继续通过非动态安全名义的更新限制打印机功能。他们指出，企业通过这种手段继续进行对用户不友好的行为，因为罚款和诉讼远不及其通过不当行为获得的利润。

• [ourmandave] 指出好的一面，即某些型号的打印机现在可以选择拒绝包含动态安全功能的固件升级。然而，他们也认为HP基本上逃脱了惩罚，因为这些披露和选项对普通用户来说远远不够。

• [jqpabc123] 提出消费者应通过抵制购买HP打印机来回应，这是对企业不当行为的直接解决方案。

• [talkingtab] 和 [mg794613] 批评当前法律体系对大企业的偏袒，认为企业可以通过支付高额律师费逃避责任，而普通公民却难以获得正义。他们将此视为企业控制立法和司法系统的证据。

• [crazygringo] 对文章中使用"bricked"一词提出质疑，认为打印机只是功能受限，而非彻底无法使用。他们还对法律上未退还用户功能损失的费用表示困惑，怀疑其中有技术性细节。

• [Cthulhu_] 呼吁立法全面禁止如厂商锁定和昂贵耗材等不良商业行为，认为这是更广泛的消费者权益问题。

补充讨论：

A United States District Court for the Northern District of California judge has signed off on a settlement agreement between HP and its customers, who sued the company for issuing firmware updates that prevented their printers from working with non-HP ink and toner.
In December 2020, Mobile Emergency Housing Corp. and a company called Performance Automotive & Tire Center filed a class-action complaint against HP [
PDF
], alleging that the company “wrongfully compels users of its printers to buy and use only HP ink and toner supplies by transmitting firmware updates without authorization to HP printers over the Internet that lock out its competitors’ ink and toner supply cartridges.” The complaint centered on a firmware update issued in November 2020; it sought a court ruling that HP’s actions broke the law, an injunction against the firmware updates, and monetary and punitive damages.
“HP’s firmware ‘updates’ act as malware—adding, deleting or altering code, diminishing the capabilities of HP printers, and rendering the competitors’ supply cartridges incompatible with HP printers,” the 2020 complaint reads.
HP calls using updates to prevent printers from using third-party ink and toner Dynamic Security. The term aims to brand the device bricking as a security measure. In recent years, HP has continued pushing this claim, despite security experts that Ars has spoken with agreeing that there’s virtually zero reason for printer users to worry about
getting hacked through ink
.
After years of litigation, in August 2024, HP and the plaintiffs reached a settlement agreement that Judge Susan Van Keulen approved on Tuesday [
PDF
].
Under the settlement agreement, HP doesn’t admit to any wrongdoing. It also won’t pay any monetary relief to customers impacted by the November 2020 firmware update.
However, HP agreed to pay $5,000 each to Mobile Emergency Housing Corp., Performance Automotive & Tire Center, and David Justin Lynch, who was eventually added to the complaint, “to compensate them for the services they performed on behalf of the classes,”
HP said
. It will also pay $725,000 in attorneys’ fees and expenses.
A win for HP users comes from the company's legal commitment to allow users of specific printers to decline firmware updates that would push Dynamic Security. The now-approved settlement terms state:
… HP has agreed to continue making certain disclosures to users of Class Printers about Dynamic Security and data collection, and to continue to allow users of Class Printers to either agree to install or decline to install firmware updates that include Dynamic Security features. The disclosures that HP has agreed to continue making include the disclosure that HP collects printer cartridge data from Class Printers through the HP Smart App, and that HP’s Dynamic Security measures are designed to block cartridges using a non-HP chip, and may be delivered to printers through periodic firmware updates.
That requirement, however, only applies to specific HP printer models (referred to as “Class Printers”), which are listed below:

HP Color LaserJet Pro MFP M479FDN

HP LaserJet Pro M404N

HP LaserJet Pro M404DW
HP Color LaserJet Pro M454DN
HP Color LaserJet Pro M454DW
HP LaserJet Pro MFP M428DW

HP LaserJet Pro MFP M428FDW
Those printers were all impacted by the November 2020 firmware update that sparked the lawsuit. However, there are numerous HP printers subject to Dynamic Security that are absent from that list. After being
criticized
and sued multiple times for abruptly issuing Dynamic Security restrictions to already-purchased printers in 2016, HP has informed users that only
specific printer models
made before December 1, 2016, can remove Dynamic Security.
HP also now provides disclaimers on the product pages for most of the printers that it sells, stating that the device “is intended to work only with cartridges that have a new or reused HP chip” and uses Dynamic Security “to block cartridges using a non-HP chip.”

美国加州北区地方法院批准了惠普与客户之间的和解协议。客户起诉惠普通过固件更新阻止打印机使用非惠普墨盒和碳粉。2020年12月，Mobile Emergency Housing Corp.和Performance Automotive & Tire Center对惠普提起集体诉讼，指控其通过未经授权的固件更新锁定竞争对手的墨盒。诉讼要求法院裁定惠普行为违法，并寻求禁令和赔偿。

惠普称此措施为“动态安全”，但安全专家认为没有必要。2024年8月，双方达成和解，惠普不承认任何不当行为，也不支付赔偿金，但同意支付共计15,000美元给三原告，并支付725,000美元律师费。

和解要求惠普对特定型号打印机用户披露动态安全和数据收集信息，并允许用户选择是否安装包含动态安全功能的固件更新。这些型号包括多款彩色和黑白激光打印机。然而，并非所有受动态安全影响的打印机都在此列。惠普还在产品页面添加了相关说明，提示打印机仅适用于带有惠普芯片的墨盒。

data.title: Autology: A Lisp with access to its own interpreter
data.author: simonpure
data.article_summary: Autology是一个用Clojure编写的函数式Lisp语言，其特点是能够访问和修改自身的解释器。通过将解释器功能绑定到一个特殊变量`*i*`，程序可以在运行时动态地改变语言的行为和语法。与通常在编译时使用的宏不同，Autology允许在运行时进行语法重写和功能扩展。例如，可以添加函数定义、改变求值顺序或实现 continuation passing style 等。尽管Autology并非实用语言（因其速度慢且资源消耗高），但它是一个探索Lisp元编程的有趣实验工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp及其相关语言的内部结构和解释器的可访问性、可修改性及其在其他编程语言中的潜在应用和优势

不同观点：
• jlarocco认为，Common Lisp的编译器或解释器通常具有与内部结构交互的包（如SBCL中的`sb-c`、`sb-vm`等），这种能力允许开发者检查和修改编译器的内部数据结构和操作，甚至可以生成SBCL不直接支持的汇编代码。这种特性非常方便，并希望其他语言也能采用。
• abeppu提到Nada Amin和Tiark Rompf的研究，关于“解释器塔”的研究工作，通过显式的分阶段操作，可以去除元循环解释器的开销。这与jlarocco提到的Lisp特性有类似之处。
• bandrami指出，访问解释器、扫描器、解析器和编译器是Lisp的本质特征，而不仅仅是使用大量括号的语言。
• sargstuff讨论了Lisp在运行时生成嵌入式虚拟机的能力，并将其与系统调用fork和并发支持进行比较，同时幽默地提到了一些与品牌名称混淆的问题。
• Cieric分享了他尝试创建一种能够修改自身语法的语言的经验，并指出Lisp适合这种需求，但他未能解决如何修改解释器的AST。
• bsima推荐了Shen语言，认为喜欢这种特性的人可能会对Shen感兴趣。
• ape4提到，由于Clojure运行在JVM上，是否也可以引入*jvm*变量。
• shadowgovt指出，Racket能够声明在文件级别应用的DSL，但jlarocco提到的特性更为精细。
• souenzzo赞赏Clojure仅用1kloc代码就能探索大量想法的能力。
• JoelMcCracken认为这有点像Kernel编程语言。
• johnisgood对“跨语言”示例表示兴趣，并询问其用例和目的。
• lifthrasiir提到CosmicOS有类似的想法，能够无缝引入特殊形式而不预先定义隐式解释器。
• timonoko感叹用语言本身编写更好的语言的强大，并反思在汇编上浪费的时间以及时间旅行的一些限制。
• behnamoh认为这是热代码重载的增强版，并提到他正在开发的类似Lisp的语言中允许重新定义任何符号，甚至数字，同时好奇这种极端灵活性的用例。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个相关语言和工具，如SBCL、Clojure、Racket、Shen、Kernel编程语言和CosmicOS，显示出对这些语言内部机制和特性的广泛兴趣。
• 争议的焦点可能在于Lisp这种高度灵活和自省的特性的实际应用价值和用例，部分评论者如johnisgood和behnamoh对此表示好奇和质疑。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，讨论中多次提到解释器和编译器的可访问性和可修改性带来的便利和潜力，以及是否希望其他语言也能具备这些特性。
