Autology
A hot take on Lisp metaprogramming,
Autology
is a Lisp with access
to its own interpreter.
What is it?
Autology is a functional interpreted Lisp language, written in Clojure.
The Autology interpreter function is defined as a data structure which is available to the Autology program, it is bound to the variable
*i*
.
Whenever an expression needs to be evaluated, Autology will retrieve the current value of
*i*
from the current lexically scoped execution environment and use it to evaluate the expression.
By binding new values of
*i*
we can modify the behaviour of the Autology language while our program is running.
Why have you done this?
Mainly for fun and to explore a neat idea.
Autology is not a particularly useful language as-is, its very slow and resource intensive.
Macros are the normal tool for Lisp languages to modify their syntax or behaviour, but these are normally only available at compile time. Autology allows dynamic rewriting of the language at runtime.
Even other non-Lisp languages are able to define some form of Domain Specific Language to allow programmers to express problems more clearly, however these are generally quite restrictive in scope. Autology allows full ad-hoc re-writing of the syntax of the language, as well as defining new features or removing existing ones.
What can you do with it?
Well to start with you might like to add functions to the language. Autology doesn't have them by default, but we can rebind the
*i*
symbol to a data structure representing a new interpreter function, one that does have functions.
(
bind
(
;;
grab a copy of the `:atl/eval-list` section of the
;
; interpreter which is responsible for evaluating lists.
original (
get-marker
*i*
:atl/eval-list
)
;
; define a case test+body for use when the list expression
;
; starts with our function special form, in this case `λ`.
λ-form (
qu
(
λ
(
let
[[_λ params body] e]
(
fn
[& values]
(
autology.core/evaluate
body
(
reduce
(
fn
[acc-env [s v]]
(
assoc
acc-env s v))
env
(
zipmap
params values)))))))
;
; rebind `*i*` to be a new interpreter with the
;
; `:atl/eval-list` section replaced with a version that
;
; includes our lambda handling special form.
*i* (
replace-marker
*i*
:atl/eval-list
(
list
:atl/eval-list
(
concat
(
butlast
original)
λ-form
(
list
(
last
original)))))
;
; We can now immediately define functions since the
;
; interpreter will have already been updated to evaluate the
;
; remaining bindings like this one.
double (
λ
(
n
)
(
+
n n)))
;
; Finally we can invoke our new function!
(
double
(
double
(
double
(
double
(
double
1.3125
))))))
After that, pretty much anything you want!
Why not switch form applicative order evaluation to normal order evaluation?
Maybe modify the language so it uses a continuation passing style?
Define a metacircular Lisp inside your program which has access to it's own interpreter as well at the Autology interpreter.
Run tests
clojure -X:test

data.title: Show HN: I Got Tired of Looking Up Words While Reading, So I Built This
data.author: yw2365
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了名为Wordship的Chrome扩展工具，它不仅提供选定文本的字面翻译，还通过结合上下文给出更准确的释义，帮助用户更好地理解语言的实际用法。该工具解决了传统词典仅提供字面定义、忽略语境的问题，使用户不再对翻译感到困惑。文章还列举了其他类似翻译工具及其功能和用户评价，强调这些工具大多依赖Google翻译提供服务。同时，文章提醒用户这些评价未经过Google验证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[提高在线阅读中的词汇学习效率]

不同观点：
• 观点一：有类似困扰并期待解决方案  
   ⁃ 用户[yw2365]提到自己在在线阅读时经常遇到不认识的单词，通过Google查询后仍然容易忘记，导致阅读变得枯燥乏味。为解决这一问题，他开发了一个Chrome扩展工具，可以帮助用户快速翻译或定义单词，并结合例句保存，方便后续复习。该工具通过自动生成对话示例来帮助巩固学习，提升了词汇学习的效率。

• 观点二：对工具的功能和效果感兴趣，希望了解更多  
   ⁃ 用户[yw2365]在评论中提到自己已经通过该工具改善了词汇学习体验，并提供了一个演示视频链接，供其他有相同困扰的人查看工具的具体功能。他邀请有相同困扰的人分享他们的看法或建议工具的未来改进方向。

补充讨论：
• 工具的具体功能包括：  
   ⁃ 高亮不认识的单词

data.title: Ask HN: Do programmers generally enjoy some amount of complexity?
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的复杂性与简化之争，以及开发者对复杂性与简化问题的不同态度和处理方式。

不同观点：
• [finnthehuman] 认为，了解开发者的个人偏好（如喜欢玩Factorio）对实际开发没有太多实用价值。他批评了将软件缺陷归咎于开发者个人特质的倾向，认为这是忽视了其他更重要的因素，如业务需求和交付压力。
• [austin-cheney] 提出，高智商和高责任心（conscientiousness）的结合决定了开发者能否将复杂问题简化为简单解决方案。他指出，责任心与智商呈负相关，责任心强但智商较低的人有时能提供高质量交付。
• [halper] 强调了自己对简化的执着，宁愿长时间思考和重写代码以避免复杂性。虽然这种做法可能降低短期生产力，但最终结果是可靠的代码。
• [mathw] 认为简化复杂问题非常困难，且多数企业的工作方式阻碍了这种简化。他还指出，技术债务和工具选择受限等问题使得开发者不得不面对复杂性。
• [9dev] 主张复杂性是恒定的，只能在系统中移动或隐藏。开发者的乐趣在于将复杂性分割并整理，而不是完全避免复杂性。
• [tacostakohashi] 认为复杂性往往源于决策拖延和设计上的妥协，而不是开发者的偏好。他批评了通过增加配置选项和重试机制来掩盖问题的方式。
• [TrackerFF] 喜欢简单、易于排查的系统，倾向于使用经过实战检验的解决方案，而不是新颖但不可靠的技术。
• [maltalex] 指出简化需要大量努力，且开发者喜欢优化系统，但这种优化有时会增加不必要的复杂性。
• [bayindirh] 支持“尽可能简单，必要时复杂”的理念，强调代码的可靠性和速度。
• [matt_s] 认为有些开发者可能因为天性或竞争心态而过度复杂化解决方案。
• [dooglius] 区分了“必要的复杂性”和“无谓的复杂性”，欣赏前者而厌恶后者。
• [FrankWilhoit] 认为开发者享受的是管理复杂性，而不是复杂性本身，且每个人对“复杂”和“简化”的理解不同。
• [achairapart] 将问题解决者分为两类：一类倾向于用复杂方案解决复杂问题，另一类则试图通过简化问题来解决复杂问题。他指出工程师通常属于前者，而设计师（尤其是UX设计师）则属于后者。
• [bakuninsbart] 喜欢研究遗留系统和设计决策，但在时间压力下这种工作变得不那么有趣。
• [wruza] 认为复杂性往往源于对代码运行环境的有限信息，开发者通过增加防御性代码来避免失败，特别是在时间紧迫和责任重大的情况下。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于开发者对复杂性的态度：一些人认为复杂性是可管理且必要的，而另一些人则极力避免复杂性，追求简化和可靠性。
- 另一个讨论要点是环境和工具对开发者选择的影响，包括技术债务、工具限制和交付压力。
- 责任心和智商的关系被提出作为一个影响开发者处理复杂性的因素。
- 开发者在面对遗留系统和时间压力时的不同反应也是一个讨论点。

data.title: The Wright brothers invented the airplane, right? Not if you're in Brazil
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：谁发明了飞机以及发明贡献的归属问题

不同观点：
• aleph_minus_one 认为Hans Grade使飞机变得实用，并提到Otto Lilienthal发明了滑翔机，为重于空气的飞行器奠定了基础。
• adev_ 强调发明先后不重要，认为Santos Dumont的成就也很显著，尤其是其设计的尾翼配置对现代商用飞机的影响。
• idoubtit 认为“谁发明了某物”的问题通常没有意义，因为发明往往是集体努力的成果， aviation技术即使没有Wright兄弟和Santos Dumont，也会由其他人完成。
• upofadown 指出Wright兄弟的主要贡献是翼翘曲控制，但其专利导致了法律纠纷，可能延缓了相关技术的发展。
• conartist6 提到Lilienthal的贡献被忽视，而Wright兄弟也曾借鉴过他的工作。
• aap_ 作为德国人，表示在其文化中Otto Lilienthal被视为飞机的发明者。

补充讨论：
• s_dev 通过Enigma破解的例子说明重大任务通常由多人共同完成。
• newsuser 提到在乌克兰，Ivan Puluj而非Röntgen被认为是X射线的发明者。
• fermigier 指出在法国，Clément Ader被认为实现了首次动力飞行。
• throw0101c 和Beijinger 提供了有关首次飞行声明的维基百科链接。
• weeksie 提到新西兰也有自己的“飞机发明者”Richard Pearse。
• arnaudsm 认为类似飞机和互联网这类重大发明的归属问题往往受到民族主义和伟人理论的影响，而忽视了科学的国际性和集体性。

争议焦点：
• 不同国家和文化对飞机发明者的认定存在争议，讨论中提到了德国、法国、巴西等国的贡献。
• Wright兄弟的专利及其对技术发展的影响存在争议，部分评论认为其法律纠纷可能阻碍了技术进步。

不同观点：
• [danirod] 认为YouTube最近向喜欢Tom Scott视频的观众推荐了一个新兴频道，由一位叫Chris Spargo的创作者制作。他指出，Chris Spargo的视频风格与Tom Scott非常相似，包括视频长度、解释概念或讲述历史的形式，以及在不同地点拍摄的特点。这表明Chris Spargo可能是在模仿Tom Scott的风格。

• [HelloUsername] 并没有直接回应danirod对Chris Spargo视频的评价，而是对视频中的具体内容提出问题，特别关注视频中提到的一个位于俄罗斯的场地，并附上了相关视频链接。这显示出对视频具体地理位置的兴趣和好奇。

• [tetris11] 表达了对Tom Scott视频的喜爱，但提到自己入坑较晚，因此看到Tom Scott谈论自己去过的地方时会感到一种诡异的感觉。这显示出对视频内容与个人经历重合的个人化体验。

• [HelloUsername] 并没有直接回应danirod对Chris Spargo视频的评价，而是对视频中的具体内容提出问题，特别关注视频中提到的一个位于俄罗斯的场地，并附上了相关视频链接。这显示出对视频具体地理位置的兴趣和好奇。

• [tetris11] 表达了对Tom Scott视频的喜爱，但提到自己入坑较晚，因此看到Tom Scott谈论自己去过的地方时会感到一种诡异的感觉。这显示出对视频内容与个人经历重合的个人化体验。

data.title: Metabolism Can Shape Cells' Destinies
data.author: isaacfrond
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了细胞代谢在生命早期发育中的关键作用，挑战了传统认为基因完全主导细胞命运的观点。新研究表明，代谢不仅为细胞提供能量，其产生的代谢物还能影响基因活动，决定细胞分化方向。例如，葡萄糖代谢被发现影响胚胎发育的早期阶段。细胞通过检测环境中的代谢物质来决定是否分化为特定类型，这与外部因素如饮食和环境有关。这一发现对理解胚胎发育、细胞死亡及癌症等有重要意义，开启了代谢与发育生物学研究的新领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对生物电实验及其影响的讨论]

不同观点：
• [rolisz] 提到这让他想起Michael Levin的研究工作，尤其是通过生物电力操控让planaria（扁平虫）长出两个头，尽管这些扁平虫在基因上与正常的个体是相同的。这暗示了对生物电操控可能带来形态变化的兴趣和关注。

• [alyssa]: 对[rolisz]的观点表示惊讶，并强调这种实验结果的伦理问题，特别是如果类似技术应用到更复杂的生物体上，可能引发不可预测的生物变异和伦理挑战。

• [rolisz] 回应称，虽然伦理问题确实存在，但这类研究的价值在于它可以帮助科学家更好地理解生物体的形态发生和再生过程，并可能为再生医学提供突破口。

• [ethan]: 提出实际应用问题，质疑这种生物电操控技术是否能够在人类医学中实际应用。他认为尽管实验结果有趣，但距离临床应用可能还很遥远，特别是在安全性与可控性方面存在巨大挑战。

• [alyssa] 进一步指出，即便技术成熟，也需要有严格的监管框架来确保不会被滥用，尤其是在设计生物体形态和结构方面的潜在应用。

• [rolisz] 和 [alyssa] 之间存在关于伦理问题的争论，焦点在于如果类似技术应用到更复杂的生物体上是否合适。
• [ethan] 则更关注实际应用的可行性，并质疑该技术从实验室到临床的实际转化能力。
• 总体而言，讨论围绕生物电实验的科学价值、伦理问题以及实际应用前景展开。

E
ach of us starts life as a single cell. To develop into a complex, multicellular being, that cell must divide, and then those cells must divide again, and again — and then these stem cells start to specialize into different types, with different destinies in our bodies. In the first week, our cells reach their first turning point: They must become either placenta or embryo. Then, in the developing embryo, cells form three primary layers — ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm — which, over time, become skin, neurons, heart, gut, and so on.
These determinations of cells’ fates — what type of specialized cell they will become — occur in stages throughout embryonic development. Because each cell type has a characteristic pattern of gene activity, scientists assumed that the decisions cells make are dictated by genes: specifically,
networks of genes
that turn each other on and off, initiating a cascade that forms the correct types of cells in the correct order.
But genes are not the whole story. New research has shown the extent to which cell metabolism — the chemical reactions within a cell that provide energy and materials for growth — has an important, underappreciated role in directing cell fates.
“Metabolism is more than just housekeeping in stem cells, especially embryonic stem cells,” said
Jan Żylicz
, a developmental biologist at the University of Copenhagen. “It’s a crucial pathway that regulates decision-making processes.”
In the course of their whirring biochemical activity, cells not only produce energy but also synthesize metabolites: molecular biological building blocks, such as amino acids, nucleotides, carbohydrates and lipids. In the last decade or two, with the development of better methods for measuring metabolites in cells, there has been a surge of interest in the various ways these small molecules regulate gene activity, and in particular cell fate and development. Now, studies suggest that their presence or absence — which can be influenced by external factors, such as environment and diet — can determine the fate of a cell and, in turn, the development of an embryo.

showing how

influences the earliest stages of embryonic development. “The possibilities are so exciting. It really changes the way we think about developmental biology, the way we think about how our own life starts.”
Scientists have traditionally believed that all the instructions a cell needs to become a particular type are encoded in its DNA. In that case, when a stem cell differentiates, part of that execution involves turning on the genes that encode that cell type’s metabolism, said

{ datagubbe }
datagubbe.se
»
bra and ket: string interpolation in amigados
BRA and KET: String Interpolation in AmigaDOS
Exploring the unnecessary, part 3735928559
Spring 2025
A Short Word on AmigaDOS Scripts
Without getting caught up in semantics, AmigaDOS in this text refers to the command line portion of the Amiga computers' operating system. AmigaDOS is based on TRIPOS, but was expanded and added to by both the original Amiga team and then Commodore. One thing that remains basically the same is the parser for shell scripts, or sequence files as they're called in TRIPOS. The script parser is reasonably competent for a 1980:s home computer OS and can be used for solving
real world made up programming problems
.
The parser accepts a few special directives, such as
.KEY
, which is used to describe the template for arguments passed to the script file. For example,
.KEY FILENAME/A
tells the parser that the script accepts a string argument called FILENAME. These directives are placed at the start of the script file.
By default, the parser does string interpolation using the characters
<
(less than) and
>
(greater than). The cleverness of this is debatable: these characters are also used for I/O redirection, which can quickly make things confusing. Luckily, the parser also accepts the directives
.BRA
and
.KET
, each followed by a single character, which lets the programmer override the default interpolation characters. The terms BRA and KET are most likely borrowed from
Dirac notation
.
A Simple Example
Usually, AmigaDOS scripts using interpolation replace the default characters with curly braces,
{
and
}
, respectively. This trend may have originated at Commodore. Consider the following script:
.BRA {
.KET }
.KEY var
Echo Hello {var}!
Here,
<
and
>
have been substituted with
{
and
}
. The script takes a single argument,
var
, and the string interpolation then replaces
{var}
with the supplied argument. If saved as the file
myscript
and executed, the following AmigaShell session can be achieved:
AmigaShell> myscript datagubbe
Hello datagubbe!
AmigaShell> _
Interpolate This!
This of course begs the question: What characters can be used for string interpolation in shell scripts? Thanks to the tireless efforts of talented researchers at Datagubbe Labs, an answer can be presented - and programmers worldwide can finally get a good night's sleep. Without further ado, let's get down to brass tacks!
Test Tooling
There are text editors on the Amiga that'll happily insert any ASCII character into a text file, but why use an existing solution when you can build your own? An ARexx program -
makescript
- was
quickly hacked together
meticulously constructed for the purpose. This program generates an AmigaDOS script file with arbitrary characters for
.BRA
and
.KET
, supplied either as plain text or ASCII char codes.
The source code for makescript is available here
.
Bread and Butter
The defaults and the standard curly substitutes both work very well, as expected. Datagubbe Labs has taken the liberty of preparing screenshots, to further emphasize the validity and rigor of this important research. The scripts can also be downloaded, for transparency and reproducibility. Witness:
Default (no .BRA/.KET directives)
Standard (curly braces)
Odds and Alphas
What about non-matching character pairs, such as
[
and
}
? That works, too, which was expected. As does standard letters, such as
A
and
B
.
Odd pair ([ and })
Letters (A and B)
Bells and Whistles
Finally, non-printable characters were introduced. First, shift out (SO, decimal char code 14) and shift in (SI, decimal char code 15) were tested. These worked, too. Then, upping the ante, our relentless researchers decided to try the ASCII BEL character (decimal char code 7). AmigaDOS handles the BEL character by flashing the screen when it's encountered in a text. How would this fare in script execution? For closing the interpolation, negative acknowledgement (NAK, decimal char code 21), was chosen. This too, proved to work flawlessly - and no screen flashing was encountered when executing the script.
Shift In and Shift Out
BEL and NAK
Another Job Well Done
Naturally, when printing the script file contents to the shell window using the AmigaDOS command
Type
, these characters cause a bit of commotion. BEL, for example, results in a screen flash as expected. In order to verify that the characters are indeed present in the script files, feel free to download them above - or study
this screenshot of MicroEMACS
, displaying the non-printable characters as control sequences.
In conclusion, AmigaDOS string interpolation offers both resilience and a wide variety of choice - a cause for celebration as good as any. Thanks for your attention, and happy hacking!

data.article_summary: Mozilla.ai推出了OpenStreetMap AI Helper蓝图，旨在通过开放协作利用人工智能（AI）赋能社区。该项目利用OpenStreetMap的开放数据和卫星图像训练计算机视觉模型，以加速地图绘制过程。项目分为三个阶段：首先，通过Nominatim和Overpass API从OpenStreetMap获取数据并创建对象检测数据集；接着，使用YOLOv11模型对数据集进行微调；最后，利用训练好的模型进行推理，帮助更新OpenStreetMap数据。整个过程结合了人工验证，确保生成数据的准确性。该蓝图提供了详细的Colab指南和示例，如游泳池检测，展示了如何使用轻量级计算机视觉模型高效完成地图绘制任务。

43447335.article_content:
Motivation
At Mozilla.ai, we believe that there are a lot of opportunities where artificial intelligence (AI) can empower communities driven by open collaboration.
These opportunities need to be designed carefully, though, as many members of these communities (and people in general) are increasingly worried about the amount of
AI slop
flooding the internet.
With this idea in mind we developed and released the
OpenStreetMap AI Helper
Blueprint. If you love maps and are interested in training your own computer vision model, you’ll enjoy diving into this Blueprint.
Why OpenStreetMap?
Data is one of the most important components of any AI application, and
OpenStreetMap
has a vibrant community that collaborates to maintain and extend the most complete open map database available.
If you haven’t heard of it,
OpenStreetMap
is an open, editable map of the world created by a community of mappers who contribute and maintain data about roads, trails, cafés, railway stations, and more.
Combined with other sources, like satellite imagery, this database offers infinite possibilities to train different AI models.
As a long-time user and contributor to
OpenStreetMap
, I wanted to build an end-to-end application where a model is first trained with this data and then used to contribute back.
The idea is to use AI to speed up the slower parts of the mapping process (roaming around the map, drawing polygons) while keeping a human in the loop for the critical parts (verifying that the generated data is correct).
Why Computer Vision?
Large Language Models (LLM) and, more recently, Visual Language Models (VLM) are sucking all the oxygen out of the AI room, but there are a lot of interesting applications that don’t (need to) use this type of models.
Many of the
Map Features
you can find in OpenStreetMap are represented with a polygon ('Area'). It turns out that finding and drawing these polygons is a very time consuming task for a human, but Computer Vision models can be easily trained for the task (when provided with enough data).
We chose to split the work of finding and drawing map features into 2 computer vision tasks using state-of-the-art non-LLM models:
Object Detection
with
YOLOv11
, by
Ultralytics
, which identifies where relevant features exist in an image.
Segmentation
with
SAM2
, by
Meta
, which refines the detected features by outlining their exact shape.
These models are lightweight, fast, and local-friendly – it’s refreshing to work with models that don’t demand a high-end GPU just to function. As an example, the combined weights of YOLOv11 and SAM2 take much less disk space (<250MB) than any of the smallest Visual Language Models available, like
SmolVLM
(4.5GB).
By combining these models, we can automate much of the mapping process while keeping humans in control for final verification.
The OpenStreetMap AI Helper Blueprint
The Blueprint can be divided into 3 stages:
Stage 1: Create an Object Detection dataset from OpenStreetMap
The first stage involves fetching data from OpenStreetMap, combining it with satellite images, and transforming it into a format suitable for training.
You can run it yourself in the
Create Dataset Colab
.
For fetching OpenStreetMap data, we use:
The
Nominatim API
to provide users with a flexible way of selecting an area of interest. In our swimming pool example, we use
Galicia
for training and
Viana do Castelo
for validation.
The
Overpass API
to download all the relevant polygons using specific
tags
within the selected area of interest. In our swimming pool example, we use
leisure=swimming_pool
discarding the ones also tagged with
location=indoor
.
Once all the polygons have been downloaded, you can choose a
zoom level
. We use this zoom level to first identify all the tiles that contain a polygon and then download them using the
Static Tiles API
from
Mapbox
.
The polygons in latitude and longitude coordinates are transformed to a bounding box in pixel coordinates relative to each tile and then saved in the
Ultralytics YOLO format
.
Finally, the dataset is uploaded to the
Hugging Face Hub
. You can check our example
mozilla-ai/osm-swimming-pools
.
Stage 2 - Finetune an Object Detection model
Once the dataset is uploaded in the right format, finetuning a
YOLOv11
(or any other model supported by Ultralytics) is quite easy.
You can run it yourself in the
Finetune Model Colab
and check all the
available hyperparameters
.
Once the model is trained, it is also uploaded to the
Hugging Face Hub
. You can check our example
mozilla-ai/swimming-pool-detector
.
Stage 3 - Contributing to OpenStreetMap
Once you have a finetuned Object Detection model, you can use it to run inference across multiple tiles.
You can run inference yourself in the
Run Inference Colab
.
We also provide a hosted demo where you can try our example swimming pool detector:
HuggingFace Demo
.

• **[stereo] 反对直接加入AI检测的地物**：认为AI算法存在误报问题，并且在绘制直线或矩形物体时会出现变形。虽然AI工具可以辅助检测缺失地物，但仍需要人工干预以确保准确性。他引用了OSM的导入指南和自动化编辑行为准则作为依据。

• **[throwaway346434] 支持某种程度的自动化和数据导入**：认为单靠人工编辑无法在全球范围内解决地图数据的完整性问题，需要一个可扩展的框架来导入和维护数据。他提出对数据质量进行注释和标记来源的想法，并认为可以接受带有已知局限性的AI推断数据，只要消费者可以根据需求过滤数据源。

• **[orbital-decay] 对自动化编辑持怀疑态度**：基于在南美旅行的经历，指出某些地区的OSM编辑看起来是自动化的，导致数据在某些地方几乎无法使用，尤其是在巴西的大城市。

• **[daavoo] 回应反馈并作出调整**：表示已经根据反馈将直接上传到OSM的代码替换为导出到OsmChange格式，并计划在OSM论坛的专门线程中继续讨论。

• **[ks2048] 提供相关资源**：提到以前在这个领域做过一些工作，并分享了相关的模型、数据集和工具链接。

• **[qwertox] 讨论Mapbox的政策**：指出Mapbox在非商业用途或OSM使用时的政策，允许使用其卫星数据进行矢量数据追踪。

• **[ySteeK] 强调地面的真实性**：坚决反对贡献任何AI幻想的数据，认为只应地图化地面真实存在的事物。

• **[gpvos] 偏题批评Mozilla**：认为Mozilla应专注于制作好的浏览器，而非其他事情。

• **[pierotofy] 分享相关项目经验**：提到几个月前做过类似的小规模地理数据项目，并分享了相关GitHub链接。

• **[anakaine] 关注AI模型的精细调整**：希望看到更多关于如何精细调整SAM/2以检测特定地物的细节，认为虽然现有模型在检测上表现良好，但边缘处理上仍需大量人工清理工作。

• **争议焦点**：是否应直接在OSM中加入AI检测的地物。反对者担心AI的误报和不准确性，支持者认为自动化和数据导入是解决全球地图数据完整性的必要手段。

• **技术实现和工具**：讨论中提到了多种技术实现和工具，如SAM/2和Yolov8模型的使用，以及相关GitHub项目和资源。

• **政策和指南**：引用了OSM的导入指南和自动化编辑行为准则，以及Mapbox的使用政策，作为讨论的基础和参考。

data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在Apple Silicon Macs上实现Linux支持的细节工作，特别是麦克风阵列和音频处理的复杂性。

不同观点：
• rob74认为，即使是内置麦克风这样看似 insignificant 的细节在Apple Silicon Macs上也需要大量工作，并引用Asahi Linux的进展报告说明Apple产品的复杂性。
• com2kid分享了20年前Toshiba Tablet PC的麦克风阵列技术，该技术允许指向性录音，并认为这是一个令人惊叹但少见的功能。
• raphlinus建议关注faer库以进行SIMD优化，并提到其博客和播客即将讨论Rust SIMD相关内容。
• marmaram指出，便宜的笔记本硬件也能通过软件DSP技术获得不错的效果，并提到Asahi的音频工作同样适用于普通笔记本。
• GeekyBear引用Asahi Linux的进展报告，强调PDM麦克风的全向性和敏感性问题，并提到PipeWire和WirePlumber在音频支持中的作用。
• JohnBooty质疑Apple在音频实现上的复杂性，并以MBP的扬声器为例，认为Apple在扬声器设计上采用了与高端蓝牙扬声器类似的技术。
• pzo关心M2/M3等新款Apple Silicon设备是否也具备类似的麦克风阵列支持，并询问是否仅在Linux或MacOS上有效。
• pvg提供了与triforce相关的Github仓库链接。
• apitman对OP使用本科一年级工程数学知识实现beamformer表示赞赏。
• qoez认为麦克风阵列可以用于测量局部几何形状，例如手部动作。
• amelius希望实现一个能让其他制造商容易采用的麦克风阵列方案。
• swyx询问麦克风阵列的实际应用，并质疑Apple为何没有提供更高层次的API。
• everfrustrated认为MacOS上的beamforming效果显著，尤其是在消除背景噪音方面。
• llm_nerd解释了软件进行beamforming需要离散的麦克风输入，并质疑Apple是否在硬件上实现了beamforming。
• _zoltan_认为讨论标题应明确指出是针对Asahi Linux，以免误导。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Apple在麦克风和扬声器实现上的复杂性是否必要，部分用户认为Apple的设计过于复杂，而其他用户则对其效果表示赞赏。
• 讨论还涉及Linux和MacOS对麦克风阵列的支持情况，以及是否有可能在其他硬件上实现类似功能。
• 部分用户分享了个人经验和历史技术背景，提供了对麦克风阵列技术的多角度理解。

data.title: The Game Designer Playing Through His Own Psyche
data.author: FinnLobsien
data.article_summary:
《史丹利的寓言》是一款由游戏设计师戴维·雷登（Davey Wreden）与其合作者威廉·普格（William Pugh）于2013年发布的成功作品。游戏围绕一名办公室员工史丹利展开，他在某天发现同事全部消失，只能跟随脑海中一个叙述声音的指引。游戏核心是玩家与叙述者之间的意志对抗。最初，雷登和普格预计游戏能卖出五万份，但发售首日就达到了这个数字。尽管取得了巨大成功，25岁的雷登却陷入了严重的抑郁。

这款游戏因其独特的哲学思考和存在主义幽默受到广泛赞誉，雷登也因此成为打破常规的游戏设计师。他的第二部作品《入门指南》同样获得好评，并影响了包括电视剧《离职》在内的其他创作。现年36岁的雷登居住在温哥华，继续创作如《Wanderstop》等挑战传统游戏结构的作品。

雷登自小喜欢设下陷阱的故事，如《搏击俱乐部》和《第二十二条军规》，并通过幽默与想象力寻求心理慰藉。尽管少年时期并不快乐，但他通过创造性工作找到了自己的价值。

A little more than a decade ago, the video-game designer Davey Wreden experienced a crippling success. In October, 2013, he and a collaborator, William Pugh, released the Stanley Parable HD, a polished and expanded version of a prototype that Wreden had developed in college, and which he had made available, free of charge, two years before. Wreden and Pugh hoped that they might sell fifty thousand or so copies of the new version in the course of its lifetime. They sold that many on the first day. Wreden was twenty-five years old, and he had everything he’d ever wanted: money, success, recognition. He became severely depressed.
The Stanley Parable is a game about a lonely man. It centers on an office worker, Stanley, who, one day, looks up from his cubicle and discovers that his colleagues have vanished. All that’s left to keep him company is a voice in his head—provided by the British actor Kevan Brighting—which narrates Stanley’s actions. But Stanley doesn’t have to do what the voice says. The game quickly becomes a contest of will between the player and the narrator.
When I first played the Stanley Parable, I was gobsmacked by
one sequence in particular
, which begins when Stanley walks down a dark corridor marked “
ESCAPE
.” He finds himself whisked toward a hydraulic press—and certain death, if the narrator’s taunts are to be believed. Just before impact, a previously unheard female narrator (voiced by Lesley Staples) describes how the machine kills Stanley, “crushing every bone in his body.” But the machine doesn’t mush him. Instead, he arrives at a brightly lit museum. Therein lies a small-scale model of his office, with signs explaining how each section was fussed over to insure that the player progresses at a good clip. On the far wall are the game’s credits. The new narrator notes that soon it will be re-started, and Stanley will be alive as ever. “When every path you can walk has been created for you long in advance, death becomes meaningless, making life the same,” she says. Then she adds, “Do you see now that Stanley was already dead from the moment he hit Start?”
I had been playing video games for thirty years, and I had never seen the medium deconstructed so skillfully or with such existential humor. I felt the way that I imagine cinephiles did in 1960, emerging from dark theatres having just seen “Breathless.” The game’s young creators seemed to be free from the trappings of what had come before.
Wreden has since released a second critically acclaimed title, the Beginner’s Guide, and cemented his reputation as a designer who defies convention. Neither of his games asks much more of the player than an ability to move through a 3-D space; what distinguishes them is their philosophical bent and penchant for narrative tricks. (Gabriel Winslow-Yost, writing in
The New York Review of Books,
invoked Nabokov, calling the Beginner’s Guide “a kind of interactive ‘Pale Fire.’ ”) Among gamers, Wreden has acquired cult-celebrity status, and his influence extends beyond his own medium: even the creator of the TV show “
Severance
”—another office drama that raises questions about free will as it veers between whimsy and dread—has cited the Stanley Parable as an inspiration. (The game also had
a brief cameo
in an episode of “House of Cards.”)
Wreden, now thirty-six, has a slim build and a sweep of brown hair. When we spoke for the first time, last year, he was dressed in a dark-gray T-shirt. He works from home, in Vancouver, and the wall behind his desk is adorned with drawings of characters from the video-game franchise Persona, images from the manga
Chainsaw Man
, and pictures of food. In a corner of the room, next to a bookcase, hangs a ramen-shop paper lantern that he acquired on a trip to Osaka. He was winding down production on his third game, Wanderstop, out this month, and in a reflective mood about its predecessors—works he described as having been designed “to break and unwind the tightly coiled, traditional structure of what games like that were supposed to do.”
As a teen-ager, Wreden loved stories that set traps: “Fight Club” and “The Usual Suspects,” with their late reveals, and works by Roald Dahl and Shirley Jackson. Growing up in Sacramento, California, as the eldest son of a pair of doctors, he gravitated toward brainy but silly humor; he was a big fan of “Weird Al” Yankovic, Flight of the Conchords, and Joseph Heller’s “
Catch-22
.” Wreden was not an especially happy kid, but from an early age he believed that he could imagine his way to something better. His father once told him that it was hard to have a conversation with him in his adolescence, because Wreden usually forgot what other people said. “It wasn’t, like, a memory thing, or an A.D.H.D. thing,” Wreden recalled. “It was literally just, like, anything that didn’t fit into my big grand plan of doing as much as possible, achieving as much as possible, and thinking as bi

data.title: Rickover's Lessons
data.author: pepys
data.article_summary: 文章总结了查尔斯·杨对美国工业政策的分析，重点介绍了海曼·里科弗上将如何通过建立核海军，推动美国在战略竞争中取得优势。文章指出，美国目前面临工业基础投资不足的问题，生产能力远不及中国，特别是在造船业和关键矿物加工方面。为应对挑战，美国需要从里科弗的成功经验中学习，他通过强有力的领导和技术创新，在短时间内成功打造了世界首艘核潜艇和核动力航母，确保了美国在20世纪的海上战略优势。里科弗注重人才选拔与持续培训，亲自面试每一位候选人，并要求他们进行深入的自学和实地考察，以确保技术专精。文章最后强调，工业政策不仅依赖立法，更需要像里科弗这样的领导力和技术培训体系。

  - [areoform] 强调Rickover并非只雇佣“最好”的人，而是开发人的潜力。他将人才视为可培养的，而非现成就完美的。
  - [sgarland] 作为前潜艇兵，支持Rickover的理念，尤其是对责任和训练的重视，但指出当代企业文化缺乏这种严格性，导致问题无法有效解决。

• **对现代管理方式的反思**：

  - [throwawaymaths] 指出Rickover在海军内部曾受到很多反对，直到他的方法被证明有效。

• Rickover的理念与现代企业管理文化的冲突与融合：讨论中多次提到Rickover的严格管理和责任追究在现代企业中难以实施，但也有观点认为某些领域（如技术操作）仍需借鉴他的做法。

Charles Yang is the executive director for the
Center for Industrial Strategy
, a bipartisan think tank focused on industrial policy. Previously, he served as an AI and Supply Chain Policy Advisor at the Department of Energy and was an ML Engineer at an AI hardware startup in San Francisco. Today, he’s here to present some excerpts from
his research
into how Admiral Hyman Rickover built the nuclear navy.
Strategic competition demands more than technological innovation — it requires building industrial power. The U.S. is realizing the damage done by decades of underinvestment in the nation’s industrial base, which now jeopardizes its ability to compete on the global stage. Today, the production capacity of
Chinese shipyards is over 200 times that of US shipyards
, and China has used its
chokehold on critical mineral processing as leverage
to retaliate against US sanctions.
A new bipartisan consensus is emerging around the need for industrial policy — from the passage of the CHIPS and Science Act, to the recent bipartisan introduction of the
SHIPS for America Act
and the
Critical Minerals for the Future Act
.
As Congress steps into this more active role, policymakers should learn from the successes of our past. Nearly 75 years ago, Admiral Hyman G. Rickover, “Father of the Nuclear Navy”, pioneered a bold program to develop and operationalize nuclear power in the Navy. Under his leadership, the U.S. government harnessed the power of the atom, building the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine and the world’s largest fleet of nuclear reactors for civilian power.
Lessons From the Past
Rickover spent his entire career in the Navy and is still the longest-serving naval officer in US history. He spent the first 20 years of his career as an electrical engineer, where he honed a strong technical foundation and unique management style. In 1946, he was assigned a 1-year tour of duty at the Oak Ridge site of the Manhattan Project. Rickover immediately recognized the transformative potential of nuclear technology — he spent the rest of his career building the “Nuclear Navy,” which ensured US strategic dominance of the high seas for the rest of the 20th century.
Within the span of 10 years, Rickover created an entire office dedicated to nuclear propulsion, and successfully launched the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine without cost overruns. He conclusively demonstrated the strategic importance of nuclear propulsion in a timeframe no one thought possible and helped the US beat the Soviets to nuclear propulsion for submarines by 3 years. His institutional legacy is the US Navy’s safe construction and operation of nuclear reactors.
As the US gears up for another strategic competition, Rickover’s story can offer helpful lessons for aspiring technocrats. Oftentimes, industrial policy is framed in terms of legislation, but Rickover demonstrates that industrial policy is as much about policy as it is about strong leadership.
USS Enterprise, the world’s first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.
Source
.
Talent, Training, and Management
Rickover spent an inordinate amount of time focused on interviewing personnel —
he made the final hiring decision for every naval officer who applied to serve on a nuclear submarine until he retired
. And he was an unorthodox interviewer, screening for high agency individuals who could think on their feet — literally! To test their composure, Rickover famously made candidates sit in a chair with the front two legs shortened as he loomed over them during questioning.
The infamous “Rickover chair”
One interview account:
For one interviewee who said he liked hiking, Rickover asked him if he had ever hiked the nearby “Goat Mountain”. When he said he had not, Rickover told him to bring him proof he had climbed it by tomorrow morning and he would be hired. It turns out that Goat Mountain was the peak of a structure for mountain goats in a zoo. He went to the zoo, asked a tourist to take his picture, jumped into the enclosure, and climbed to the top. He’s hired the next day!
But it didn’t end at the interview process — Rickover believed in continued technical training for his staff and in building out a talented workforce base for this new technology:
While Rickover worked to staff up quickly in the short term, he also set out to build a deep bench and a long-term pipeline of talent. He required each officer and engineer he hired to submit a self-study plan demonstrating mastery of advanced texts in metallurgy, physics, and chemistry, along with field trips to AEC facilities, totaling 854 hours of study or 16 hours per week. He also worked with MIT to develop a survey course on nuclear physics and a master's degree in nuclear engineering,

data.author: Petiver

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：疼痛的主观性、测量方式及其在医疗系统中的应用

不同观点：
• **j_bum** 认为疼痛包括感觉辨别和情感情绪两个主要成分，且两者都可以独立或同时发生。虽然寻找感觉辨别成分的生物标志物可能有价值，但对情感情绪成分的测量持怀疑态度。同时担心依赖生物标志物会导致医生更加怀疑患者的主观疼痛体验，特别是女性和有色人种患者常常不被信任。
• **GarnetFloride** 强调急性和慢性疼痛的处理方式不同，慢性疼痛类似于与配偶相处，需要共存。还提到男女对疼痛的感受不同，女性的疼痛往往不被认真对待。描述疼痛对工作的影响更容易引起医生的注意。
• **gaoshan** 提到文化差异可能导致疼痛描述的误解，例如在中文中用“酸”来形容疼痛，但美国医生却认为这不具有意义。
• **PaulKeeble** 指出，在实际医疗中，患者使用6分（满分10分）的疼痛评分最有可能获得保险赔付和医疗关注。但由于缺乏生物标志物和阿片类药物的撤回，许多慢性疼痛患者得不到有效治疗。医疗系统中对疼痛的偏见和污名化问题严重。
• **lijok** 认为准确的疼痛测量机制在兽医学中尤为重要，因为动物无法自我报告疼痛。描述了因无法准确评估狗的疼痛而面临的困境，强调了改进疼痛评估方法的必要性。
• **perching_aix** 对疼痛测量技术的发展表示欢迎，但也担心这些方法可能无法全面捕捉疼痛现象，导致误解和争议。
• **Fin_Code** 认为疼痛是相对的，依赖患者的主观输入是存在缺陷的。

补充讨论：
• **INTPenis** 以幽默的方式设想未来医生可以使用机器感受患者的疼痛，以更准确地诊断。
• **m3kw9** 补充说明心理因素可以放大疼痛感受，例如对针头的恐惧会使疼痛更加严重。

争议焦点：
• 生物标志物是否能够准确测量和反映疼痛，特别是情感情绪成分的疼痛。
• 依赖生物标志物是否会导致医生更加怀疑患者的主观疼痛体验，特别是在特定群体（如女性和有色人种）中。
• 疼痛评估方法在不同文化和语言背景下的适用性和理解差异。

data.title: Show HN: We made an MCP Server so Cursor can build things from REST API docs
data.author: goargp
data.article_summary:
Apidog MCP Server是一个允许开发者将Apidog项目中的API文档作为AI开发环境（如Cursor）的数据源的工具。它可以帮助Agentic AI直接访问和使用API文档，从而加快开发速度，提高工作效率。开发者可以通过它实现基于API文档的代码生成、DTO更新、注释添加以及MVC代码创建等功能。

### 安装步骤：
1. 在Apidog生成访问令牌并获取项目ID。
2. 配置IDE的MCP配置文件，添加相应的JSON代码。
3. 根据操作系统（Windows或其它）调整配置文件格式。
4. 配置完成后，AI即可利用API文档进行各种开发操作。

### 其他功能：
- 支持直接读取Swagger或OpenAPI规范文件。
- 建议将访问令牌配置为环境变量以防泄露。

该工具目前处于测试阶段，欢迎用户提供反馈和建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Model Context Protocol）的实际应用价值和实现方式

不同观点：
• **jascha_eng** 认为，尽管许多公司发布了专门的MCP产品，但它们的实际生产力价值有限。他认为，MCP在与特定工具（如cursor和claude code）结合时才显得有用，而自定义功能对他来说并不实用。同时，他认为提供相关文档有助于结果，但尚未看到自动化方式的成功案例。

• **smokel** 提供了MCP的定义，指出它是一个开放协议，标准化了应用程序如何向LLM提供上下文，并提供了相关链接。

• **koakuma-chan** 指出，MCP似乎仅在使用其商业API平台“Apidog”时才有效，并质疑这与从普通文档网站抓取文档相比有何优势。

• **khvirabyan** 认为MCP非常有趣，并指出许多API平台现在可以提供一个MCP服务器来连接所有现有的API集成。他提到Zapier已经发布了他们自己的MCP服务器，并期待看到未来如何发展，包括GitHub是否会提供官方MCP或社区支持的集成。

• **hariharasudhan** 希望能够在本地运行MCP，而不是通过服务器和令牌，因为文档已经是公开的。

• **musha68k** 质疑“vibe coding”方法在实际生产环境中的可行性，询问是否有人使用这种方法开发了 robust 和可维护的代理系统，而无需进行重大重构或重写。

• **nindalf** 认为MCP对其付费工具过于特定，建议一个暴露devdocs.io或类似的MCP，缓存选定语言/框架文档，并结合向量/BM25搜索，将其作为一个工具暴露给LLM。

• **shiraayal** 提供了一个将fastapi转换为MCP服务器的repo链接，指出不需要“apidog”即可实现。

• **franky47** 对MCP没有让代理读取包文档和类型定义以防止API幻觉感到失望，并建议从现有文档和代码中获取真相来源，而不需要第三次工作。

• **Matsta** 提到一个类似的项目DevDocs，但指出在运行时遇到问题。

• **z3t4** 质疑代码是否被混淆/压缩，并询问原因。

• **tb1989** 分享了一篇文章，认为MCP不是AI的USB-C，而只是一个USB-Claude Dongle，但仍认为这项工作非常有价值。

• **zaleria** 简明指出，文档是为人类准备的，让LLM读代码即可。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP的实际应用价值和其在不同平台上的实现方式，特别是商业工具和开放协议之间的平衡。
• 对MCP的期望包括本地运行能力、与现有文档系统的整合以及在生产环境中的可行性。
• 对文档和代码的处理方式也有讨论，部分参与者希望LLM直接读取代码而不是依赖文档。

Formal Verification of Machine Learning Models in Lean
Welcome to the
Formal Verification of Machine Learning Models in Lean
project. This repository provides a framework for specifying and proving properties—such as robustness, fairness, and interpretability—of machine learning models using Lean 4.
A live, interactive webpage is available at:
proof-pipeline-interactor.lovable.app
Overview
In high-stakes applications (e.g., healthcare, finance, autonomous systems), ensuring that machine learning models meet strict reliability and fairness properties is essential. This project provides:
Lean Library
: Formal definitions for neural networks, linear models, decision trees, and advanced models (ConvNets, RNNs, Transformers), along with properties like adversarial robustness, fairness, interpretability, monotonicity, and sensitivity analysis.
Model Translator
: A Python-based tool that exports trained models (e.g., from PyTorch) to a JSON schema and automatically generates corresponding Lean code.
Web Interface
: A Flask application for uploading models, triggering Lean verification, visualizing model architectures (using Graphviz), and viewing proof logs.
CI/CD Pipeline
: A reproducible, Dockerized environment using Lean 4’s Lake build system with GitHub Actions for continuous integration and deployment.
Features
Formal Verification
: Prove key properties of ML models including adversarial robustness and fairness.
Advanced Model Support
: Extendable to support convolutional networks, recurrent architectures, transformers, and even symbolic models.
Interactive Web Portal
: Upload model JSON files, view generated Lean code, trigger Lean proof compilation, and visualize the model architecture.
Automated Build Pipeline
: Docker and GitHub Actions integration for reliable, reproducible builds.
Quick Start
Clone the Repository:
git clone https://github.com/fraware/formal_verif_ml.git
cd
formal_verif_ml
Build the Docker Image:
docker build -t formal-ml
.
Run the Container:
docker run -p 5000:5000 formal-ml
Access the Web Interface:
Open
http://localhost:5000
in your browser.
For detailed usage and contribution guidelines, please refer to the User Guide and Developer Guide.
Contributing
Contributions, improvements, and bug reports are welcome. Please see the
docs/
folder for additional developer guidelines and contribution standards.

43448457.article_content:
Andi Kleen's blog
Tilting at windmills and other endeavors
Quitting an Intel x86 hypervisor
with one comment
This is an esoteric topic that might be of interest to people implementing Intel hypervisors. It assumes you know the basics of the Intel virtualization architecture, see
Hypervisor from scratch
for a tutorial. The actual full VT architecture is described in Volume 3 of the
Intel SDM
Let’s say we write an x86 hypervisor that starts in the UEFI environment and virtualizes the initialization phase of an OS. But the hypervisor wants to eventually quit itself to not cause extra overhead during OS run time.
The way the hypervisor works is that it runs in its own memory and with its own page tables which are switched atomically on every VM exit by the VT-x implementation. This way it is isolated from the main OS.
At some vm exit with the hypervisor running in its own context it decides that it is not needed anymore and wants to quit. To disable VT support the VMXOFF instruction can be used. But what we really need is an atomic VMXOFF + switch to the original OS page tables plus a jump, and all that without using any registers which need to be already restored to the original state of the OS.
One trick is to use the MOV to CR3 instruction that reloads the page table as a jump. As soon as the page table is reloaded the CPU will fetch the next instruction with the translations from the freshly loaded page table, so we can transfer execution to the guest context. However to do that the MOV CR3 needs to be located just before the page offset of the target instruction. This can be done by copying a trampoline to the right page offset (potentially overlapping into the previous page). The trampoline is located in a special transfer page table mapping that places writable code pages overlapping the target mapping.
But there are some complications. The hypervisor also needs to load the segmentation state (like GDT/LDT/IDT) of the guest. In theory they could just be loaded by mapping these guest pages into the transfer mapping and loading them before the transfer.  But what happens if the GDT/LDT/IDT is on the same page as the target address? This is common in real OS’ assembler startup code which is implemented in a small assembler file without any page separation between code and data. One option would be to copy them to the transfer page too and load it there, or the hypervisor first copies them to a temporary buffer and loads it from there. In the second option the base addresses of these structures will be incorrect, but in practice you can often rely on them getting reloaded eventually anyways.
Another problem is the register state of the target. MOV to CR3 needs a register as the source of the reload, and it needs to be the last instruction of the trampoline. So it is impossible to restore the register it uses. But remember the hypervisor is doing this as the result of a VM exit. If we chose an exit for a condition that already clobbers a register we can use the same register for the reload and the next instruction executed in the original target (and which caused the exit originally) will just overwrite it again.
A very convenient instruction for this is CPUID. It is executed multiple times in OS startup and overwrites multiple registers. In fact VMX always intercepts CPUID so it has to handle these exits in any case. So the trick to quit an hypervisor is to wait for the next CPUID exit and then use one of the registers clobbered by CPUID for the final CR3 reload.  This will have inconsistent register state for one instruction in the target, but unless the original OS is currently running a debugger it will never notice. In principle any exit as a result of an instruction that clobbers a register can be used for this.
There is another potential complication if the target address of the OS conflicts with where the hypervisor is running before entering the transfer mapping. The transfer mapping needs to map the original code so that it can be jumped to. This could be solved with a third auxiliary mapping that is used before jumping to the transfer trampoline. In practice it doesn’t seem to be a problem because x86 OS typically run in a 1:1 mapping for startup, and that cannot conflict with the 1:1 mapping used by  UEFI programs as our hypervisor.
Happy hypervisor hacking!

43448457.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在Intel x86架构下，如何实现一个hypervisor在完成初始化阶段后自行退出，以避免在操作系统运行时造成额外开销。关键在于使用VMXOFF指令关闭虚拟化支持，并通过特定技巧实现从hypervisor到原操作系统的原子切换。主要方法包括利用MOV到CR3指令重新加载页表，并通过一个"trampoline"技巧跳转到目标指令。文章还提到处理GDT/LDT/IDT段状态和寄存器状态的复杂性，以及通过选择合适的VM退出条件（如CPUID指令）来解决寄存器冲突问题。最终，文章提供了一种在实际操作中有效退出hypervisor的解决方案。
43448457.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕早期操作系统和处理器模式的技术讨论，包括对特定技术细节的回忆和多处理器场景下的技术挑战。

不同观点：
• userbinator提到早期的Windows系统需要在进入保护模式之前退出V86模式，并引用了未公开的GEMMIS接口来处理该任务。这一评论强调了早期系统技术实现的复杂性和未公开接口的使用。

• gblargg分享了自己在编写代码恢复声音模块状态时的技术细节，描述了如何巧妙利用几字节的指令和循环来逐步恢复内存和寄存器状态。这一观点展示了在资源受限环境下编程的创造性和技巧。

• dooglius提出了关于多处理器场景下的潜在问题，质疑在多个处理器上执行不同指令时，是否能保持行为的一致性，特别是涉及像CPUID这样的指令时。这反映了对多处理器系统中同步和一致性问题的关注。

• snvzz对x86架构持负面态度，认为这种技术即将被淘汰，暗示未来将不再需要处理这些复杂的x86特性。这一观点表达了对技术更新换代的期望。

补充讨论：
• mrnage提供了一个存档链接，可能是对相关讨论或信息的存档参考，但未直接参与技术讨论。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在dooglius提出的多处理器场景下的技术挑战，以及snvzz对x86架构的负面评价与其他技术爱好者的怀旧和技术分享形成对比。

data.title: European Union OS – Fedora Linux and KDE Plasma Based
data.author: maverick74
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款名为Secure OS的操作系统，该系统基于开源软件构建，主打隐私和安全。与许多现代操作系统不同，Secure OS不会在未经用户同意的情况下向开发者或第三方发送数据，即所谓的"不回传"（doesn't phone home）。这种设计旨在保护用户隐私，防止信息泄露。Secure OS适用于对数据安全有较高要求的用户，如企业、政府机构和注重隐私的个人。文章还强调了开源社区在提升软件透明度和安全性方面的贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲自主开发技术项目的潜力和背景

不同观点：
• Rick76的观点：  
   - 支持欧洲开发独立于美国大科技公司的技术项目，特别是在当前贸易战和欧洲希望与美国大科技保持距离的背景下。  
   - 认为美国人也可能欢迎这种竞争，因为当前互联网被少数公司垄断，导致过度极化。  
   - 特别指出YouTube缺乏竞争。

• akagusu的观点：  
   - 对项目的基础表示质疑，指出该项目基于Fedora，而Fedora由一家美国公司拥有。  
   - 隐含的质疑是，既然项目基于美国技术，如何真正实现独立于美国大科技公司的目标。

• WhereIsTheTruth的观点：  
   - 简短评论，似乎对akagusu的观点表示赞同，提到Red Hat（Fedora的所有者）后即结束，暗示对项目独立性的怀疑。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于，欧洲自主开发的技术项目如果基于美国公司的技术（如Fedora和Red Hat），是否能够真正实现其政治和经济上的独立目标。  
- Rick76的支持立场与其他两位的质疑立场形成对比，讨论的核心在于项目的基础技术选择是否与其目标一致。

data.title: The Race to Decipher Cuneiform in the 19th Century
data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 在1850年代，楔形文字仍是未解之谜。1857年，四位学者展开竞争，试图破译这种世界上最古老的文字系统。关键文物是藏于大英博物馆的一块有3000年历史的 clay tablet，上面记录了亚述国王提格拉特帕拉沙尔一世的军事胜利。最终，他们的独立工作成功验证了楔形文字的释读方法，揭示了美索不达米亚古代文明的秘密。这场竞赛标志着人类对古代历史理解的重要突破。

data.title: A single-fibre computer enables textile networks and distributed inference
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种纺织纤维计算机，它集成了模拟传感、数字存储、处理和通信功能，重量不到5克。通过可折叠的插层技术，将微型设备的二维结构转化为符合纤维几何形状的三维布局，并通过螺旋铜微线连接，制成可机洗、可拉伸的弹性纤维。该纤维计算机包含32位浮点微控制器，可独立执行边缘计算任务，并能编织、缝合到衣物中。其组装过程允许集成额外功能，如可充电纤维电源，能持续工作近6小时。通过无线通信方案，实现了光学链路和射频通信。实验显示，配备四个纤维计算机的衣物能通过简单加权投票将身体活动分类的准确率从67%提高到95%。

43410666.article_content:
Subjects
Electrical and electronic engineering
Electronic devices
Abstract
Despite advancements in wearable technologies
1
,
2
, barriers remain in achieving distributed computation located persistently on the human body. Here a textile fibre computer that monolithically combines analogue sensing, digital memory, processing and communication in a mass of less than 5 g is presented. Enabled by a foldable interposer, the two-dimensional pad architectures of microdevices were mapped to three-dimensional cylindrical layouts conforming to fibre geometry. Through connection with helical copper microwires, eight microdevices were thermally drawn into a machine-washable elastic fibre capable of more than 60% stretch. This programmable fibre, which incorporates a 32-bit floating-point microcontroller, independently performs edge computing tasks even when braided, woven, knitted or seam-sewn into garments. The universality of the assembly process allows for the integration of additional functions with simple modifications, including a rechargeable fibre power source that operates the computer for nearly 6 h. Finally, we surmount the perennial limitation of rigid interconnects by implementing two wireless communication schemes involving woven optical links and seam-inserted radio-frequency communications. To demonstrate its utility, we show that garments equipped with four fibre computers, one per limb, operating individually trained neural networks achieve, on average, 67% accuracy in classifying physical activity. However, when networked, inference accuracy increases to 95% using simple weighted voting.

data.title: Why we chose LangGraph to build our coding agent
data.author: timbilt
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Qodo团队在开发AI编程助手过程中，从早期结构化的工作流转向更灵活的系统，利用LangGraph框架实现了兼具灵活性和主见性的编码助手。初始阶段，团队使用预定义的工作流处理不同编码任务，如测试生成和代码审查。随着LLM模型（如Claude Sonnet 3.5）的进步，他们转向构建动态且灵活的代理，以适应各种用户请求，同时保持对编码最佳实践的坚持。

LangGraph采用图形化方法，通过状态机和节点定义工作流，允许从完全开放到完全结构化的多种方式。其灵活性使得团队能够根据新模型调整工作流的结构。主工作流包括上下文收集、任务规划、执行和验证等步骤，验证失败时会反馈而非重头开始。LangGraph的API简化了复杂系统的构建，通过声明式方法定义工作流，使其易于理解和修改。这种方法确保了系统在适应新模型的同时，保持高质量的编码标准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对LangGraph及其相关技术（如Mastra、LangChain等）的评价和对比，特别关注其文档质量、开发挑战、商业模式等方面。

不同观点：

We’ve been building AI coding assistants at Qodo since the GPT-3 days. Our initial approach was highly structured with predefined flows for different coding tasks like test generation, code reviews, and improvements. This approach worked well with earlier generations of LLMs and with structured flows we were able to get real-world value from older models, despite all of their limitations.
Since Claude Sonnet 3.5 was released 9 months ago, LLMs have become significantly more capable at general-purpose coding tasks. The new models opened up the possibility to build something more dynamic and flexible while still maintaining our standards for code quality. We wanted to move away from rigid workflows to an agent that could adapt to any kind of user request, while still reflecting our opinionated views on how AI can be best used for coding.
Initially, we needed a framework that would let us quickly validate our ideas and from the few options that were available about 4 months ago, we settled on LangGraph for our initial proof of concept. We were pleasantly surprised to see that the framework has proven flexible and mature enough to carry us all the way to production.
In this post, I’ll explain why LangGraph was the right choice for us, and how it enabled us to build a coding assistant that balances flexibility with our opinionated approach to coding best practices.
Flexibility to be opinionated
Our key consideration was the ability to create opinionated workflows while maintaining adaptability. LangGraph takes a graph-based approach that gives you flexibility to build agents that land anywhere on the spectrum from completely open-ended — where you just give an LLM all available tools and let it run in a loop — to fully structured deterministic flows (like the ones we started with).
At its core, LangGraph lets you define a state machine for your agent. You create nodes that represent discrete steps in your workflow and edges that define the possible transitions between them. Each node can perform specific functions—gathering context, planning, generating code, or validating—while the graph structure determines how these functions connect.
The density of connections in the graph corresponds to how structured or flexible your agent is. A sparse graph with few connections corresponds with a more rigid, predictable flow where each step leads to exactly one next step. A dense graph with many interconnections gives the agent more freedom to choose its path.
Future, more capable models might work best with fully open-ended approaches. But even with the best current LLMs, you still get better results when you guide them through the problem. If you use LLMs directly for coding, you’ve probably already developed your own workflow — like breaking problems down, providing context strategically, guiding the model through complex reasoning, and backtracking or iterating when needed.
The nice thing about LangGraph’s flexibility is that we can easily recalibrate how structured our flows are when new, more powerful models are released.
Our main flow follows a pattern that you might recognize: first, a context collection node gathers relevant information from the codebase (and external resources
via MCP integration
); next, a planning node breaks down the task into manageable steps; then an execution node generates the actual code; finally, a validation node checks the output against best practices and requirements. When validation fails, the agent loops back to execution with specific feedback rather than starting from scratch.
Coherent interface
When you’re building a complex system, a framework should simplify rather than complicate your work. LangGraph’s API does exactly that.
Here’s how a simplified version of our main workflow looks when implemented with LangGraph:
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
workflow = StateGraph(name="coding_assistant")
workflow.add_node("context_collector", collect_relevant_context)
workflow.add_node("task_planner", create_execution_plan)
workflow.add_node("task_executor", execute_plan)
workflow.add_node("validator", validate_output)
# Define flow between nodes
workflow.add_edge("context_collector", "task_planner")
workflow.add_edge("task_planner", "task_executor")
workflow.add_edge("task_executor", "validator")
# Conditional routing based on validation results
workflow.add_conditional_edges(
"validator",
should_revise,
{
True: "task_executor",  # Loop back if revision needed
False: END               # Complete if validation passes
}
)
graph = workflow.compile()
graph.invoke({"user_input": "build me a game like levelsio"})
This declarative approach makes the code almost self-documenting. The workflow definition directly mirrors our conceptual diagram, which makes it easy to reason about and modify.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对物理学家保罗·狄拉克（Paul Dirac）的个性、历史背景及其影响的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• [dctoedt] 分享了关于狄拉克“与众不同”个性的故事，并提到神学家、物理学家转为圣公会牧师的John Polkinghorne曾是狄拉克小组的博士生，强调了狄拉克在科学界的影响力及其个性对后人的吸引力。
• [mdp2021] 提供了狄拉克视频讲座的资源链接，将讨论引向对狄拉克教学资源的分享，而不是其个性或历史背景。
• [dkfmn] 引用奥本海默对费曼的评价，称其为“更人性化的第二个狄拉克”，暗示狄拉克虽然在科学上有巨大贡献，但其个性可能较为孤僻或不同常人。

补充讨论：
• [pm3003] 提到了物理学家Friedrich Hund在二战后东德的经历，特别是获得一双鞋 voucher 的事件，并询问这是否是东德社会主义背景下的典型现象，还是一种更具深意的“隐藏信息”，引发对历史背景的讨论。
• [koolala] 提问关于月球时间与原子钟差异的问题，将讨论引向物理学中的具体科学问题，但未得到直接回应。
• [cubefox] 和 [ndsipa_pomu] 的评论更偏向个人感受和观察，前者享受两位老知识分子对话的氛围，后者则关注狄拉克的口音，带有一定的调侃性质。
• [WhitneyLand] 提出未来在量子力学与广义相对论结合方面的潜在突破，并将其与20世纪20年代的物理学发展类比，暗示未来可能需要像狄拉克那样具有独特洞察力的科学家来推动科学进步。

争议焦点：
• 狄拉克的个性是否“人性化”或“孤僻”成为间接的争议点，[dkfmn] 引用奥本海默的话暗示狄拉克可能因个性不如费曼“人性化”而著称。

总结：讨论围绕狄拉克的个性和科学贡献展开，部分评论分享了资源和故事，另一些则探讨了历史背景或提出了科学问题。争议点主要集中在狄拉克的个性评价上。

主要讨论点：捷克的谷歌地图替代品mapy.cz正在以mapy.com的名义进行品牌重塑，以进入全球市场。

不同观点：
• 观点一：支持并看好mapy.com的全球化发展。  
  - 论据1：mapy.cz在捷克国内已经非常成功，具有良好的用户基础和技术积累，有能力向全球扩展。  
  - 论据2：用户对多样化地图服务有需求，谷歌地图并非唯一选择，mapy.com可能提供不同的功能和更好的用户体验。  

• 观点二：对mapy.com的全球竞争力持怀疑态度。  
  - 论据1：谷歌地图已经占据全球市场的主导地位，用户习惯和品牌认知度极高，mapy.com很难撼动其地位。  
  - 论据2：全球市场对新进入者有较高的技术和营销要求，mapy.com需要投入大量资源才能获得一定的市场份额。  

• 观点三：关注品牌重塑和市场推广策略。  
  - 论据1：mapy.cz更名为mapy.com是一个重要的品牌重塑步骤，但需要有效的市场推广和用户教育才能成功打入国际市场。  
  - 论据2：品牌名称的变化可能导致原有用户的困惑，需要确保过渡期的平稳和品牌一致性。  

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于mapy.com能否在全球市场中取得成功，尤其是在谷歌地图已经非常强势的情况下。  
- 讨论中还提到技术差异和用户体验可能成为mapy.com的竞争优势，但需要通过实际使用来验证。  
- 市场推广和用户习惯的改变被认为是mapy.com面临的主要挑战之一。

data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在代码库中创建新类型的犹豫现象，特别是在Java和Go项目中。作者指出，这种犹豫导致函数使用大量局部变量、多个参数或返回多个结果，以及扩展现有类型而非创建新类型。这种现象可能源于对干扰代码库“整体设计”的恐惧，尤其对初级开发者而言。作者认为，这种想法是荒谬的，当一组值需要一起传递时，创建新类型是合理的。类型系统正是为了将相关信息组织成易于使用的整体。作者建议，即使是处理较小的信息片段，如请求数据，也可以创建新类型，如“CreateSubscriptionRequest”结构体，以简化代码。虽然过度使用新类型会增加认知负担，但适当地使用新类型能使代码更清晰、更易维护。作者鼓励开发者勇敢地创建新类型，不必担心其仅用于单一函数或局部信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对类型的使用及其在编程中的必要性

不同观点：
• DeathArrow：认为在OOP（面向对象编程）中，类型不仅仅是数据的容器，还应包含封装、继承和多态等特性。他质疑过度使用这些原则的必要性，并提出通过不可变记录和静态方法来简化软件逻辑，但其观点遭到管理者的反对。
• beders：强调命名的重要性，指出在Java中每个小东西都需要名字，如果没有合适的名字，可能不需要新类型。他以Clojure为例，说明无需为每个数据结构创建新类型。
• darioush：不完全同意引入新类型，认为新类型意味着新的抽象，这会带来维护成本，尤其是在需求变化时可能导致抽象的破裂，建议遵循开闭原则。
• parpfish：认为将代码视为类型转换能简化维护和测试，命名和结构化变得更系统。
• jt2190：质疑严格数据类型的必要性，特别是在CRUD应用中，客户端和数据库的约束可能已经足够。
• karparov：认为类型的主要目的是区分不同的事物，而不仅仅是将相似的信息分组。
• paulddraper：指出数据库表的数量不必过于担心，DBMS可以处理大量表。
• salmonellaeater：支持使用小型专用类型，如TypeScript中的类型声明，以提高代码的可维护性和测试性，但注意到在Java等语言中的阻力。
• salgernon：认为Java在声明新类型时较为困难，人们期望类型包含一些逻辑，而这并非必需。
• jongjong：不喜类型，认为类型过度细分和命名会使系统复杂化，特别是在业务领域未完全理解时。
• enriquto：支持无类型或单一类型的编程风格，认为这可以带来解放和自由的编程体验。
• teeray：提倡在Go语言中使用方法而不是函数集，以减少结构体作为数据袋的烦恼。

补充讨论：
• joaonmatos：认为随着新语言特性的引入，如Java的记录和值类型，正在超越对类型的恐惧，发展出一种轻量级的纯数据操作语言。

争议焦点：
• 类型的必要性和复杂性之间的平衡，特别是在不同编程语言和应用场景下的适用性。
• 对OOP原则的严格遵循与简化逻辑之间的取舍。
• 新类型引入带来的抽象和维护成本与代码可读性和可测试性之间的权衡。

43403321.article_content:
I found that there’s a slight aversion to creating new types in the codebases I work in. I saw it during my early days while I was working in Java projects, and I see it today in the occasional Go project. Function bodies with lots of local variables, functions that take a large number of arguments or returning a large number of results, extensions to existing types rather than making new ones. It’s a strange phenomenon.
I can’t explain why this is. Maybe it’s a fear of feeling like you’re tampering with the “grand design” of the codebase. This is plausible as it was the feeling I had as a junior dev. Afraid to create new classes in Java thinking that I’m introducing a new concept to the project that others had to deal with going forward. _I can add all the verbs I want, but who am _ I
to introduce a new noun?
This is obviously a ridiculous notion when you think about it for more than a few seconds. If you come up with a concept or a series of values that naturally go together, so much so that you’re carrying them together as a series of arguments through multiple function calls, it’s probably in your interested to make a type for it. That’s what the type system is for: a means of grouping similar bits of information into an easy-to-use whole.
This makes total sense for the application models: the entities to which you’re software’s reason for being hinges on. But I’ve found it useful to make types for the lesser bits of information: requests from handlers passed through to the service layer, for instance. Just now, I’m working on some code that deals with creating subscriptions. I need to carry the office ID, customer ID, price ID, the subscription quantity, the tax settings, and the subscription metadata from the API handler all the way through to the Stripe client. This is less than what the subscription model deals with, but it’s still a pain to carry these six bits of information separately through the unmarshalling logic, the validation logic, and then through to the server.
So what did I do? I made a “CreateSubscriptionRequest” struct, a new type. Yes, it’s not going to be reusable, but who cares? It makes the code and my life simpler. And honestly, I think the whole “object-orientated approach” to software design really screwed up our thinking here. There was this feeling in the zeitgeist that
types and classes are sacred
, and that to create a new one is a privilege bestowed only to the leads, architects, and anyone else that had write access to the UML diagrams. Each type was to be an artefact of design, probably because of how much baggage came from defining a new one: they had to be in a separate file, must have seven different constructors, and the fields must be mediated through the use of getters and setters. And if you need something similar to what you’re working on, you didn’t “copy-and-paste” like some animal; you inherited or composed what was there. Given all this, it’s probably understandable that creating new types felt like a decision with a significant bit of “weight”; and who are you, mere lowly junior developer, to make such a decision to create a type just to make it easier to handle data from your handler?
I think the culture around C and Go have got it right. Need to carry a few things for a single function? Create a new type. Don’t worry that it’s used only for a single function. Don’t worry that it only contains a subset of fields of the model you’re operating on.
1
Now obviously it’s possible to go too far, and start having way too many types than is necessary. Don’t forget that a new type is a bit more cognitive load, as the person maintaining you application will now need to unpack and reference your type when they need to work on it. Just stick with what you need, and make it clear what the purpose of the type is. “CreateSubscriptionRequest” makes it plan that this type only deals with the areas of a code that creates subscriptions, and will probably only make sense through those code paths.
But take it from someone that’s had do deal with codes passing through and returning several values of strings, ints, and bools through a series of function calls: a single struct value is much easier to work with. All it takes is the courage for someone to say “yes,
that
should be a type.”
Don’t be afraid for that someone to be you.
In fact, that might actually better than using the model type and adding “this field is ignored, that field must be zero, etc. etc.” in the function docs.
↩︎

data.title: "Data" Sucks
data.author: JohnScolaro
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了编程中变量命名的重要性，特别指出了使用"data"作为变量名的问题。作者认为"data"是一个糟糕的变量名，因为它的意义过于宽泛，无法明确表示变量具体代表什么。它是一个不可变名词，像"sheep"一样，无法判断是否可迭代。文章通过多个Python代码示例展示了使用"data"作为变量名导致的困惑，即使在有类型提示的情况下，仍可能让人不解。作者建议程序员应花时间思考更具描述性的名称，以提高代码可读性和可维护性。总之，避免使用"data"作为变量名，可以促使代码更清晰易懂。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机科学中对数据的理解和抽象层次的争论

不同观点：
• brudgers认为，"data"这个词作为计算术语是不合适的，因为数据和随机值的区别在于结构，数据并非随机值。如果它是随机的，就不是数据；如果是数据，就不是随机的。他引用Micheal Jackson的观点来支持自己的立场。

• ssivark将这一问题与Alan Kay和Rich Hickey之间关于裸数据和对象的争论联系起来。对象封装数据并允许解释和交互，而裸数据则不具备这种特性。这一观点强调了数据和对象在计算中不同的角色和抽象层次。

• Rucadi提出"buffer"也是一个候选的抽象层，暗示在不同场景下，可能存在其他更合适的术语来描述数据结构。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了历史背景（"ye olden days"）和过去的争论（如Alan Kay和Rich Hickey的讨论），表明对数据抽象的理解是一个长期存在的议题。
• 提到了具体人物（Micheal Jackson和Alan Kay等）的观点，显示出这些讨论背后有理论和经验的支持。
• 争议的焦点在于数据作为计算中的基本概念，其抽象层次和定义是否准确，以及是否需要通过其他结构（如对象或buffer）来更好地表达数据的意义和功能。

43452184.article_content:
'Data' sucks
March 23, 2025
One of the
two hard things
about programming is naming things, and as programmers we spend a fair bit of time thinking about what we name different 'things'. Having a consistently good naming scheme across a large codebase can significantly speed up development, and having confusing names will slow it down.
Let's say the "badness" of a variable name is: "how badly named something is" multiplied by "how often you see the bad name". I think the worst variable name in all of programming is the word "data".
Why it sucks:
It doesn't mean anything. Everything is data.
I guarantee you can think of a better name. You're being lazy.
It is an
invariable noun
. Like the word "sheep", it could mean one sheep, or many sheep. (Some might argue that the singular is "datum" but that's pretty uncommon). So you can't even reason about whether the "data" is iterable or not.
If I run the query "
(data, language:Python
" in GitHub across all public repos, we can look at some nice Python examples of functions where "data" is the first arg. Here is the first example:
def
imgcat
(
data, lines=-
1
):
See what I mean? What is data? What type is it? What does the function do? 🤷
Since Python has type hints, and everyone who endeavors to actually write good Python should be using them, let's do ourselves a favour and change our search to "
(data: language:Python
" so it only finds
typed
examples.
async
def
stream_offline
(
data:
dict
):
What's data? I mean, it's a dictionary, but since it's only half typed, and not something strict like a
dict[str, int]
or something, once again, it could technically be anything.
Or this great example!
def
calc_zscore
(
data: np.ndarray
) -> np.ndarray:
"""
计算数据的z分数。
Nice, "data" is actually a numpy array! A strict type! However,
np.ndarray
s are actually quite spicy multi-dimensional containers, so you usually want to specify what sort of data array you're expecting unless a "z-score" is something that applies to all
ndarrays
regardless of size and dimensionality. What does this function do anyway? Let's translate the comment using ChatGPT:
I don't know what I expected.
Let's say we have a great example like the following.
from
dataclasses
import
dataclass
@dataclass
class
JohnsSpecialObject
:
bing:
int
bong:
str
def
do_something
(
data: JohnsSpecialObject
) ->
None
:
pass
Now we know exactly what data is! In this case though, wouldn't it make more sense to write:
def
do_something
(
johns_special_object: JohnsSpecialObject
) ->
None
:
pass
instead of calling it "data"?
If I find myself ever using the word "data" in code, I do some more thinking and come up with a better name. Please for everyone's sake, you should do the same.

data.title: Show HN: A terminal emulator in pure PHP
data.author: aarondf
data.article_summary:
**SoloTerm/Screen** 是一个用纯 PHP 编写的终端渲染器，用于在 PHP 应用中创建富文本用户界面，尤其为 **Laravel** 的 **Solo** 提供支持。它专注于解释和渲染带有格式的文本内容，而非处理输入或进程管理。通过虚拟终端缓冲区，它安全地解释 ANSI 转义序列（如光标移动、颜色变化），并在隔离环境中管理屏幕输出，确保复杂操作不会干扰界面其他部分。

**功能特点**：
- 纯 PHP 实现，仅依赖 **Grapheme** 库。
- 支持 ANSI 转义序列，包括光标定位、文本样式和屏幕操作。
- 支持 Unicode/多字节字符和双宽度字符（如 CJK 字符）。
- 管理缓冲区和滚动功能。

**安装**：
通过 Composer 安装，要求 PHP 8.1 及以上版本。

**使用示例**：
创建屏幕对象，写入文本和 ANSI 转义序列，并输出渲染内容。Screen 使用多个缓冲区管理内容和样式，支持复杂的光标操作和文本样式。

该库最初为 **Solo** 开发，现已独立，可用于任何需要终端渲染的 PHP 应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个名为"screen"的新项目引发的反馈和命名争议

不同观点：
• [adminm] 对项目命名的质疑，指出在收到大量负面反馈后，项目方仍然坚持使用该名称，且以讽刺语气回复“感谢反馈”。这表明项目方对反馈的处理方式可能存在问题。
• [aarondf] 对反馈表示感谢，并根据反馈修改了文档中的一些术语（如将"emulator"改为"renderer"），但坚持使用"screen"作为项目名称。
• [whalesalad] 强烈反对使用"screen"作为项目名称，指出该名称与已有38年历史的GNU Screen工具重名，容易造成混淆，并提到该项目可能被不当使用（如黑客攻击）。
• [electroly] 对项目的技术细节提出疑问，不确定该项目是交互式终端还是仅为静态结果输出的ANSI渲染器，指出项目缺乏JavaScript来实现交互功能。
• [atarian] 表达了对项目期望的落差，原本期待的是一个由PHP驱动的桌面应用程序，认为这将是一个很酷的实现。
• [mrweasel] 回忆起2001年的类似情况，提到曾因安全问题将一名在Solaris系统上安装PHP控制台的成员踢出项目，暗示对该类项目可能带来的安全风险持保留态度。
• [donatj] 对项目表示兴奋和支持，提到自己曾在十年前尝试过类似项目，并解释了当时的动机是为了对控制代码输出进行测试。
• [MrBuddyCasino] 对项目的输出形式提出疑问，不清楚项目是输出纯文本还是带有样式的HTML。
• [throwaway150] 对项目表示赞赏，但指出项目并非终端仿真器，而是一个终端渲染器，强调了项目定位的区别。
• [cf100clunk] 指出项目名称与GNU Screen工具重名，存在名称冲突问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在项目的名称"screen"上，多个评论指出该名称与已有的GNU Screen工具重名，容易造成混淆。
• 另一个讨论要点是项目的功能定位，部分评论对项目是终端渲染器而非终端仿真器提出了澄清和建议。
• 有评论对项目的技术实现细节提出疑问，如是否为交互式终端、输出形式等。
• 部分评论对项目的潜在用途和安全风险表达了担忧。

总结：评论中对项目名称的争议较大，同时也有对项目功能和技术细节的讨论与澄清。

Solo Screen
Screen is a terminal renderer written in pure PHP. It powers
Solo for Laravel
and
can be used to build rich text-based user interfaces in any PHP application.
Note
Screen is a library intended to be integrated into PHP applications. It is not a standalone terminal application.
About terminal renderers
A terminal renderer processes text and ANSI escape sequences to create a virtual representation of terminal output.
Unlike a full terminal emulator, Screen focuses specifically on correctly interpreting and rendering text content with
formatting rather than handling input, interactive sessions, or process management.
Terminal renderers interpret escape sequences to:
Track cursor position
Apply text colors and styles (bold, underline, etc.)
Manage screen content
Handle special character sets
Generate a final rendered output
Screen implements this functionality in pure PHP, allowing developers to build terminal user interfaces without relying
on external dependencies or native code.
Why this exists
Screen was originally created to solve a specific problem in
Solo for Laravel
.
Solo provides a TUI (Text User Interface) that runs multiple processes simultaneously in separate panels, similar to
tmux. However, when these processes output ANSI escape codes for cursor movement and screen manipulation, they could
potentially "break out" of their visual containers and interfere with other parts of the interface.
To solve this problem, Screen creates a virtual terminal buffer where:
All ANSI operations (cursor movements, color changes, screen clears) are safely interpreted within an isolated
environment
The final rendered state is captured after all operations are processed
Only the final visual output is displayed to the user's terminal
This approach provides complete control over how terminal output is rendered, ensuring that complex ANSI operations stay
contained within their designated areas. While initially built for Solo, Screen has evolved into a standalone library
that can be used in any PHP application requiring terminal rendering.
Features
Pure PHP Implementation
: Only one dependency (
Grapheme
, another Solo
library)
Comprehensive ANSI Support
: Handles cursor positioning, text styling, and screen manipulation
Unicode/Multibyte Support
: Properly handles UTF-8 characters including emojis and wide characters
Buffer Management
: Maintains separate buffers for text content and styling
Character Width Handling
: Correctly calculates display width for CJK and other double-width characters
Scrolling
: Support for vertical scrolling with proper content management
Installation
Install via Composer:
composer require soloterm/screen
Requirements
PHP 8.1 or higher
mbstring extension

43438797.article_summary:
**SoloTerm/Screen** 是一个用纯 PHP 编写的终端渲染器，用于在 PHP 应用中创建富文本用户界面，尤其为 **Laravel** 的 **Solo** 提供支持。它专注于解释和渲染带有格式的文本内容，而非处理输入或进程管理。通过虚拟终端缓冲区，它安全地解释 ANSI 转义序列（如光标移动、颜色变化），并在隔离环境中管理屏幕输出，确保复杂操作不会干扰界面其他部分。

**功能特点**：
- 纯 PHP 实现，仅依赖 **Grapheme** 库。
- 支持 ANSI 转义序列，包括光标定位、文本样式和屏幕操作。
- 支持 Unicode/多字节字符和双宽度字符（如 CJK 字符）。
- 管理缓冲区和滚动功能。

**安装**：
通过 Composer 安装，要求 PHP 8.1 及以上版本。

**使用示例**：
创建屏幕对象，写入文本和 ANSI 转义序列，并输出渲染内容。Screen 使用多个缓冲区管理内容和样式，支持复杂的光标操作和文本样式。

该库最初为 **Solo** 开发，现已独立，可用于任何需要终端渲染的 PHP 应用。

data.title: The Vectrex Computer
data.author: erickhill
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者多年来寻找一本关于未发布的Vectrex计算机的杂志文章的经历。Vectrex是一款游戏机，曾宣布将推出一个计算机附加组件，但最终未实现。作者因病在家，将《Electronic Games》杂志逐期下载并转换为可搜索文本，最终找到了这篇描述Vectrex计算机的文章。文章提到，该计算机附件包括一个65键键盘、16K ROM和16K RAM，并使用"wafer-tape"存储技术，提供128K存储空间，以及五款计划于1984年初发布的软件。尽管最终未能实现，但文章和相关图片的重现让作者感到欣慰。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vectrex游戏机及其相关技术（包括其矢量显示技术）的历史、技术特点、市场表现和现代应用。

不同观点：
• [ChuckMcM] 对Vectrex持积极态度，表示自己曾拥有所有卡带和外设，并提到相关的Steve Ciarcia的矢量显示项目，提供了相关的扫描文档链接。
• [gcanyon] 认为Vectrex很有趣，但指出其矢量显示技术有限，只能绘制有限的线条，导致其未能取得更大成功。
• [bsenftner] 分享了自己在Vectrex发明者Jay Smith公司工作的经历，提到参与开发PlayStation 1游戏和Tiger Woods PGA Golf游戏。
• [leytdk] 提到自己拥有一个经过改装的Vectrex，使用Raspberry Pi Zero驱动外设和显示。
• [NikkiA] 讨论了Vectrex的存储设备，推测其基于Exatron Stringy Floppy技术，并提到了不同公司销售的磁带格式。
• [wsintra2022] 对Vectrex的技术限制和其未能在市场上取得成功的原因表示好奇。
• [thomassmith65] 指出目前没有面向现代计算机的消费级矢量显示器，并提到自己曾进行过相关搜索。
• [gedy] 曾拥有过Vectrex，但已出售，现在仍保留其光笔，询问是否有复古硬件爱好者需要。
• [ndsipa_pomu] 提到在eBay上看到售价近400英镑的Vectrex，但认为没有足够的理由购买。
• [anthk] 认为使用6809处理器进行矢量图形编程非常简单，只需追踪X和Y坐标。
• [TMWNN] 关心Vectrex的矢量显示是否会对眼睛造成伤害。

补充讨论：
• Vectrex的技术特点和限制：包括其矢量显示只能绘制有限线条的问题。
• Vectrex的市场表现：讨论了其未能广泛成功的原因。
• Vectrex的现代应用：如改装和使用现代硬件驱动。
• Vectrex的历史和相关人物：包括发明者Jay Smith及其公司对后续游戏开发的影响。
• 对Vectrex的怀旧情感：如用户对其过去拥有的经历和现在保留的配件。
• 对Vectrex健康影响的关注：如矢量显示是否会对眼睛造成伤害。

争议焦点：
• Vectrex矢量显示技术的实际表现和市场失败的原因：一些用户认为其技术限制是主要原因，而另一些用户对其怀旧并认为其有趣。

If you're a Vectrex fan, be prepared to mourn what never came to be…
Since I have nothing better to do as I get over an annoying head cold, I've been lying in bed today downloading every issue of
Electronic Games
magazine and converting each one into OCR searchable text. For decades I've had this nagging memory of a
Vectrex computer
announcement that never made it to production, and I was convinced it was from that publication. I owned a Vectrex at the time and would scour the game magazines for any tiny shred of news they might provide about my system. To their credit they seemed to bend over backwards to mention when a new Vectrex game hit store shelves, it just didn't happen that often enough for the Vectrex. I was usually lucky to find a couple inches of text per issue, and these were over 100 pages long each month.
But I remember reading about this supposed computer "add-on" and that the article was actually more than just a blurb and had some images. I never forgot about it. But, all these decades later I was never able to find that announcement. Every few years I'd look around and give up. I honestly started to wonder recently if I'd invented the memory.
Some of the magazine scans on Archive.org are giant unsearchable image-based PDFs so not even Google could see inside them. So, today I started to download issues one at a time, convert them to 600 dpi for OCR scanning in Adobe Acrobat and started searching for "vectrex". Over, and over, and over. Amazing what illness can spawn sometimes.
After a few hours I FOUND IT. AFTER ALL THESE YEARS!!!
Behold (in text) - the mythological
Vectrex Computer
. Supposedly it even had 5 titles ready to ship in early 1984!
Both the light pen and goggles mentioned in the article were in fact produced and sold for a brief time.
Since not everyone can see images, here is the text that matters from the article:
Believe it or not, the Vectrex stand-alone unit can now be transformed into a home computer!
With the assistance of a new keyboard developed by General Consumer Electronics, the plug-in adds 16K ROM and 16K RAM to the unit, and even incorporates a 65-key typewriter-style keyboard. Software for the computer is made on wafer-tapes, providing for 128K bytes of storage. BASIC's built into the system, and the keyboard is just the first step toward a word processor that'll be introduced in early 1984.
Five cartridges for the 1983 computer include:
The Sound Studio, a music composition aid
Exploring the Solar System
Create-A-Game/Maze, which teaches the user to program his very own video-entertainment
Basic Animation Domination
Basic Science, a game teaching the fundamental concepts of physics
A 65-key keyboard would have been one less key than a Commodore 64. I have no idea what "wafer-tape" storage is, but 128K storage sounds pretty interesting for the timeframe. A typical 5.25" floppy disk could hold ~170KB per side and a datasette cassette could hold about 100KB per side.
The Vectrex has 1KB of RAM and 8KB of ROM. So this computer would have beefed it up to a knee-buckling 17KB of RAM. That seems a little light given the fact the C64 and Atari 800xl were already on the market with 64KB. Regardless, the games the Vectrex had already had impressive visuals and sound even with such meager system stats thanks to cartridge storage, so who knows what may have been possible?
I remember being so excited as a kid when I read that news. Sad it never came to pass, but I'm really glad I finally rediscovered the article and it wasn't a human intelligence (HI) hallucination!

Since posting this (and it kind of blowing up) someone shared with me two un-sourced images which appear to be photographic evidence of a Vectrex computer prototype.
An actual full-color photo of what appears to be a physical Vectrex computer prototype.
Very interesting albeit grainy photography of the Vectrex Computer. It appears so show the controllers being plugged into the right side of the machine rather than draping cables over the keyboard. It also seems to have some sort of "mega cartridge" which presumably is the computer interface.
Note how there is a Vectrex logo to the right of the spacebar. It's so wide it actually makes the spacebar look off-centered and a bit awkward.
Fascinating stuff! If I can discover the source of these additional photos I'll update/credit things accordingly.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲数字基础设施创新项目的年龄限制及其合理性

不同观点：
• [jamesblonde] 认为该项目的要求局限于25岁以下的年轻人是不合理的。他指出，数字基础设施的创新需要资本和经验，而非仅仅开发应用程序。他还质疑该项目有跟风"欧洲创新"潮流的嫌疑。

• [Kezzo] 对25岁的年龄限制提出疑问，认为大多数有创新能力的人通常在25岁以上，因为他们需要时间积累行业经验以发现创新机会。不过，Kezzo在查阅FAQ后理解了项目方的意图，即鼓励年轻一代承担更多风险，使创业精神在欧洲文化中更被接受。但他仍然认为，如果项目聚焦于年轻人，就不应该被称为"欧洲项目"。

• [ulfw] 表示自己已经超过25岁，因此无法参与该项目，并对这种年龄限制表示不满，认为这种限制排除了许多有经验和创新能力的人。

• [ivewonyoung] 简单表达了对25岁年龄限制的惊讶和不解。

补充讨论：
• 项目方的解释指出，该项目旨在填补风险投资对年轻创业者支持的空白，虽然风险较高，但他们希望通过这个项目改变欧洲创业者的形象。
• 争议焦点在于年龄限制是否合理，部分评论者认为创新和创业需要经验和资本，而非仅凭年轻和冒险精神。
• 项目的名称"Project Europe"也被质疑，因为其年龄限制使得项目的广泛性受到影响，部分评论者认为名称与实际目标不符。

总结：评论主要围绕年龄限制的合理性及其对项目广泛性的影响展开讨论，部分评论者支持项目鼓励年轻创业者的初衷，但质疑其命名和范围。

• [Kezzo] 对25岁的年龄限制提出疑问，认为大多数有创新能力的人通常在25岁以上，因为他们需要时间积累行业经验以发现创新机会。不过，Kezzo在查阅FAQ后理解了项目方的意图，即鼓励年轻一代承担更多风险，使创业精神在欧洲文化中更被接受。但他仍然认为，如果项目聚焦于年轻人，就不应该被称为"欧洲项目"。

• [ulfw] 表示自己已经超过25岁，因此无法参与该项目，并对这种年龄限制表示不满，认为这种限制排除了许多有经验和创新能力的人。

• [ivewonyoung] 简单表达了对25岁年龄限制的惊讶和不解。

补充讨论：
• 项目方的解释指出，该项目旨在填补风险投资对年轻创业者支持的空白，虽然风险较高，但他们希望通过这个项目改变欧洲创业者的形象。
• 争议焦点在于年龄限制是否合理，部分评论者认为创新和创业需要经验和资本，而非仅凭年轻和冒险精神。
• 项目的名称"Project Europe"也被质疑，因为其年龄限制使得项目的广泛性受到影响，部分评论者认为名称与实际目标不符。

总结：评论主要围绕年龄限制的合理性及其对项目广泛性的影响展开讨论，部分评论者支持项目鼓励年轻创业者的初衷，但质疑其命名和范围。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于20世纪中期医疗伦理的历史背景及其演变，以及宗教机构（特别是基督复临安息日会）在社会、道德问题上的立场变化。

不同观点：
• [mullingitover的观点] 认为基督复临安息日会（Adventist church）已经偏离了其最初的道德立场，尤其是在堕胎和疫苗问题上的态度发生了显著变化。他提到自己小时候在安息日会的经历与现在的教会形成了鲜明对比，如今的教会在许多问题上与右翼福音派立场相似，失去了原本的独特性。他批评了现代教会成员在堕胎和疫苗等问题上的强硬保守立场。

• [aredox的观点] 讨论了20世纪中期在医学实验中不道德行为的普遍性，指出当时有些实验常以“当时的普遍做法”为借口而忽视患者的知情同意。与此同时，同一时期也有人坚持遵循适当的伦理程序。aredox将这种现象类比为历史上奴隶制盛行时，也有很多人对奴隶制感到厌恶。

补充讨论：
• [mullingitover] 提到了自己从安息日会学校转到福音派学校的经历，强调了福音派学校在堕胎问题上的强硬教育以及当时反堕胎运动的策略。他还指出安息日会医院曾允许进行堕胎手术，这与今天的教会立场形成鲜明对比。

• [aredox] 则聚焦于历史背景下的医学伦理问题，认为即使在某些不道德行为普遍存在的时代，也有部分人坚持伦理标准，这与[mullingitover]对安息日会道德立场变化的观察形成了有趣的对比。

争议焦点：
• 基督复临安息日会是否在道德立场上发生了根本性的转变，以及这种转变是否合理。
• 现代教会成员在社会问题上的保守立场是否与其历史相符。

总结：讨论围绕宗教机构在社会和道德问题上的立场变化以及历史背景下医疗伦理的不同表现展开，涉及教会历史、堕胎、疫苗等具体问题。

主要讨论点：对Delphi等传统UI开发工具与现代开发工具的比较及其实用性讨论

不同观点：
• FeistySkink认为Delphi与VB6、WinForms曾是UI开发的巅峰，而现在尤其是web开发变得复杂得多。他指出，现代web开发需要多个不相关的依赖，导致"依赖地狱"，使得项目移植或运行时环境稍有变化就会破坏构建。

• WillAdams提出一个问题，询问上述观点是否适用于Lazarus IDE，暗示可能有其他工具可以提供类似的简便开发体验。

• markus_zhang对Delphi在现代操作系统（Windows 10/11）上的运行情况表示关注，并认为Delphi仍可能适合个人项目使用，表现出对Delphi nostalgic或实用价值的兴趣。

• theamk对博文内容提出质疑，询问是否真的指Borland Delphi 5，特别是其历史版本和功能（如XML支持和ADO数据库），表明对讨论内容的准确性有疑问。

• michael-ax简单表达了对Marco的祝贺，未深入讨论技术细节，但对讨论主题表现出积极态度。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及对Delphi历史版本及其现代适用性的关注，特别是其在当前开发环境中的实用性和技术支持情况。
• 提到了Lazarus IDE作为一个可能的替代工具，扩展了讨论范围，不仅仅是Delphi，还包括其他类似开发环境。
• 争议焦点在于现代web开发的复杂性与传统UI开发工具的简便性对比，以及Delphi等老旧工具在当前技术环境下的适用性和可行性。

data.title: TUI editor and Vim/Neovim alternative
data.author: znano
data.article_summary: Lilly 是一个处于预先测试阶段（pre-alpha）的终端文本编辑器，旨在成为 Vim 和 Neovim 的替代品。其目标是提供基本功能，避免用户依赖复杂的 Lua 插件体系，从而简化使用体验，特别适合开发者使用。当前版本实现了一些基础功能，如分屏、搜索文件、工作区搜索等，但仍有诸多特性待开发。Lilly 强调性能优化，尤其在处理大文件时表现出色，并且完全避免了内存泄漏。用户需使用 V 语言编译器和 Clockwork 工具来构建和运行 Lilly。尽管项目处于早期阶段，但其核心是提供一个功能全面、易于使用且高效的编辑器。

A VIM-Like editor for your terminal (
chat on Discord
)
Important
Lilly is in a pre-alpha state, and only suitable for use by developers.
This editor is technically usable, it is the exclusive editor used to work on itself,
however many features are missing, and there is no guarantee of stable features or a lack of bugs.
Features, bug fixes and issues are welcome.
Our project is focused on the development of a text editor that serves as a practical alternative to Vim and Neovim. The primary aim is to provide users with essential features, eliminating the need to navigate a complex ecosystem of Lua plugins. This approach is intended to be welcoming to users of all experience levels.
Milestone 1: A pre-alpha release
Targets:
Gap buffer to replace string array
Within line visual mode (kind of)
Fix found search result highlighting
Horizontal scrolling
Splits (horizontal + vertical)
Goto def
List of active but not open buffers
Search/Find files
Workspace wide search (ripgrep + roll your own)
How to build (requires the V compiler
https://vlang.io
)
Install the clockwork build tool by executing this command:
v run ./install-clockwork.vsh
Build lilly by executing:
clockwork build
or build and run with
clockwork run
You can see what other tasks are available to run with
clockwork --tasks
The Rationale
Inclusive Functionality
We have set out to create an editor that encompasses the fundamental capabilities expected by users, rendering it a compelling choice as a Vim/Neovim alternative. Our emphasis is on streamlining the editing process without the necessity of configuring numerous plugins – our core features aim to fulfill these needs.
Simplified User Experience
The intricacies of Lua plugins can be daunting for newcomers and even pose a management challenge for seasoned users. Our editor simplifies the user experience by removing the requirement for extensive plugin management. It offers an approachable and intuitive platform, eliminating the complexities that often accompany plugin management.
Performance Enhancement
Our editor is optimized to offer improved performance, particularly when handling extensive files. It is engineered for speed and responsiveness, designed to enhance your editing efficiency.
VIM-Like Experience
We've crafted the editor to deliver a VIM-like experience, preserving the functionalities that VIM users appreciate. The difference lies in the absence of reliance on a multifaceted ecosystem – our editor consolidates these features within a unified framework.
Transition to our text editor to explore an alternative that is rooted in functionality, accessibility, and performance.
Not convinced?
Not a problem, Neovim/VIM are fantastic existing projects and are freely available for you to use today.
