data.title: Goblin.tools: simple, single-task tools to help neurodivergent people with tasks
data.author: ValentineC
data.article_summary: Magic Todo是一款带有特殊功能的待办事项工具。它可以根据任务的"辣度"自动分解任务步骤，辣度越高，分解的步骤越详细。任务会自动分配一个表情符号作为类别，用户可以通过按钮筛选和隐藏已完成的任务。每个任务项都有编辑、删除、添加子任务和估算等功能。用户还可以拖动图标重新排序任务。整个列表的额外操作包括设备同步、多种导出选项、撤销和重做以及批量操作。同步功能使用用户名和密码加密保护待办事项，确保只有用户能访问。同步可能需要几秒时间在不同设备间生效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在帮助神经发散人群（尤其是ADHD患者）进行任务管理和提高生产力方面的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• quibono：认为将ADHD作为身份认同的核心部分可能有些过度泛化。虽然ADHD确实对日常生活有影响，但很多情况下，人们过于频繁地将其作为解释一切行为的理由，甚至在无关紧要的情况下也提起。例如，走神、忘记事情、生气等都被简单归因于ADHD。同时，对一些以ADHD为主题的YouTube内容提出批评，认为它们可能加剧了这种趋势。

• BaudouinVH：作为一名同时患有ADHD和自闭症谱系障碍的人，认为没有任何应用程序能够完全解决注意力分散的问题。建议goblin.tools应针对更广泛的神经典型市场进行营销。

• raybb：希望有一个基于语音的AI工具，可以跟进项目和下一步行动，尤其是在多任务处理时，帮助提醒和追踪任务进展。

• kixiQu：认为LLM在帮助人们克服空白页效应方面非常有用，即使它们出错，也比人们自己开始一项任务要容易。

• stared：作为神经发散者，认为某些网站（即使是善意设计的）因为提供太多选项而显得混乱。更倾向于使用LLM模型来处理下一步行动，而不是扩展列表。

• huvarda：举例说明AI将简单任务（如吃派）过度分解成多个步骤，可能让基本任务显得更复杂和吓人。

• 0000000000100：认为AI工具的自动分解功能不错，但需要改进用户界面，尤其是删除按钮的位置和操作流程。

• senkora：对AI工具的时间估算提出质疑，认为其对简单任务的时间估算过长，建议结合整体任务和子任务的估算进行调整。

• shmageggy：对AI工具作为缺失的执行功能替代品持谨慎乐观态度，但难点在于记住使用它。

• bityard：发现AI工具在处理侮辱性内容时表现出幽默和耐心，认为这是其亮点之一。

• dbreunig：介绍了自己应用中的类似功能，并分享了一个生成步骤的工具链接（steplist.app），指出该工具在执行功能管理中的应用。

• fluidcruft：认为AI工具在任务分解和子任务管理方面表现出色，尤其是在感到不知所措时非常有帮助，希望该功能可以集成到其他任务管理工具中。

• HiPHInch：认为该AI工具是2025年最伟大的AI创意之一，但产品仍有其问题。

• nailer：分享了初次使用体验，认为AI工具在处理复杂任务（如启动网站）时，分解出的子任务过于简单和表面化，没有考虑到用户的具体角色和需求。

补充讨论：
- AI工具在任务分解和时间估算方面的有效性和准确性存在争议，部分用户认为其过度分解任务可能导致任务显得更复杂。
- 用户对AI工具的界面设计和操作流程提出改进建议，尤其是在删除无用子任务时操作不便。
- 神经发散人群对AI工具的需求和使用体验存在差异，部分用户认为其非常有帮助，而另一些用户则认为仍有改进空间。
- 对AI工具在处理复杂任务时需要更多上下文理解和个性化调整提出要求，以提高其实用性。

Magic Todo acts as a standard todo list, with some special sauce. Try the
button and let it automatically come up with the steps you need to accomplish your task!
The 🌶 spiciness level 🌶 gives the tool a hint about how hard or stressful you find the task. The spicier, the more steps it will attempt to break it down into. It's not an exact measure, more a hint to the system.
Top level tasks are automatically assigned a category indicated by an emoji. You can filter your list to one or more categories with the
button. The filter button also allows you to hide all completed items.
Common task tools (edit, remove, add subtask, and estimator) are under the
button on each item. The
icon on the left can be dragged to reorder items to anywhere.
Additional actions for the entire list can be found below it. They include
synchronisation between devices,
export options , undo and redo, and
bulk actions.

43461375.article_summary: Magic Todo是一款带有特殊功能的待办事项工具。它可以根据任务的"辣度"自动分解任务步骤，辣度越高，分解的步骤越详细。任务会自动分配一个表情符号作为类别，用户可以通过按钮筛选和隐藏已完成的任务。每个任务项都有编辑、删除、添加子任务和估算等功能。用户还可以拖动图标重新排序任务。整个列表的额外操作包括设备同步、多种导出选项、撤销和重做以及批量操作。同步功能使用用户名和密码加密保护待办事项，确保只有用户能访问。同步可能需要几秒时间在不同设备间生效。

主要讨论点：AI工具在帮助神经发散人群（尤其是ADHD患者）进行任务管理和提高生产力方面的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• quibono：认为将ADHD作为身份认同的核心部分可能有些过度泛化。虽然ADHD确实对日常生活有影响，但很多情况下，人们过于频繁地将其作为解释一切行为的理由，甚至在无关紧要的情况下也提起。例如，走神、忘记事情、生气等都被简单归因于ADHD。同时，对一些以ADHD为主题的YouTube内容提出批评，认为它们可能加剧了这种趋势。

• BaudouinVH：作为一名同时患有ADHD和自闭症谱系障碍的人，认为没有任何应用程序能够完全解决注意力分散的问题。建议goblin.tools应针对更广泛的神经典型市场进行营销。

• raybb：希望有一个基于语音的AI工具，可以跟进项目和下一步行动，尤其是在多任务处理时，帮助提醒和追踪任务进展。

• kixiQu：认为LLM在帮助人们克服空白页效应方面非常有用，即使它们出错，也比人们自己开始一项任务要容易。

• stared：作为神经发散者，认为某些网站（即使是善意设计的）因为提供太多选项而显得混乱。更倾向于使用LLM模型来处理下一步行动，而不是扩展列表。

• huvarda：举例说明AI将简单任务（如吃派）过度分解成多个步骤，可能让基本任务显得更复杂和吓人。

• 0000000000100：认为AI工具的自动分解功能不错，但需要改进用户界面，尤其是删除按钮的位置和操作流程。

• senkora：对AI工具的时间估算提出质疑，认为其对简单任务的时间估算过长，建议结合整体任务和子任务的估算进行调整。

• shmageggy：对AI工具作为缺失的执行功能替代品持谨慎乐观态度，但难点在于记住使用它。

• bityard：发现AI工具在处理侮辱性内容时表现出幽默和耐心，认为这是其亮点之一。

• dbreunig：介绍了自己应用中的类似功能，并分享了一个生成步骤的工具链接（steplist.app），指出该工具在执行功能管理中的应用。

• fluidcruft：认为AI工具在任务分解和子任务管理方面表现出色，尤其是在感到不知所措时非常有帮助，希望该功能可以集成到其他任务管理工具中。

• HiPHInch：认为该AI工具是2025年最伟大的AI创意之一，但产品仍有其问题。

• nailer：分享了初次使用体验，认为AI工具在处理复杂任务（如启动网站）时，分解出的子任务过于简单和表面化，没有考虑到用户的具体角色和需求。

补充讨论：
- AI工具在任务分解和时间估算方面的有效性和准确性存在争议，部分用户认为其过度分解任务可能导致任务显得更复杂。
- 用户对AI工具的界面设计和操作流程提出改进建议，尤其是在删除无用子任务时操作不便。

- 对AI工具在处理复杂任务时需要更多上下文理解和个性化调整提出要求，以提高其实用性。

主要讨论点：对新闻链接的重发行为及其影响的看法

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：支持重发行为，认为重发能够让更多人看到重要内容。支持者指出，不同时间段的用户群体不同，重发可以让未看到原始帖子的人获得信息。例子：有人提到Reddit等平台上重发是常见做法，能够提高信息覆盖率。

• 第二种观点：反对重发行为，认为这会导致信息过载和内容重复，降低讨论质量。反对者担心频繁的重发会让用户对平台失去兴趣，因为重复内容会让浏览体验变得乏味。例子：有人提到重发可能让用户感觉内容缺乏新意，从而减少参与度。

• 第三种观点：中立态度，认为重发是否有益取决于具体情况。中立者建议，重发的频率和时机需要谨慎选择，以避免负面影响。例子：有用户建议只在原帖沉没或在不同社区中分享时才进行重发。

补充讨论：
• 关于平台规则的讨论：一些用户提到不同平台对重发的规则和限制各不相同，建议遵循平台的社区 guidelines。例子：有的平台会对重发行为进行限制或标注，以示区分。

• 争议的焦点：重发行为是否构成对用户时间的浪费以及对内容质量的影响。部分用户认为重发是有效的信息传播手段，而另一些用户则认为这是对用户注意力的不尊重。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：有用户提到重发行为可能涉及到搜索引擎优化（SEO）和流量获取的策略，这可能影响到内容的传播和排名。例子：在新闻和博客网站上，重发可能帮助内容获得更高的搜索排名。

data.author: rahil627
data.article_summary: PicoRuby 是一个专为单片微控制器设计的微型 Ruby 实现，具有小尺寸和可移植性特点。它在 32 位架构下仅需 256 KB ROM 和 128 KB 或更少的 RAM。PicoRuby 依赖标准 C 库，如 glibc 或 Newlib，并支持 Raspberry Pi Pico 等微控制器板。它提供了 API 文档和演示视频，并依赖于 mruby/c 实现的虚拟机。PicoRuby 可用于构建 PRK Firmware 键盘固件和 PicoRuby WASI WebAssembly 运行时。构建过程需要 C 工具链、git 和 Ruby 3.0 以上版本。项目仍在开发中，遵循 MIT 许可协议，并获得了 Ruby Association Grant Program 的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Picoruby与C语言在微控制器开发中的使用和优劣比较

不同观点：
• jononor认为Picoruby值得进一步研究，同时表达了对MicroPython的喜爱。他指出，与C语言结合开发是一个优势，因为对于微控制器设备，有时确实需要使用低级语言来充分发挥其性能。

• rahil627提到了开发者对C语言的两种不同态度：一些人不喜欢使用C，而另一些人则接受甚至喜爱C语言，特别是在游戏开发者中很常见。rahil627质疑在微控制器如传感器上实现像Ruby这样复杂语言的必要性，并提出“C语言真的那么糟糕吗？”的疑问，但也承认这些实现很酷并仍在维护中。

补充讨论：
• 关于C语言的争议：讨论中反映了对C语言的褒贬不一的态度，有人不喜欢其复杂性，而有人则欣赏其提供的完全控制。
• Picoruby的实用性：jononor对其感兴趣，而rahil627则对其在小型设备上的应用表示怀疑，同时承认其存在价值和维护的努力。
• 开发者偏好：讨论反映了不同开发者对编程语言的个人偏好，以及这些偏好如何影响他们对工具和语言的选择。

争议焦点：C语言在微控制器开发中的优劣以及在小型设备上使用像Ruby这样复杂语言的合理性。

PicoRuby is an alternative mruby implementation which is:
Small foot print
ROM: 256 KB (depending on build config)
RAM: 128 KB or less (depending on app code)
(Figures in 32 bit architecture)
Portable
Depends on only standard C library such as glibc, Newlib or Newlib-nano

C toolchain

command will make three kinds of executable binary

path/to/source.mrb

ruby
command

bin/picoruby path/to/your_script.rb
to run your script

主要讨论点：美国能源市场的监管与 deregulation（去监管化）对可再生能源发展的影响，以及与中国等国家的比较。

不同观点：

• Kragen：认为文章忽略了美国对中国太阳能板和电动汽车的高关税问题，这些关税显著提高了相关技术在美国市场的成本。他还认为文章低估了中国可再生能源发展的速度，提出中国在未来十年可能增加20太瓦（TW）的容量，而非文章中提到的3太瓦。

• Ratherbefuddled：支持去监管化，认为在美国，"监管"往往意味着企业通过政治贿赂来控制市场，而在政治影响力较难发挥作用的地区，监管更有可能推动市场进步。

• Belorn：质疑完全自由的能源市场，指出公民期望政府维持电网的稳定和合理价格。在能源危机中，公民的愤怒往往指向政府而非企业，因此市场化可能会导致政府承担更多成本，而非企业。

• Xbmcuser：提到德州计划对电力市场进行新的监管，暗示当前政府可能在削弱美国企业的成本节约空间。

• Lakis：引用数据指出，德州和加州的储能能力在满足需求方面的差距，认为不能仅看绝对数值，还应关注效率和可再生能源的比例。

• Mmanfrin：质疑文章未提及安然事件（Enron），对去监管化持怀疑态度，认为不能忽视市场过度自由化的风险。

• Nomercy400：担心能源市场的去监管化和私有化可能导致政府失去对市场的控制，特别是在未来20年，可能导致类似其他已经私有化的公共服务领域的问题。

• TheGrimGeometer：认为文章未清晰解释三种能源市场模式（"监管"、"部分去监管"和"去监管"）与太阳能采用率之间的关系，且对德州和TVA的例子提出质疑，指出政治意愿和政策选择对能源转型的重要性。

• Makotech221：对比中国中央集权经济下的可再生能源生产与西方去中心化、私有化的经济模式，认为前者在生产规模上具有明显优势。

• Buckle8017：指出德州电网去监管化时代的市场设计未考虑太阳能和风能的不稳定性，导致可靠但较昂贵的传统能源被挤出市场。他认为应调整合同要求以反映实际情况。

• Throw949999：认为欧盟的可再生能源在没有强力监管和补贴的情况下不具备竞争力，且由于可再生能源的不稳定性，传统能源需要保持待命状态，同时长期投资受限，因此去监管化并非良策。

补充讨论：

• Hannob：提供了一篇关于德州可再生能源建设的文章作为反例，指出可再生能源建设的数量并非唯一重要的指标，减排效果更为关键，而德州在减排方面并不成功。

争议焦点：

1. 去监管化是否能真正推动可再生能源的发展，还是反而会导致市场不稳定和价格波动。
2. 政府和市场在能源转型中的角色分配，特别是政府的监管责任与企业的市场化运作之间的平衡。
3. 高关税和贸易壁垒对可再生能源技术和设备成本的影响程度。
4. 去监管化和市场化是否会导致能源基础设施的私有化，进而削弱政府的控制力并增加未来风险。

43462593.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国能源市场的监管与 deregulation（去监管化）对可再生能源发展的影响，以及与中国等国家的比较。

不同观点：

• Kragen：认为文章忽略了美国对中国太阳能板和电动汽车的高关税问题，这些关税显著提高了相关技术在美国市场的成本。他还认为文章低估了中国可再生能源发展的速度，提出中国在未来十年可能增加20太瓦（TW）的容量，而非文章中提到的3太瓦。

• Ratherbefuddled：支持去监管化，认为在美国，"监管"往往意味着企业通过政治贿赂来控制市场，而在政治影响力较难发挥作用的地区，监管更有可能推动市场进步。

• Belorn：质疑完全自由的能源市场，指出公民期望政府维持电网的稳定和合理价格。在能源危机中，公民的愤怒往往指向政府而非企业，因此市场化可能会导致政府承担更多成本，而非企业。

• Xbmcuser：提到德州计划对电力市场进行新的监管，暗示当前政府可能在削弱美国企业的成本节约空间。

• Lakis：引用数据指出，德州和加州的储能能力在满足需求方面的差距，认为不能仅看绝对数值，还应关注效率和可再生能源的比例。

• Mmanfrin：质疑文章未提及安然事件（Enron），对去监管化持怀疑态度，认为不能忽视市场过度自由化的风险。

• Nomercy400：担心能源市场的去监管化和私有化可能导致政府失去对市场的控制，特别是在未来20年，可能导致类似其他已经私有化的公共服务领域的问题。

• TheGrimGeometer：认为文章未清晰解释三种能源市场模式（"监管"、"部分去监管"和"去监管"）与太阳能采用率之间的关系，且对德州和TVA的例子提出质疑，指出政治意愿和政策选择对能源转型的重要性。

• Makotech221：对比中国中央集权经济下的可再生能源生产与西方去中心化、私有化的经济模式，认为前者在生产规模上具有明显优势。

• Buckle8017：指出德州电网去监管化时代的市场设计未考虑太阳能和风能的不稳定性，导致可靠但较昂贵的传统能源被挤出市场。他认为应调整合同要求以反映实际情况。

• Throw949999：认为欧盟的可再生能源在没有强力监管和补贴的情况下不具备竞争力，且由于可再生能源的不稳定性，传统能源需要保持待命状态，同时长期投资受限，因此去监管化并非良策。

• Hannob：提供了一篇关于德州可再生能源建设的文章作为反例，指出可再生能源建设的数量并非唯一重要的指标，减排效果更为关键，而德州在减排方面并不成功。

1. 去监管化是否能真正推动可再生能源的发展，还是反而会导致市场不稳定和价格波动。

data.title: Can Large Vision Language Models Read Maps Like a Human?
data.author: thinkingemote
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为MapBench的数据集，专门用于评估大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）在基于地图的户外导航任务中的表现。MapBench包含超过1600个从复杂路径寻找场景中提取的地图路径问题，并提供了地图空间场景图（MSSG）作为索引数据结构，用于在自然语言和LVLM生成的结果之间进行转换。实验表明，即便是最先进的LVLM在零样本提示和基于思维链（CoT）的推理框架下，仍然在地图导航任务中面临显著挑战，尤其是在空间推理和结构化决策能力方面存在明显不足。数据集和代码已公开发布。

HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
In this paper, we introduce MapBench-the first dataset specifically designed for human-readable, pixel-based map-based outdoor navigation, curated from complex path finding scenarios. MapBench comprises over 1600 pixel space map path finding problems from 100 diverse maps. In MapBench, LVLMs generate language-based navigation instructions given a map image and a query with beginning and end landmarks. For each map, MapBench provides Map Space Scene Graph (MSSG) as an indexing data structure to convert between natural language and evaluate LVLM-generated results. We demonstrate that MapBench significantly challenges state-of-the-art LVLMs both zero-shot prompting and a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) augmented reasoning framework that decomposes map navigation into sequential cognitive processes. Our evaluation of both open-source and closed-source LVLMs underscores the substantial difficulty posed by MapBench, revealing critical limitations in their spatial reasoning and structured decision-making capabilities. We release all the code and dataset in
this https URL

data.title: Colored Bar Paper Colors
data.author: m_walden
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了用于计算机打印的彩色条纹纸的颜色，主要用于帮助文本对齐。这些纸张在20世纪90年代常见，通常有绿色或蓝色条纹，具体颜色由制造商决定。本文提供了25种颜色示例，以十六进制RGB值表示，如#A9D0BE（绿色）和#A0E0A0（浅绿色）等，并说明如何在现代软件中使用这些颜色作为背景。虽然无法完全模拟交替的白色条纹，但在网页或文档中可以接近这种效果。这些颜色仅为示例，更多选择可通过搜索“柔和颜色”找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：颜色选择及其应用的合理性和用途

不同观点：
• **zokier的观点**：认为文章中颜色的选择显得随意，缺乏关于具体颜色值如何产生的信息。他强调，如果有相关信息的补充，文章会更有价值。

• **nottorp的观点**：解释了文章中的颜色条仅是模拟，不代表真实图像，且颜色的显示效果依赖于显示器的校准。nottorp指出了显示器校准对颜色显示的影响，暗示读者不应期望看到实际印刷颜色。

• **sevensor的观点**：提出颜色可能用于文本编辑器的功能，以提供行导向的强调，而不是结构性强调。虽然不确定这个想法是否可行，但认为这是一个有趣的思考实验。

• **NikkiA的观点**：基于个人经验，提到过去使用的绿条纸的颜色是作为细条纹出现的，因此很难确定哪种颜色最接近。她推测可能是#BB..或#CC的绿色，但感知上由于条纹效应类似于#A9的绿色。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于颜色的准确性和其生成依据，zokier强调需要更多技术细节，而nottorp指出显示器的显示效果可能影响颜色的真实性。
- NikkiA基于个人经验提供了对颜色感知的见解，并指出了条纹效应可能影响颜色的实际感知。
- sevensor从功能应用的角度提出了颜色在文本编辑器中的潜在用途，扩展了讨论的范围。

Colored Bar Paper Colors
By Michael Walden - Created: 2025-03-18 - Updated: 2025-03-20
Introduction
Recently I created an article titled
Retro Monochrome and High Contrast Color Display Palettes
.  That article deals with colors that are used when having bright text on dark backgrounds.  In this article I feature colors to be used as light background colors with dark (usually black) foreground text on top.
Up until the late 1990s it was common to see continuous form tractor-feed paper, for use with computer printers, with colored bars on it that facilitated easy following of lines of text across the width of the printed page.  Generally, it was common to see green bar paper and blue bar paper available for purchase.  There may have been other colors, but not widely sold.  The exact shade of color (blue or green) was not standardized and I believe was left up to the paper manufacturer to determine.
This page has simulations of colored bar papers which are not meant to mislead you into thinking they are real images.  They are just here to illustrate what real colored bar papers would look like in various different colors.
Some of these colors were sampled from images of real paper.  I also recorded some of these from simulations I found in the past while visiting web pages or using software.  Others are numerically created by hand, such as #CCFFCC which is an ideal number, as opposed to something like #CDFECB which would likely be sampled from an image.
Most of these color names are general and not to be considered as specific to the exact color shown.
This page does not have an exhaustive collection of colors.  It features only 25 different color examples.  One of those should be sufficient to satisfy your needs.  Many other suitable colors can be found by searching for "pastel colors" on the web.
When configuring software on modern PCs (such as your text editor, email client, etc.) you can use these colors as background colors with black foreground text to only 50% mimic the colored bar papers shown below.  This is because you are not able to configure software to have a background color from below bar and then alternate with a background white bar.  That means you are just left with a solid non-alternating background.
When creating web pages (in HTML, CSS, etc.), word processing documents, or other types of documents (graphics) that have black foreground text information, you can have a background color from below bar alternate with a background white bar to 100% mimic the green bar paper style of presentation.  Note that the alternating of a background color from below bar with a background white bar is usually done in groups of three lines of text in each bar, repeat that as necessary to the end of the document.
The colors are represented as hexadecimal (hex) triplet 24-bit RGB values (#RRGGBB).
Enjoy!

data.title: Thinking Different, Thinking Slowly: LLMs on a PowerPC Mac
data.author: tambourine_man
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在2005年款PowerBook G4上成功运行大型语言模型（LLM）推理的实验过程。这台老式硬件配备1.5GHz处理器、1GB内存和32位地址空间。作者借鉴了Andrej Karpathy的llama2.c项目，通过C语言实现了Llama2模型的推理，并对其进行改进，创建了名为"ullm"的项目。作者对代码进行了多项优化，包括改进系统函数的封装、引入状态返回机制、组织成库结构并提供公开API以支持单元测试。最终，通过回调函数处理输出，实现了对整个推理流程的集成测试，成功让老旧硬件运行现代AI模型。

data.article_summary: 本文讲述了一位被称为Tim Mackinnon的程序员，虽然根据生产力指标他的贡献为零，因为他从不认领任务，但实际上他对团队有巨大价值。Tim通过与团队成员结对编程，帮助他人解决问题，提升了整个团队的效率和凝聚力。管理层最初想根据生产力指标辞退他，但在作者解释了Tim的真正贡献后，决定保留他，并放弃了个体生产力指标，转向团队整体问责制。文章强调，在复杂系统中，个体贡献难以衡量，应关注团队整体对业务的影响。作者还推荐有机会的话应与Tim合作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发者生产力衡量方式及其争议

不同观点：
• **反对生产力衡量的观点**：
  - morsecodist认为衡量个体开发者的生产力是荒谬的，因为开发过程中的变量太多。单纯衡量故事点或代码行数反而可能鼓励无意义的工作。真正的价值在于业务成果，但这些难以归因到个人。
  - NalNezumi分享了一个失败案例，说明不当的生产力衡量（如OKR）会导致团队成员不愿合作，影响整体效率。

• **支持生产力衡量有其价值的观点**：
  - JohnMakin认为生产力指标并非完全无用，比如通过PR和Jira票的关联可以获得有用的信息。即使这些数据可能被操纵，但仍可作为参考。
  - crazygringo认为Tim的情况反映的是角色和指标分配不当，而不是指标本身的失败。应该通过调整角色和任务分配来解决问题。

• **关于Tim角色的讨论**：
  - dmoy和lapcat认为团队中需要像Tim这样的人，但Tim的帮助应合理分配，且他应承担一些个体工作以保持团队平衡。
  - iamleppert认为如果团队过度依赖某个人来解决问题，可能反映出代码和流程的缺陷。

• **对具体衡量方法的建议与反思**：
  - bsindcatr列举了多种无法衡量开发者是否“优秀”的指标，强调应关注对业务和团队的实际贡献。
  - andix指出通过故事点衡量开发者生产力的弊端，分享了类似案例。
  - croes认为管理者对团队成员的了解才是关键指标。
  - mjburgess提出“教育性代码”理念，认为代码应教导其读者如何思考问题，而不仅仅是实现功能。

• **对管理角色的质疑**：
  - franktankbank质疑管理者的角色和作用，认为Tim实际上在履行管理的职责。
  - PeterStuer强调非技术管理者在处理此类问题时的失败，指出信任了解业务的人做决策的重要性。

补充讨论：
- Waterluvian和_fat_santa关注了支持性角色的量化难题，认为某些贡献难以通过数据衡量，需依赖管理者的判断。
- 总体而言，评论中对生产力衡量的争议焦点在于其可行性和对团队合作的潜在影响。许多评论者建议更关注业务成果和团队整体表现，而非单一指标。

43452649.article_content:
2 Sep 2023
4 mins
productivity
metrics
The great thing about measuring developer productivity is that you can quickly identify the bad programmers. I want to tell you about the worst programmer I know, and why I fought to keep him in the team.
A few years ago I wrote a Twitter/X thread about
the best programmer I know
, which I should write up as a blog post. It seems only fair to tell you about the worst one too. His name is
Tim Mackinnon
and I want you to know how
measurably unproductive
he is.
We were working for a well-known software consultancy at a Big Bank that decided to introduce individual performance metrics, “for appraisal and personal development purposes”. This was cascaded through the organisation, and landed in our team in terms of story points delivered. This was after some considered discussion from the department manager, who knew you shouldn’t measure things like lines of code or bugs found, because people can easily game these.
Source:
http://dilbert.com/strip/1995-11-13
Instead we would measure stories delivered, or it may have been story points (it turns out it
doesn’t matter
), because these represented business value. We were using something like Jira, and people would put their name against stories, which made it super easy to generate these productivity metrics.
Which brings me to Tim. Tim’s score was consistently zero. Zero! Not just low, or trending downwards, but literally zero. Week after week, iteration after iteration. Zero points for Tim.
Well Tim clearly had to go. This was the manager’s conclusion, and he asked me to make the necessary arrangements to have Tim removed and replaced by someone who actually delivered, you know, stories.
And I flatly refused. It wasn’t even a hard decision for me, I just said no.
You see, the reason that Tim’s productivity score was zero, was that
he never signed up for any stories
. Instead he would spend his day pairing with different teammates. With less experienced developers he would patiently let them drive whilst nudging them towards a solution. He would not crowd them or railroad them, but let them take the time to learn whilst carefully crafting moments of insight and learning, often as
Socratic questions
, what ifs, how elses.
With seniors it was more like co-creating or sparring; bringing different worldviews to bear on a problem, to produce something better than either of us would have thought of on our own. Tim is a heck of a programmer, and you always learn something pairing with him.
Tim wasn’t delivering software; Tim was delivering a team that was delivering software. The entire team became more effective, more productive, more aligned, more idiomatic, more
fun
, because Tim was in the team.
I explained all this to the manager and invited him to come by and observe us working from time to time. Whenever he popped by, he would see Tim sitting with someone different, working on “their” thing, and you could be sure that the quality of that thing would be significantly better, and the time to value significantly lower—yes, you can have better and faster and cheaper, it just takes discipline—than when Tim wasn’t pairing with people.
In the end we kept Tim, and we quietly dropped the individual productivity metrics in favour of team accountability, where we tracked—and celebrated—the business impact we were delivering to the organisation as a high-performing unit.
tl;dr
Measure productivity by all means—I’m all for accountability—ideally as tangible business impact expressed in dollars saved, generated, or protected. This is usually hard, so proxy business metrics are fine too.
Just don’t try to measure the individual contribution of a unit in a complex adaptive system, because the premise of the question is flawed.
DORA metrics, for example, are about how the system of work works, whether as Westrum culture indicators or flow of technical change into production. They measure the engine, not the contribution of individual pistons, because that
makes no sense
.
Also, if you ever get the chance to work with Tim Mackinnon, you should do that.
We can help
your
organisation to go faster —
ask us how

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于存档网页服务（如archive.ph）的有效性和道德性讨论

不同观点：
• 支持使用存档服务：
  - 论据：存档服务有助于保存可能被删除或更改的网页内容，确保信息的长期可访问性。
  - 例子：有用户提到，某些网站可能会因为各种原因下线或更改内容，存档服务可以作为一种备份手段。
  - 论据：存档服务可以绕过付费墙或注册要求，使得更多人可以访问有价值的信息。

• 反对使用存档服务：
  - 论据：未经内容原创者同意而存档网页可能侵犯版权或知识产权。
  - 例子：有用户指出，某些内容提供者可能依赖于付费墙或广告收入，存档服务会损害其商业模式。
  - 论据：存档服务可能会被滥用，例如用于传播过时或错误的信息，误导公众。

• 对存档服务的技术性讨论：
  - 论据：存档服务有时可能无法完整保存网页的所有动态内容或交互功能，导致用户体验不完整。
  - 例子：有用户提到，JavaScript重度依赖的网页在存档后可能无法正常运作。
  - 论据：存档服务的技术限制可能会影响其保存网页的准确性和完整性。

补充讨论：
• 用户提到存档服务的合法性问题，指出在某些司法管辖区，未经许可存档网页可能违反法律。
• 讨论中涉及存档服务的道德责任，有用户认为服务提供者有义务在存档网页上明确标注来源和版权信息。
• 争议的焦点在于存档服务是否在保护公共信息和侵犯知识产权之间取得平衡。

以上是关于存档网页服务的主要不同观点和讨论要点。

data.title: I won't connect my dishwasher to your stupid cloud
data.author: HieronymusBosch
data.article_summary: 作者因旧的GE洗碗机故障不得不购买新机，最终选择了Bosch 500系列。安装过程总体顺利，但发现一些功能（如冲洗循环、延迟启动和节能模式）需要通过应用程序控制，而使用这些功能还需将洗碗机连接到WiFi并注册云账户。作者对此设计感到不满，认为这是不必要的复杂化。此外，作者对比了旧GE机型的问题，如控制面板电力故障和锈蚀，最终决定换新机。尽管Bosch的安装较顺利，但作者对触控感应控制和云需求感到困惑和不便，认为简单的按钮设计更实用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：云连接家电的隐私、安全、可靠性及消费者应对方法

不同观点：
• [Avamander] 认为本地化操作的家电会更好，能够减少延迟、提升隐私和安全，并指出许多厂商的云连接不安全且不可靠，经常出现宕机。他还提到，目前没有好的解决方案，除非通过立法强制要求厂商在产品生命周期结束时开放访问权限。
  
• [pavel_lishin] 表示未来购买家电时可能会先下载说明书，检查是否存在类似问题，以此作为购物决策的依据。

• [mmmlinux] 认为像"消费者报告"这样的评测并不可信，暗示其未充分揭露家电产品在隐私和安全方面的问题。

• [fpauser] 提出简单直接的解决方案，建议直接退货不安全的智能家电。

• [bell-cot] 提出可以通过法律手段解决问题，包括控告产品未如实告知功能需求、不符合ADA（美国残疾人法案）规定以及违反数据安全法规。还建议建立一个网站来曝光那些强制使用云服务的家电产品，帮助消费者避开这些问题产品。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于智能家电的云连接带来的隐私、安全和可靠性问题。
• 不同用户提出的应对方法各异，从技术检测、购物前调查、退货到法律行动和公众曝光。
• 立法和消费者保护被认为是潜在的长远解决方案。

43463200.article_content:
I won't connect my dishwasher to your stupid cloud
This weekend I had to buy a new dishwasher because our old GE died.
I bought a Bosch 500 series because that's what Consumer Reports recommended, and more importantly, I could find one in stock.
After my dad and I got it installed, I went to run a rinse cycle, only to find that
that
, along with features like delayed start and eco mode, require an app.
Not only that, to
use
the app, you have to connect your dishwasher to WiFi, set up a cloud account in something called Home Connect, and then, and only then, can you start using all the features on the dishwasher.
This blog post is a lightly-edited transcript of my latest YouTube video on
Level 2 Jeff
:
I won't connect my dishwasher to your stupid cloud
.
So getting back first to that old GE dishwasher, it was, I don't know, I think that
planned obsolescence
is something that applies to many consumer products today.
Companies know if they design something to last only 5 or 10 years, that means in 5 or 10 years someone's going to have to buy a whole new one.
And on my GE Amana dishwasher, it started having weird power issues, like the controls would just not light up unless I reset the circuit breaker for a few minutes. That started happening more often, and this past Saturday it just wouldn't come on no matter what, even after I tested and re-wired it all the way from the panel up to the dishwasher's internal power connector.
So it was dead.
Next up, I looked at what it took to get a control board. Well...
$299 for a control board
that was 'special order' and might not even fix the problem? That's a non-starter for my $600, 8-year-old dishwasher.
Even if I got it fixed, the front panel was starting to rust out at the hinge points (leaving some metal jaggies that my soon-to-be-crawling 6 month old could slice his fingers on), and other parts of the machine were showing signs of rust/potential future leaks...
It was Saturday night, and for a family of five, a dishwasher is kinda important. We don't have 1.5 hours every night to spend hand-washing dishes (not to mention the water bill!).
So I needed to get a new one, and it's really hard for me to schedule a few hours for my Dad and I to get it done in the middle of the week (plus that's multiple days without a dishwasher!).
So I did some research, and I found Bosch
seemed
to have the best bet for under $1,000, available locally on a Sunday.
Consumer Reports, random Redditors, etc. seemed to have some praises for Bosch—on Reddit many also praised Miele, but I couldn't find any of those available locally. And Consumer Reports especially praised
all
the Bosch units, with them topping all their reliability and customer satisfaction charts!
I remembered five or ten years ago, whenever I had bought my old GE, I remembered Bosch topped the charts too, but back then I settled for GE to save a few bucks...
Installation was (mostly) great!
So I spent a little more this time, hoping for a better experience. And installation was actually great—it was a lot easier to install the Bosch than it was that the GE.
It has a plastic base that slides better on the floor, and there's easier routing of the drain hose, inlet hose, and power wire that makes it less risky when you're pushing the thing into the blind cutout under the counter.
The one weird thing was that whoever like tightened the feet on the bottom at the factory must've used an impact driver or something because they were all practically embedded, and wouldn't budge.
I was turning the little screw on the front that pushes the rear foot down through a little gearing, but the worm gear slipped out and kinda shoved the long rod that connects the front to the back out of place. I had to buy a 10mm hex socket to wiggle the foot loose enough the gearing would actually work.
But once that was done, the rest of the install was seamless. (Thanks especially to some help from my Dad).
First use, encountering the Cloud requirement
So I turned it on, and immediately hated the new touch sensor stuff on it.
The old GE had buttons: you press them in, they click and you know that you pressed a button.
The touch sensor, you kind of touch it and the firmware—like this new dishwasher actually takes time to boot up! I had to reset it like three times and my wife meanwhile was like laughing at me like look at this guy who does tech stuff and he can't even figure out how to change the cycle on it.
That took about five minutes, sadly.
But eventually I pulled out the manual book because I was like... "this is actually confusing."
It should be like: I touch the button and it changes to that mode! But that was not how it was working.
I wanted to run just a rinse cycle to make sure the water would go in, the water would pump out through the sump, and everything worked post-install.
But I couldn't find a way to do a rinse cycle on the control panel.
So I looked in the manual and found this note:
It says options with an asterisk—including Rinse, Ma

data.author: nosferalatu123
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何对变换 \(T\) 进行平滑插值，以使点 \(x\) 从初始位置沿路径移动到由 \(T\) 变换后的位置。关键在于通过变换的指数和对数来计算随时间变化的变换 \(T(t)\)，从而实现插值。

具体步骤如下：

1. **定义随时间变化的变换**：设 \(T(t) = T^t\)，其中 \(T(0)\) 是单位变换 \(I\)，\(T(1) = T\)。
2. **使用矩阵指数和对数**：通过 \(T^t = e^{log(T) \cdot t}\) 计算 \(T(t)\)。
3. **插值点位置**：点 \(x\) 在时间 \(t\) 的位置为 \(x(t) = e^{log(T) \cdot t} \cdot x(0)\)。
4. **计算速度（导数）**：点 \(x\) 在时间 \(t\) 的速度为 \(\dfrac{d}{dt}x(t) = log(T) \cdot e^{log(T) \cdot t} \cdot x(0)\)，即 \(log(T)\) 乘以插值变换作用在初始位置上的结果。

对数变换 \(log(T)\) 可以看作是变换的向量场，它表示每个点的速度（切向量），并且不随时间变化。通过这些公式，可以实现变换的平滑插值和速度计算。

文章还提供了一个交互示例，演示如何通过操纵工具来改变变换，并观察向量场的变化和插值路径。

43430498.article_content:
Given a transform
\(T\)
and a point x, we can find the transformed point with
\(T * x\)
. But what if we want to smoothly interpolate
\(T\)
so it moves
\(x\)
along the path from its initial position to its position transformed by
\(T\)
?
What we want to find is the point
\(x\)
at time
\(t\)
:
\(x(t) = T(t) * x(0)\)
where
\(x(0)\)
is the point’s initial position, and
\(T(t)\)
is the transform at time
\(t\)
. Since we have only a single transform
\(T\)
, we need to find a way to interpolate it over time.
One way to accomplish this is to raise
\(T\)
to the power of
\(t\)
, which can be done using the exponential and logarithm of the transform. Interestingly, the logarithm of a transform can also be used to easily find the velocity of a point
\(x\)
in space: the velocity vector (also called the tangent vector) is just
\(log(T) * x\)
. This blog post shows the relationship between the logarithm and velocity.
Example
Check out this interactive example to see how the vector field changes as you manipulate the gizmo to translate and rotate the transform. The vector field represents the velocity vector at each point in space during the transformation.
As you move the gizmo, you’ll notice a white curve that traces the path from the origin to the gizmo’s transform. Along this curve, you’ll see the interpolated transform as it travels from the origin to the gizmo. As you can see, the interpolation follows the flow of the velocity vector field. The applet’s code is using the exponential and logarithm of the transform to compute the curve, interpolated transform, and vector field.
The source code for the applet can be found
here
, which includes an implementation of closed-form log() and exp() for rigid body transforms.
Next, I’ll describe how to compute the interpolated transform and the velocity vector field you see in this example.
What’s
\(T(t)\)
?
We have
\(T\)
, but not
\(T(t)\)
, which changes with time. Assuming that multiplying two transforms represents the composition of those transforms, we can find
\(T(t)\)
by saying
\(T(0) = I\)
(the identity transform)
\(T(1) = T\)
\(T(2) = T * T\)
\(T(3) = T * T * T\)
More generally, we can find
\(T\)
at any time by saying
\(T(t) = T^t\)
.
The above trick is from a blog post by Fabian Giesen
here
but works for any transform that uses multiplication for composition.
Now that we know
\(T(t) = T^t\)
, the original equation can be rearranged to
\(x(t) = T^t * x(0)\)
.
What’s
\(T^t\)
?
To compute
\(T^t\)
, we need to use the matrix exponential and matrix logarithm.
Let’s start with two facts about a matrix X:
\(e^{log(X)} = X\)
and
\(log(X^y) = log(X) * y\)
.
Put together, we can say that
\(T^t = e^{log(T^t)} = e^{log(T)*t}\)
which we can plug into the earlier equation, giving us
\(x(t) = e^{log(T) * t} * x(0)\)
.
This says that to find the point x at time t, find the transform at time t using
\(e^{log(T) * t}\)
, and use that to transform the point at its initial position (at time 0).
What’s the derivative?
In calculus, we learned that
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}e^{a t} = a e^{a t}\)
which holds true for matrices as well:
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}e^{A t} = A e^{A t}\)
This relationship is explained in more detail in the section
the derivative of the matrix exponential
.
We can use this property to find the derivative of our earlier equation
\(x(t) = e^{log(T)t} x(0)\)
with respect to t:
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}x(t) = log(T) e^{log(T) t} x(0)\)
.
This equation states that to find the first derivative (the velocity vector, also called the tangent vector) of the point at time t, you first transform the point’s initial position
\(x(0)\)
with the interpolated transform
\(e^{log(T)t}\)
and then multiply it by the logarithm of the transform
\(log(T)\)
. This expression follows the right-to-left convention of column vectors, so you would start with the initial position
\(x(0)\)
, then apply the interpolated transform
\(e^{log(T)t}\)
, and finally multiply by the logarithm
\(log(T)\)
.
\(e^{log(T) t}\)
acts as an operator that maps points from their initial position to their new position at time t. The matrix exponential can be thought of as like integration. At time 0,
\(e^{log(T) t}\)
is the identity matrix (
\(e^0=I\)
for matrix exponentials), and at time 1.0,
\(e^{log(T) t}\)
is equal to the original transform matrix T (
\(e^{log(T)}=T\)
).
What’s this all mean?
If we take the equation at the end of “What’s
\(T^t\)
?”
\(x(t) = e^{log(T) t} x(0)\)
and substitute that into the equation at the end of “What’s the derivative?”
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}x(t) = log(T) e^{log(T) t} x(0)\)
,
then we have:
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}x(t) = log(T) x(t)\)
.
This relates the derivative of a moving point to the logarithm of the transformation moving that point.
One way to think of
\(log(T)\)
is as a vector field of tangent vectors for the transformation. In other words, it’s the field of first derivatives. This vector field is independent of time and shows the velocity for every point in space.

data.title: The Trump Administration Accidentally Texted Me Its War Plans
data.author: _tk_
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者在2024年3月11日收到一条来自Signal用户“Michael Waltz”的联系请求，此人自称是特朗普总统的国家安全顾问。随后，作者被加入一个名为“Houthi PC小群”的聊天组，群内成员包括多位据称是美国高级国家安全官员的人，如国务卿、副总统的代表等。作者被告知此群用于协调未来72小时内对也门胡塞武装的行动。在群里，作者收到时任国防部长Pete Hegseth发来的详细作战计划，提前两小时得知美国即将轰炸胡塞目标。作者曾怀疑这些信息可能是假情报或误导性宣传，但最终证实行动确实发生。文章揭示了美国政府在应对胡塞武装问题上的内部沟通和决策过程。

43462783.article_content:
The world found out shortly before 2 p.m. eastern time on March 15 that the United States was bombing Houthi targets across Yemen.
I, however, knew two hours before the first bombs exploded that the attack might be coming. The reason I knew this is that Pete Hegseth, the secretary of defense, had texted me the war plan at 11:44 a.m. The plan included precise information about weapons packages, targets, and timing.
This is going to require some explaining.
The story technically begins shortly after the Hamas invasion of southern Israel, in October 2023. The Houthis—an Iran-backed terrorist organization whose motto is “God is great, death to America, death to Israel, curse on the Jews, victory to Islam”—soon launched attacks on Israel and on international shipping, creating havoc for global trade. Throughout 2024, the Biden administration was ineffective in countering these Houthi attacks; the incoming Trump administration promised a tougher response.
This is where Pete Hegseth and I come in.
On Tuesday, March 11, I received a connection request on Signal from a user identified as Michael Waltz. Signal is an open-source encrypted messaging service popular with journalists and others who seek more privacy than other text-messaging services are capable of delivering. I assumed that the Michael Waltz in question was President Donald Trump’s national security adviser. I did not assume, however, that the request was from the actual Michael Waltz. I have met him in the past, and though I didn’t find it particularly strange that he might be reaching out to me, I did think it somewhat unusual, given the Trump administration’s contentious relationship with journalists—and Trump’s periodic fixation on me specifically. It immediately crossed my mind that someone could be masquerading as Waltz in order to somehow entrap me. It is not at all uncommon these days for nefarious actors to try to induce journalists to share information that could be used against them.
I accepted the connection request, hoping that this was the actual national security adviser, and that he wanted to chat about Ukraine, or Iran, or some other important matter.
Two days later—Thursday—at 4:28 p.m., I received a notice that I was to be included in a Signal chat group. It was called the “Houthi PC small group.”
A message to the group, from “Michael Waltz,” read as follows: “Team – establishing a principles [
sic
] group for coordination on Houthis, particularly for over the next 72 hours. My deputy Alex Wong is pulling together a tiger team at deputies/agency Chief of Staff level following up from the meeting in the Sit Room this morning for action items and will be sending that out later this evening.”
The message continued, “Pls provide the best staff POC from your team for us to coordinate with over the next couple days and over the weekend. Thx.”
The term
principals committee
generally refers to a group of the senior-most national-security officials, including the secretaries of defense, state, and the treasury, as well as the director of the CIA. It should go without saying—but I’ll say it anyway—that I have never been invited to a White House principals-committee meeting, and that, in my many years of reporting on national-security matters, I had never heard of one being convened over a commercial messaging app.
One minute later, a person identified only as “MAR”—the secretary of state is Marco Antonio Rubio—wrote, “Mike Needham for State,” apparently designating the current counselor of the State Department as his representative. At that same moment, a Signal user identified as “JD Vance” wrote, “Andy baker for VP.” One minute after that, “TG” (presumably Tulsi Gabbard, the director of national intelligence, or someone masquerading as her) wrote, “Joe Kent for DNI.” Nine minutes later, “Scott B”—apparently Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, or someone spoofing his identity, wrote, “Dan Katz for Treasury.” At 4:53 p.m., a user called “Pete Hegseth” wrote, “Dan Caldwell for DoD.” And at 6:34 p.m., “Brian” wrote “Brian McCormack for NSC.” One more person responded: “John Ratcliffe” wrote at 5:24 p.m. with the name of a CIA official to be included in the group. I am not publishing that name, because that person is an active intelligence officer.
The principals had apparently assembled. data.title: Landrun: Sandbox any Linux process using Landlock, no root or containers
data.author: Zoup
data.article_summary:
**landrun** 是一个轻量级、安全的 Linux 进程沙箱工具，利用内核中的 Landlock LSM 模块实现无特权进程的限制。相比 firejail，landrun 更轻量、易用，且直接集成在内核中。它支持细粒度的文件系统和网络访问控制，无需 root 权限或容器技术，也不需要配置 SELinux/AppArmor。

**主要特性**：
- 内核级安全，使用 Landlock LSM
- 轻量快速
- 精细目录访问控制（读、写、执行）
- TCP 网络访问控制（绑定、连接）

**安装与使用**：
- 通过 `go install` 快速安装
- 使用不同选项控制文件和网络权限，如 `--ro`（只读）、`--rw`（读写）、`--bind-tcp`（绑定 TCP 端口）等
- 支持指定日志级别和环境变量

**要求**：
- Linux 内核 5.13 及以上（基础功能），6.7 及以上（网络限制）
- Go 1.18 及以上（从源码构建时）

**示例**：
- `landrun --rox /usr/ --ro /path/to/dir ls /path/to/dir`：以只读和执行权限运行命令
- `landrun --bind-tcp 8080 --connect-tcp 80 /usr/bin/my-server`：限制网络访问端口 8080 和 80

补充讨论：
• 关于 `landrun` 的命令行选项命名和用户体验的讨论，特别是对 `--ro` 和 `--exec` 等选项的困惑和改进建议。
• 对 Linux 安全机制（如 Landlock、AppArmor、命名空间）之间的功能比较和应用场景的探讨。
• 关于是否可以在 Linux 上实现类似 macOS 的动态权限授权机制的讨论。
• 对 `landrun` 工具潜在应用场景的讨论，如与 Nix 包管理器的结合使用。

争议焦点：
• 命令行选项的命名和直观性问题，特别是 `--ro` 和 `--exec` 的使用。
• `--best-effort` 选项是否应默认开启，涉及到安全性和用户体验的权衡。

landrun
A lightweight, secure sandbox for running Linux processes using Landlock LSM. Think firejail, but with kernel-level security and minimal overhead.
Linux Landlock is a kernel-native security module that lets unprivileged processes sandbox themselves - but nobody uses it because the API is ... hard!
Landrun is designed to make it practical to sandbox any command with fine-grained filesystem and network access controls. No root. No containers. No SELinux/AppArmor configs.
It's lightweight, auditable, and wraps Landlock v5 features (file access + TCP restrictions).
Features
🔒 Kernel-level security using Landlock LSM
🚀 Lightweight and fast execution
🛡️ Fine-grained access control for directories
🔄 Support for read and write paths
⚡ Path-specific execution permissions
🌐 TCP network access control (binding and connecting)
Demo
Requirements
Linux kernel 5.13 or later with Landlock LSM enabled
Linux kernel 6.7 or later for network restrictions (TCP bind/connect)
Go 1.18 or later (for building from source)
Installation
Quick Install
go install github.com/zouuup/landrun/cmd/landrun@latest
From Source
git clone https://github.com/zouuup/landrun.git
cd
landrun
go build -o landrun cmd/landrun/main.go
sudo cp landrun /usr/local/bin/
Usage
Basic syntax:
landrun [options]
<
command
>
[args...]
Options
--ro <path>
: Allow read-only access to specified path (can be specified multiple times or as comma-separated values)
--rox <path>
: Allow read-only access with execution to specified path (can be specified multiple times or as comma-separated values)
--rw <path>
: Allow read-write access to specified path (can be specified multiple times or as comma-separated values)
--rwx <path>
: Allow read-write access with execution to specified path (can be specified multiple times or as comma-separated values)
--bind-tcp <port>
: Allow binding to specified TCP port (can be specified multiple times or as comma-separated values)
--connect-tcp <port>
: Allow connecting to specified TCP port (can be specified multiple times or as comma-separated values)
--env <var>
: Environment variable to pass to the sandboxed command (format: KEY=VALUE or just KEY to pass current value)
--best-effort
: Use best effort mode, falling back to less restrictive sandbox if necessary [default: disabled]
--log-level <level>
: Set logging level (error, info, debug) [default: "error"]
Important Notes
You must explicitly add the directory to the command you want to run with
--rox
flag
For system commands, you typically need to include
/usr/bin
,
/usr/lib
, and other system directories
Use
--rwx
for directories where you need both write access and the ability to execute files
Network restrictions require Linux kernel 6.7 or later with Landlock ABI v4
By default, no environment variables are passed to the sandboxed command. Use
--env
to explicitly pass environment variables
The
--best-effort
flag allows graceful degradation on older kernels that don't support all requested restrictions
Paths can be specified either using multiple flags or as comma-separated values (e.g.,
--ro /usr,/lib,/home
)
Environment Variables
LANDRUN_LOG_LEVEL
: Set logging level (error, info, debug)
Examples
Run a command with read-only access to a directory:
landrun --rox /usr/ --ro /path/to/dir ls /path/to/dir
Run a command with write access to a directory:
landrun --rox /usr/bin --ro /lib --rw /path/to/dir touch /path/to/dir/newfile
Run a command with execution permissions:
landrun --rox /usr/ --ro /lib,/lib64 /usr/bin/bash
Run with debug logging:
landrun --log-level debug --rox /usr/ --ro /lib,/lib64,/path/to/dir ls /path/to/dir
Run with network restrictions:
landrun --rox /usr/ --ro /lib,/lib64 --bind-tcp 8080 --connect-tcp 80 /usr/bin/my-server
This will allow the program to only bind to TCP port 8080 and connect to TCP port 80.
Run a DNS client with appropriate permissions:
landrun --log-level debug --ro /etc,/usr --rox /usr/ --connect-tcp 443 nc kernel.org 443
This allows connections to port 443, requires access to /etc/resolv.conf for resolving DNS.
Run a web server with selective network permissions:
landrun --rox /usr/bin --ro /lib,/lib64,/var/www --rwx /var/log --bind-tcp 80,443 /usr/bin/nginx
